The model works out the smallest radius of each curve (an arc’s radius, an ellipse’s at its flattest point, a helix’s, a spline’s sampled inside its knot spans) and the length each straight piece needs, and warns for each such curve with the place and the numbers: the path bends with radius 3 mm at a curve of Sketch1; the pipe needs at least 5 mm, a curve of Sketch1 is 2.828 mm long; the pipe's mitered corners need at least 4.142 mm there. When the geometry then refuses the pipe, its error ends with these messages. Where the geometry builds such a pipe in pieces (below), each becomes a note instead: the path bends with radius 3 mm at a curve of Sketch1, tighter than the 5 mm the pipe reaches; the pipe was built in pieces there, joined into one solid, a curve of Sketch1 is 2.828 mm long, shorter than the 4.142 mm the pipe's mitered corners need; the pipe was built in pieces there, joined into one solid. Rounded corners have no miters, so only bends are checked for them; a pipe along part of its path (extent partial) is not checked. Test: pipe_tight_bends_tests (mock kernel), the unit tests in features/pipe.rs.
  • Passing through itself (mitcad#1697): the geometry builds a pipe (and a sweep) whose section passes through itself in pieces, each a sound solid, and fuses them with the kernel’s boolean union, so the material they share counts once, as a tube bent that tightly holds it. It cuts the path at both ends of each circular arc the section reaches past the centre of, at the corners of each straight piece too short for its miters, and, where the path comes back within twice the section’s reach of itself (points farther apart along it than four reaches) and the pipe in one piece has faces crossing each other (OCCT’s checker; mitcad#1788: where two points of the path, each at least two reaches from its ends, lie closer than the circle inside the section about the path is wide, the faces cross for certain and neither the pipe in one piece nor the checker, 88 of 89 s along four turns of a helix, is run), between those places so that no piece comes back on itself, never closer to a mitered corner than its miter cuts back. A straight or smooth piece is swept as before; an arc the section reaches past the centre of is the section cut along the arc’s axis, each side turned about the axis by the arc’s angle (the side beyond the axis turns round the other way, behind it); at a corner cut, a mitered joint is the corner’s miter beyond the two pieces’ square ends (the section swept mitered along the two directions a little way on, within the wedge between the planes square to them at the corner), a rounded one the section turned about the corner. A hollow pipe’s pieces are hollow, so the wall of one fills the bore of another where they overlap. The pieces’ faces keep the pipe’s names (side<i>, inner<i>, the caps at the path’s ends; split faces numbered #k). The solid carries the information the swept profile passes through itself along the path; it was built in pieces joined into one solid (Kernel::infos, sweeps::FOLDS_RESOLVED); the pipe then turns the tight-bend warnings above into notes, or shows that information when it has none. Only where the frames along the path are known exactly: a path in one plane (the section keeps its angle to the plane’s normal), a lone helix, and (mitcad#1708) a path in no plane made of lines and circular arcs, along which the section keeps its frame on a line, turns about an arc’s axis along the arc and turns at a corner by the least rotation that takes the arriving direction to the leaving one (as OCCT’s corrected Frenet frame does); for a circular section about the path (a circular pipe, hollow or not) the frame does not matter, so any path. A curved piece between two mitered corners is cut at both corners where some point of the section runs along it less far than the miters cut into it (mitcad#1708, as for a straight piece), and swept on its own with square ends. (mitcad#1709) A tight bend of another curve in a path in one plane (an ellipse, a spline), under a circular section (hollow or not), whose bend is tightest at one point inside the curve and less tight than the section’s reach at its ends, is built from its boundary: the points within the section’s radius of the path, the tube its rim sweeps up to the crease where that tube meets itself (the points as far from a point of the curve before the tightest point as from one after it, at the rim’s reach), each side of the tightest point and of the path’s plane its own face, sewn with the tubes along the rest of the path and closed by the end caps; a hollow pipe’s bore, whose radius must be below the tightest bend’s (else it is not built so), is its own tube inside, the caps rings. No boolean is needed. The surface through the centres of the bend lies inside such a solid: each point is held by the section at the point of the path nearest to it. Only where the path joins smoothly everywhere, nothing else folds and the path does not come back near itself. Along a path in no plane under a circular section (a tight bend of a helix between straight legs) the solid is built the same way from the whole tube less the slot round the inside of the bend where the tube meets itself: the slot’s edge, the crease, runs through the points as far from two points of the path as the rim reaches, traced to its corners, where the other point comes to the station itself (solved exactly at the path’s joints, where the bend jumps), and on from the other point back again; the tube’s faces are split at the slot’s ends, at the joints, at its corners and where the other point crosses a joint. A tight bend of other curves (a curve in no plane whose crease has a corner inside it, a curve that bends tightest at more than one point or at its end), and a corner that turns back more than 179°, are not built in pieces: along such a curve the centre of the bend moves across the section, so no cut of the section keeps each side from folding; along a helix the line through it stays put only where the frames follow the helix’s screw motion, and the surface that line sweeps touches the section’s plane at both ends of the piece, an edge as thin as a knife that the kernel’s union of the sides does not build reliably. The pipe in one piece stays, with the warnings, where it builds; where it does not, the pipe is refused with the pipe passes through itself along its path and could not be built in pieces there, its place the point where it folds, or (a corner turning back, mitcad#1708) with the pipe's path turns right back at a corner, where no mitered corner can be built, its place the corner. A union of the pieces that holds less than its largest piece or more than all of them is not taken. Where a pipe without such folds fails in one piece, it is built in pieces at its corners the same way. Test: geometry.pipe_folds (a circle along a three-quarter arc tighter than its radius, alone, and between two legs, hollow too; a square along a chamfer too short for its miters; a circle along a path that crosses itself; a square, hollow too, along a polyline in no plane with a leg too short for its miters and along an arc between two 45° corners whose miters cut into it; each a valid solid without crossing faces whose volume is the union of its pieces built from OCCT’s primitives within 1e-6, as a pipe and as a sweep; a corner that turns back refused; mitcad#1709: a circle of radius 2, hollow too, along a tight bend of an ellipse and of a spline inside a longer path, each one valid solid without crossing faces whose volume round the bend is the sampled volume of the points within reach of the path within 1e-5, and whose sampled points lie in it exactly when they are within reach; a circle of radius 3, hollow too, along a quarter turn of a helix between two legs, as a pipe and as a sweep with the profile’s seam turned three ways, one valid solid without crossing faces, the same for every seam, whose volume is that of the points within reach of the path, sampled along the rays from it, within 3e-7, and whose sampled points lie in it exactly when they are within reach), pipe_tight_bends_tests and f3_tests (mock kernel: the notes).
  • Turns that overlap (mitcad#1788): along a helix (a fixed helix, a Helix Curve) whose turns lie closer to each other than the circle inside the section is wide (the circle’s diameter, the square’s side, two thirds of the triangle’s height), the pipe’s turns would pass through each other: joined in pieces as above, they took minutes and gave a ribbed sleeve round the axis rather than a pipe along the helix (a hollow one’s bore filled by the next turn’s wall), the shape a Coil refuses for the same reason. The model refuses such a pipe at once, before the geometry: the helix's turns lie 4.984 mm apart, so a section of 8 mm makes the pipe's turns pass through each other; make the section smaller than 4.984 mm or the helix's pitch larger (four turns of radius 10 rising 5 a turn). How close the turns lie is the least distance between points of the helix half a turn to a turn and a half apart along it (5 cos α there, α the helix’s angle); its places are those two points, in the middle of the part swept, their coordinates in the detail only. A lone helix is checked as far as the pipe runs along it (extent), a helix among other curves along the whole path only; a square’s or a triangle’s corners that may pass between the turns, turned away from them, are not refused. Test: the unit tests in features/pipe.rs, pipe_helix_turns_tests (mock kernel: refused without the kernel, a section of 2 mm, less than a turn and an edit to 2 mm built), tools/cli/tests/pipe_helix_turns.json (cli.pipe_helix_turns: the 8 mm refused, 2 mm built with the volume of its length). With MITCAD_TRACE_PIPE_FOLDS set, the geometry prints the time of each stage of a pipe or sweep that may pass through itself on standard error (pipe folds: <stage>: <ms> ms).
  • A pipe’s preview adds sweep_path as a sweep’s (sweep), the section at the start of an open path, with corners: how many sharp corners the path has (left out when none; a closed path’s joint of its last curve to its first counts). The Pipe panel shows Corners only for such a path.

Faces: side<i> for the section’s edges (side0 for a circle; the square’s and the triangle’s sides in turn), inner<i> inside a hollow pipe, start and end as for a sweep.

coil 

{"type": "coil", "plane": "xy", "center": [0, 0], "diameter": 40,
 "helix": {"type": "revolutions_and_pitch", "revolutions": 3, "pitch": 10},
 "angle": 0, "clockwise": false, "section": "circular",
 "section_position": "on_center", "section_size": 4, "operation": "new_body"}
  • plane: an origin plane, a construction plane or a planar face; center in its coordinates. The axis is the plane’s normal; the coil starts on the plane on the side the plane’s x axis points to and turns counter-clockwise about the normal (a right-handed helix) unless clockwise (isClockwise false in .f3d designs).
  • helix: revolutions_and_height, revolutions_and_pitch, height_and_pitch, or spiral (revolutions, pitch: flat, growing pitch in radius per turn). Height and pitch are measured at the section’s centre.
  • angle: a cone, positive widening as it rises (not for a spiral).
  • section: circular, square, triangular_external (a corner pointing out) or triangular_internal; section_size the diameter of the circle, the side of the square or the height of the triangle (its radial extent). section_position: inside, on_center (default) or outside the diameter: the section’s radial extent touches the diameter from inside, is centred on it, or touches it from outside. The section lies in the plane through the axis and moves by a screw motion (the helix’s; the volumes of the .f3d variant models, mitcad#25), so the volume is the section’s area times the path of its centroid.

Coils whose turns would overlap, or whose section reaches the axis, fail. Faces: side<i>, start, end.

helix 

{"type": "helix", "profiles": [{"sketch": "F1", "region": "r{c1}"}],
 "axis": "z", "pitch": 5, "revolutions": 4, "left_handed": false, "flip": false,
 "operation": "new_body"}

The profiles turn about the axis (a line reference, as a revolve’s) while they move along its direction (against it with flip): revolutions turns (need not be whole) rising pitch each, right-handed about the direction of travel unless left_handed. Every section of the result in a plane through the axis is the profile turned there (a screw motion; a coil’s sections are instead fixed shapes at right angles to its helix). A height is given as a ratio: "<height> / <pitch>" for revolutions or "<height> / <revolutions>" for pitch (as the FreeCAD import and the application write it). operation and participants as for extrude. A profile longer along the axis than the pitch overlaps its next turn: the tool is the union of the turns (mitcad#60). With surface it makes surface bodies of the profiles’ walls and of open or closed sketch curves instead, a helicoid from a line (mitcad#1777, Surface Helix).

growth (a length, optional; mitcad#59) widens the helix: the profiles move that far out from the axis per turn (negative: in); a cone’s angle is the growth pitch * tan(angle). construction (mitcad#83) says how a growth is built:

  • "mitcad" (the default for commands): the screw motion, the profiles also moved out along the direction from the axis towards their centre (across their plane’s normal when the centre is on the axis) in proportion to the turn. Every section in a plane through the axis is the profile turned there and moved out, the same for every profile position, growth sign and direction, so the volume of a profile in a plane through the axis is its area times 2 pi revolutions times its centre’s mean distance from the axis. A narrowing that would take the profiles to the axis fails.
  • "freecad" (what the FreeCAD import writes): as FreeCAD builds its conical and growing helices, so that they import exactly. The profiles follow the Frenet frame of a spiral of the same pitch and growth a hundred times as far from the axis, which FreeCAD raises along the axis by ten thousand times the profiles’ height above the axis’ origin when the growth is not positive (otherwise by that much of the origin’s height); the profiles stay nearly in planes through the axis, and a narrowing helix whose profiles sit at the axis’ origin runs the other way, as in FreeCAD.

A growing helix always stores its construction. A command without one gives MitCad’s, or keeps the construction of the helix it edits; in files written before the field (by the FreeCAD import, mitcad#59) a growing helix without one is FreeCAD’s, so it keeps its shape. Without a growth both are the screw motion and the field is left out unless given.

start and end (optional; mitcad#235), each {"transition_angle": a, "flat_angle": b}, make flat ends as a coil’s: over the transition the pitch changes linearly between zero at the outer end and pitch, and over the flat part the profiles turn without rising. They come in addition to the revolutions, which are the turns at the full pitch: the start’s flat part comes first, then its transition, the turns, the end’s transition and its flat part. With ends a growth follows the rise (the profiles move out by growth for every pitch they rise, so a cone’s growth stays pitch * tan(angle) and the flat parts keep their distance from the axis), and the helix is built by MitCad’s construction (freecad with ends is an error).

piece_shift (turns, optional, at least 0 and less than a third; mitcad#235) shifts the seams of the pieces the helix is swept in (a third of a turn each): the shape is the same, but a boolean that failed or left part of the helix uncut where those seams meet the seams of the bodies' faces about the axis can work with them moved. The .ipt import tries a coil as decoded once more with "piece_shift": 1/6 when it does not give the file’s state. Without it, a join, cut or intersection that fails, or whose result the geometry kernel’s checker finds invalid, is tried once more with the seams shifted by a sixth of a turn, and the feature then has a warning that says so; a helix whose boolean works is built once, as before.

A helix of one profile (of corners, no closed curve) touching one of the bodies’ cylinders about the axis (a thread), whose turns do not overlap and whose seams are not shifted, is built as a B-rep whose faces each run all the turns, as the bodies stored in files keep threads: each edge of the profile sweeps one face (a B-spline surface whose rows of poles are the helices of the edge’s poles, an exact cylinder for a straight side along the axis), the profile at both ends closing it (mitcad#235: the sweep in pieces left a thread running out past the end face of a body in many small faces, some of them slivers, that a later union with that body’s surroundings could not take). The booleans on such faces work on the parts of them they meet (OCCT port patches 0591 to 0593: the cut of a 25-turn thread and the union with its part take a few seconds each).

A side of such a profile on a cylinder as long as the pitch (at most one, more than one turn) makes the turns meet in one edge there, as the bodies stored in files have them: no strip of the cylinder is left between the turns, and a rolling ball rounds that crest. The solid holds a core beyond that side (out to a tenth of the pitch, at most a fifth of the room to the bodies' next cylinder beyond it; twice that at the side’s middle), so that its turns join along faces instead of touching along an edge; along the bodies’ faces on that cylinder the core lies where the boolean changes nothing. Beyond those faces the core is cut away over the whole helix, and the turns meet in an edge there too (a thread running out past a blind bore’s bottom into the material). For the booleans the faces are split every third of a turn into pieces that share their surface, and the face merge after the boolean makes each face whole again. When the core cannot be cut away, the helix fails.

Other helices with a side on a cylinder (more profiles, closed curves, overlapping turns, shifted seams, more than one side as long as the pitch) are swept in pieces, a side as long as the pitch moved 0.1 µm off its cylinder along the bodies' faces there (the shifted seams’ retry), and their straight sides along the axis made exact cylinders.

Faces: side(<segment>), start(<region>) at the profile and end(<region>) (geometry/src/path_sweep.cpp).
