sketch.* see Sketch commands
  • New features go in at the timeline marker, which moves after them (with after or index, at that place before the marker).
  • add_parameter and set_parameter reject commands containing both value and expression. set_parameter also accepts only unit, comment, favorite or group; a unit-only edit keeps the existing expression.
  • Parameters copied from another document retain that document’s default units for implicit units inside expressions. The parameters query and saved parameter record expose them as expression_units (length, angle). Editing the expression or applying a configuration keeps these defaults; the parameter’s own unit still takes precedence for its dimensions. Changing the destination document’s units does not reinterpret these copied expressions. Their parameter references remain editable.
  • delete_feature refuses while other features refer to the feature (Extrude1 is used by Fillet1; …); with "dependents": true they go too (the dependents query lists them). A cut whose cut_scope only excludes the feature’s component or body does not refer to it (mitcad#1236): the delete goes ahead, the cut stays, and an exclusion of a body the feature made is dropped with an info notice. A joint that goes as a dependent (one on a face, an edge, a frame or a joint origin of what goes) leaves what it placed where it is (mitcad#1820), as build_remove and delete_occurrence do (mitcad#1811): its sides keep their pose, a move of them on the timeline taken into account (Document::held_placements); only the joints to what goes are removed, and undo brings back the features, the joints and the occurrences’ own placements. A free part of a flexible occurrence such a joint placed stays as that occurrence’s own placement of it (mitcad#2017, Flexible subassemblies). A joint deleted by itself (its own uid) still lets what it placed go back where it was placed.
  • reorder_feature refuses a position where a feature would come before something it refers to (the can_reorder query asks first).
  • Features after the marker are rolled back (not evaluated); suppressed features are skipped.
  • set_marker with "temporary": true evaluates a command editor’s rollback without adding an undo step, dropping redo or changing the revision. The editor must restore the original marker with the same flag before committing an edit or saving. Cancellation leaves the marker, history, revision and displayed results unchanged. Ordinary marker moves keep their existing undo behavior.
  • After a command, new bodies get display names (Body1, Body2, … the next free number), which are saved.
  • A timeline group stays a run: deleted features leave it, a feature added or moved between its members joins it, a member moved away leaves it (the only member takes the group along), an empty group goes. Saved as "groups": [{"name", "features"}]; a favourite parameter as "favorite": true.

Recompute All (mitcad#1982)

{"cmd": "recompute", "all": true} evaluates every feature again from the start of the timeline, with none of the results the memory cache or the result store holds (Document::try_recompute_all); its result’s recomputed counts every feature it evaluated. The results of the run become the cache; a cancelled run leaves the document, its results and its cache as they were. What the run measures anew (a driven dimension’s value, a Flex item’s nodes) is one undo step, Recompute All, when it differs from the state, and changed is true; otherwise there is no step and changed is false. A failed feature is reported as in every command (error, error_notice, failed_features). The application’s Manage › Design › Recompute All runs it. Test: core.model.api (recompute_all_tests.rs).

Feature names are not unique (mitcad#1107)

Features may share a name: a sketch and the extrude made from it can both be named Holder (add_feature, sketch.create and rename_feature take a name in use; an empty name is refused). Default names (Extrude3) still skip the names in use. The model’s own references, the timeline and the application go by uid; other names stay unique as before (bodies, components, parameters, annotations, drawings).

A field that takes a feature by uid or name (a script’s feature and sketch expectations, export_sketch’s sketch, the joint of drive_joint (also previewed), add_motion_link, add_motion_study, edit_motion_study, set_study_key and remove_study_key, the profiles query’s sketch) reads it so:

  • the uid of an existing feature is that feature;
  • a name one feature has is that feature (a field of one kind then says when it is not of that kind: Holder is not a joint);
  • a name several features have is refused with their uids and kinds, Holder names several features: F1 (sketch), F2 (extrude); give the uid, unless the field takes only one kind and exactly one of them is of that kind: a sketch field and one sketch named Holder find that sketch.

An import that names a feature after the item of the file keeps that name, also one another feature has (before, it took the default name). A design file saves and opens features of one name; only a version 1 file, whose features refer to each other by name, still needs each name once.

Undo, revisions and the saved state

Command Fields Result
undo, redo label of the step, or null
begin_command token: an opaque string identifying a checkpoint of the current definition, revision, saved state and both history stacks
restore_command token restores that checkpoint after its scene recomputes successfully; keeps the token for retries
discard_command token releases the checkpoint without changing the current definition or history
merge_undo depth: the undo depth before the action, label merges the undo steps after depth into one step named label (clears redo), and the sketch work steps they recorded into one per sketch (The work steps of a sketch); undo_depth. Refuses a depth past the last step
mark_saved revision; the definition state is the design file’s (saved or opened). No undo step, nothing recomputed
  • Undo and redo restore the whole definition (parameters, timeline, marker, body names). Cached results make them fast.
  • An asynchronous frontend begins one command checkpoint before temporary marker moves or applied sketch previews. Cancel restores and then discards it; accept discards it. Restore recovers the exact preexisting redo stack, even when a command completed before cancellation reached the worker. A failed or cancelled restore changes nothing and retains the token for retry. Only one checkpoint may be active per document; stale tokens are rejected. Tokens and newly allocated revision numbers are never reused. Checkpoints are session state, absent from saved designs; finish the command before marking a saved file or replacing the document.
  • One user action is often several commands (a rectangle snapped to the origin is sketch.add_point, sketch.rectangle and a coincident constraint; a drag a sketch.drag per mouse move). The caller reads undo_depth (document query) before the action, runs its commands and merges them, or undoes back to that depth to take the action back.
  • Every accepted command gives the state a new revision, also one that recomputes nothing (a rename, a named view); a rejected command, a command that changes nothing, a recompute and a preview keep it. Undo and redo take back the revision of the state they restore, so undoing to the saved state is unmodified again; merge_undo keeps the current revision. A new command after undo gets a new revision even when it makes the same definition. update_links gives a new revision when it takes new bodies (no undo step).
  • A new document is not modified. A design file read (Document::from_json, the bridge’s load_document) is modified until mark_saved, since it need not be the file it will be saved to (an imported design, recovered work). Saving (to_json) does not mark it saved by itself.
  • Document::to_json_with_marker(marker) (bridge to_json_with_marker) writes the design file with another marker without changing the document (autosave while an edit has rolled the timeline back).

Visibility and display

Command Fields Result
set_feature_visible uid (a sketch or a construction plane, axis or point), visible undo step Show Sketch1 / Hide Plane1 unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
set_body_visible uid, visible, or expression (a condition; Bindings)
set_body_material uid, material (a built-in id below or one of the design’s materials, or null: its component’s default, steel when none is set), appearance (replace: the material’s appearance becomes the body’s; keep: the body keeps its own; left out: replace unless the body’s appearance was set by hand, see Materials), or expression (a text naming the material; Bindings) undo step Set Material of Body1 (material and appearance together); nothing recomputed
set_body_appearance uid, appearance (an id of the library or the document, see Appearances, or null for the default look), or expression (a text naming the appearance; Bindings)
set_origin_visible visible, opening (default false: an undo step; true: as a new design opens, mitcad#1683, with no undo step and no new revision, so the document stays as modified as it was; the application shows the origin of every new design it opens so) the root’s Origin folder shown; undo step Show Origin / Hide Origin unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
set_isolation items: {"body": "F3.b0", "occurrence": "O1"} (a body, in the occurrence that places it, none for the root’s) or {"occurrence": "O1/O4"} (an occurrence by its path); none: unisolate undo step Isolate 2 item(s) / Unisolate; an occurrence that is not there is refused
  • Body commands are undo steps (Hide Body1, Show Body1, Set Material of Body1, …) unless nothing changes; the body must exist at the marker. The bodies query and the design file list "visible": false, "material" and "appearance" when set, and "appearance_set_by_hand": true for an appearance that is not its material’s. Built-in materials: steel (7.85 g/cm³, the default), stainless_steel, cast_iron, aluminum, copper, brass, titanium, abs, pla, nylon, polycarbonate, glass, water, resin_standard (core/model-base/src/analysis.rs, core/model/src/material.rs), and the woods and panels wood_pine, wood_oak, wood_birch, plywood_birch, mdf_raw (mitcad#1706, their values from the bundled dataset); a design’s own materials and components' default materials are in Materials.
  • Sketches and construction features: by default a sketch is hidden while a feature uses it (a profile, curves or points; suppressed features and those after the marker count too) and shown while none does; construction geometry is shown. A sketch or a 3D sketch that projects or intersects another sketch’s curves or points (sketch.project, also with section, and a 3D sketch’s linked projections) does not use that sketch: the source stays shown while more of its curves are picked (mitcad#2045). A light bulb set with set_feature_visible wins; it is kept and saved with the feature ("visible": true or false) only where it differs from the default, so showing a hidden sketch that no feature uses forgets it.
  • The command that gives a sketch its first consumer or takes its last one away forgets the sketch’s light bulb in its own undo step: the new extrusion’s sketch hides, and shows again when that extrusion is deleted, even if it was hidden by hand meanwhile. A second consumer keeps a light bulb set by hand. Deleting a feature forgets its visibility; paste_new and copied designs start with the defaults. Code: document/browser.rs.
  • The display state (Origin folder, isolation) is per user: the design file keeps it as "display": {"origin": true, "isolated": [...]} (left out when nothing is set), and a project keeps it outside the design file (Design files). Isolation lists only the items there at the marker; none left isolates nothing.
  • Occurrences have set_occurrence_visible (Components and occurrences).

Transparent bodies and occurrences (mitcad#1093)

Command Fields Result
set_body_transparent uid, transparent undo step Make Body1 Transparent / Make Body1 Opaque unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed; the body must exist at the marker
set_occurrence_transparent occurrence (uid, name or path, as for set_occurrence_visible), transparent undo step Make Bracket:1 Transparent / Make Bracket:1 Opaque unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
  • Transparency is kept like visibility: per body (in every occurrence that places it) and per occurrence, in the definition state, so it is saved with the design and undo restores it. It is independent of the light bulb: a hidden transparent body or occurrence is transparent again when it is shown. It changes no appearance or material.
  • An occurrence’s transparency applies to its contents, the bodies of its component and of the occurrences inside it.
  • The bodies query lists "transparent": true for a body set so, the components query’s occurrences "transparent": true for an occurrence set so, and the instances query "transparent": true for a placed body that is transparent itself or lies in a transparent occurrence (left out otherwise). The design file keeps "transparent": true on the body and on the occurrence (left out when false). A copy of an occurrence (Paste) starts opaque, as it starts shown; Paste New copies the transparency of the occurrences inside it. The design comparison lists a change as transparent or opaque.
  • The application draws a transparent body as a faint shaded surface with its edges in its own appearance’s colour, and a click goes through it to what lies behind (app/COMMANDS.md, “Transparent bodies and components”).

Display size of construction planes and axes (mitcad#1748)

Command Fields Result
set_datum_display_size uid (a construction plane or axis), size (mm, greater than 0 and at most 1 000 000; null or left out: drawn fitted to what it is made from, or at the default size) undo step Resize Plane1 / Resize Axis1 unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed

  • How large the application draws a construction plane (its square’s side) or axis (its line’s length): its resize handles in the 3D view send this command (app/COMMANDS.md, “Origin planes and the size of construction geometry”). Display only: the datum’s plane or line, what sketches and features use, does not change. Other features, construction points among them, are refused (Point1 has no display size: …).

  • The datums and datum queries list "display_size" for a datum that has one (left out otherwise); the design file keeps it on the feature ("display_size": 40, left out when not set), a design comparison lists it as a display_size change. Deleting the feature forgets it; a file with a size on another feature reads without it, a size that is not a positive number is refused. Code: document/browser.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/datum_display_size_tests.rs.

  • Where it is drawn (mitcad#1827, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#321): without a display_size a construction plane or axis is drawn at the size and shape of what it is made from, worked out with the feature (features/construction/drawn.rs), so it follows the model. The datums and datum queries (and a construction feature’s preview, under datum) give it as drawn:

    Field Meaning
    source fitted (what it is made from), display_size (its resize handles’ size) or default (nothing to measure)
    rect a plane’s: center, x_axis, y_axis (unit, in the plane), width, height (mm, the margin included)
    segment, length an axis’s: start, end (along its direction), and the distance between them
    size with display_size and default: the square’s side or the line’s length
    • A plane made on or from a face (offset, offset_through_point, angle, tangent, tangent_at_point, midplane): a rectangle over the faces’ outlines seen along its normal (Kernel::face_boundary, else Kernel::face_outline), along their longest straight edge, else along the plane’s x_axis; made from another construction plane, over that plane’s extent (without its margin).
    • A plane through edges or points (and one on a face without an outline, and perpendicular_at_point, edge-on to its face): a square over where it cuts the boxes of the bodies its references are on, else over the referenced geometry.
    • An axis: along its edge’s, faces’, planes’ or points’ extent, else where it passes through their bodies’ boxes.
    • The margin all round: 5 % of the larger side, at least 3 mm. Nothing to measure (a fixed or flange_wall plane, an offset of an origin plane, a fixed axis): default, 100 mm about the datum’s origin.
    • A display_size draws a square of that side (a line of that length) about the middle of the fitted extent (about the origin without one); null brings the fitted extent back. Origin datums, points, joint origins and coordinate systems have no drawn.
    • Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/datum_drawn_extent_tests.rs (a plane off a face and one off that plane, an axis along an edge, the default, a display size over it, the file, an edit followed), the unit tests in features/construction/drawn.rs; app.ui-*construction-size.

Acknowledged warnings (mitcad#1935)

Command Fields Result
acknowledge_warnings uids (features that built with warnings), acknowledged (default true; false shows them again) undo step Acknowledge Fillet1 / Acknowledge 3 Warnings (Unacknowledge … when shown again) unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
  • A feature’s warning the user has seen (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#380): the design keeps the warning’s text as it was acknowledged (its warnings joined with ; ). While the feature builds with that very text, the timeline query gives it "acknowledged": true (left out otherwise); its status, level and notices stay those of a warning, so agents still read it. The application does not paint it yellow nor count it in the warnings badge (app/COMMANDS.md, “Acknowledged warnings”).
  • It lapses by itself: when the feature fails, or builds with another warning text or none, it is no longer acknowledged, and the edit that recomputed forgets it in its own undo step, so the same warning coming back later shows again. Suppressed and rolled back features keep theirs.
  • Refused: a feature that failed (Fillet1 failed: an error cannot be acknowledged), one without a warning (Fillet1 has no warning to acknowledge), an unknown uid. One already acknowledged, or shown again without an acknowledgement, is left as it is.
  • The design file keeps it on the feature ("acknowledged_warning": "<text>", left out when none); deleting the feature forgets it. Code: document/acknowledged_warnings.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/acknowledged_warnings_tests.rs.

Named views

Command Fields Result
add_named_view name (the next free NamedView<n> when left out), eye, target (points, mm), up, perspective (default false), height (mm of the model the view shows at the target), replace (default false: a name in use is refused) name; undo step Add Named View Detail (Change Named View Detail when replaced) unless nothing changes
rename_named_view name, new_name
delete_named_view name

Named views change no geometry and recompute nothing; they are saved in the design file ("views", left out when there are none). The view named Home is the document’s home view.

Analyses

Section analyses (mitcad#41), print analyses (mitcad#620) and draft analyses (mitcad#2166) kept in the document (core/model/src/document/analyses.rs): the browser’s Analysis folder.

Command Fields Result
add_analysis def, name (the next free Section<n>, Print<n> for a print analysis or Draft<n> for a draft analysis, when left out) name; undo step Add Section1. It is shown and the others are hidden
edit_analysis name, def, visible (optional: true shows it and hides the others, false hides it; as it was when left out) undo step Edit Section1 unless nothing changes
set_analysis_visible name, visible undo step Show Section1 / Hide Section1 unless nothing changes; showing hides the others
rename_analysis name, new_name undo step Rename Section1
delete_analysis name undo step Delete Section1

A def is {"type": "section", "plane": <plane reference>, "offset": mm, "flip": bool} (offset default 0, flip default false): the bodies cut at plane moved by offset along its normal, the side the normal points to cut away; flip reverses the normal. The plane is a plane reference (origin plane, construction plane, planar face, fixed plane); add_analysis and edit_analysis refuse one that is no plane at the marker, and other fields than these.

An optional occurrence is the selected plane’s UID path from the design root, for example "O1/O3" (empty for the root). Component-owned faces and construction planes are transformed through that path into design coordinates before applying the offset. Flip reverses only the normal, after offsetting, and leaves the physical plane in place. Without a path, older analyses infer a component’s unique placement; repeated components require an explicit path. A path that does not own the referenced face or datum is refused. Fixed planes and origin planes without a path remain in design coordinates.

{"query":"section_plane","plane":<reference>,"occurrence":"O1/O3", "offset":-5,"flip":false} resolves the same definition without adding an analysis. It returns design-space origin, normal, and the resolved occurrence; the optional fields have the same defaults as an analysis.

A section can be turned by an angle about an axis (mitcad#823): angle (radians, default 0, not written when 0), axis (a line reference: a straight edge, a sketch line, a construction axis or an origin axis) and axis_occurrence (the axis’ UID path from the design root, as occurrence is the plane’s; inferred and checked the same way). The picked plane is first turned rigidly by angle about the axis, right-handed about the axis’ direction, in design coordinates after both occurrence paths; then it is moved by offset along the turned normal; flip then reverses only the normal. An axis with angle 0 leaves the plane as it is. add_analysis and edit_analysis refuse a non-zero angle without an axis, and an axis along the plane’s normal; an analysis whose axis cannot be found at the marker gets the analyses query’s error and cuts nothing, as a plane that cannot be found. The section_plane query takes the same three fields and then also returns axis ({"origin", "direction"} in design coordinates) and the resolved axis_occurrence. Analyses without an angle are written as before; a MitCad older than mitcad#823 refuses a design with these fields. Drawing section views cut by a Section Analysis follow its angle.

The analyses query lists them in the order added: name, type, visible, the def’s fields, and section: {origin, normal} (the plane in design coordinates at the marker, offset and flip applied; the origin is the plane’s origin, see References to geometry), or error when the plane cannot be found there (a face of a body that is gone or rolled back). A face reference follows the model by its topological name, as features’ do.

A def of "type": "print" is a print analysis: its bodies, bed face and settings, and in the analyses query down (the print direction at the marker) or error (a body or the bed face is gone).

A def of "type": "draft" is a draft analysis (mitcad#2166, default names Draft1, Draft2, …): its bodies, pull direction, flip and angle, and in the analyses query pull_direction (the unit pull at the marker) or error (a body or the pull reference is gone).

  • At most one analysis is shown at a time: one section cuts the bodies. Showing one hides the others, also in a file read with several shown (the first shown stays).
  • Analyses change no geometry and recompute nothing. They are saved in the design file ("analyses": [{"name", "visible" (only when false), "type", "plane", "occurrence" (when supplied), "offset", "flip"}], left out when there are none; files without it have none), and the comparison of versions lists them by name.

A section through a pick (mitcad#1769)

plane also takes one face or edge that places a plane, stored as the reference (with its occurrence) so that the section follows the model:

  • a cylindrical face (also a conical or toroidal one: a hole, a boss, a countersink, a fillet): the plane contains the face’s axis;
  • a circular edge or arc: the plane contains the circle’s axis (through its center, along its normal);
  • a straight edge: the plane passes through the edge’s midpoint, normal to the edge (its normal runs from the edge’s start to its end).

For the first two the axis points along its largest component (as an axis reference) and the plane’s turn about it starts at the first of the origin planes XY, XZ and YZ (of the reference’s component) whose normal is at least 45 degrees from the axis: that normal, made square to the axis, is the plane’s. For an axis along a model axis this is the first origin plane that contains it (XZ for a hole along Z, XY for one along X or Y); it never depends on the view. angle then turns the plane about that axis without an axis field (an axis, when given, is used instead); offset and flip work as for any plane. A straight edge’s plane needs an axis for an angle, as a plane does. The section_plane query returns the picked axis as axis (without axis_occurrence), so that a panel can draw the Angle’s ring about it. A face that is neither planar nor round about an axis, or an edge that is neither straight nor circular, is refused; an analysis whose face or edge is gone at the marker gets the analyses query’s error, as a plane that cannot be found. A MitCad older than mitcad#1769 reads such an analysis but cannot find its plane, and refuses a design with one turned without an axis.

Appearances

How bodies look (mitcad#46, core/model-base/src/appearance.rs, core/model/src/document/appearances.rs): a physically based parameter set, a subset of OpenPBR’s and the Principled BSDF’s. MitCad’s library is built in and read-only; a document keeps appearances of its own, saved in the design file. A body names its appearance by id (set_body_appearance), and single faces can have their own (Appearances of faces, mitcad#53).

Parameter Range Default
base_color sRGB [r, g, b], 0–1 [0.8, 0.8, 0.8] a dielectric’s diffuse colour, a metal’s reflection, the tint of transmitted light
metalness 0–1 0 1 for metals
roughness 0–1 0.5 0 a mirror finish
specular 0–1 1 the weight of a dielectric’s specular reflection
transmission 0–1 0 light going through (glass, clear plastic)
ior 1–5 1.5 index of refraction
coat, coat_roughness 0–1 0, 0.03 a clear coat over the base (lacquer, car paint)
emission, emission_color 0–1000, sRGB 0, [1, 1, 1] emitted light: 1 is the colour’s own radiance
opacity 0–1 1 a cut-out (glass transmits instead)
texture {"path", "size": [w, h] mm (default 100 x 100), "rotation" rad, "projection": "box" (default), "planar", "uv" or "grain", "data", "normal", "roughness", "metalness", "occlusion", "source"} none an image for the base colour (PNG or JPEG), with the other maps of its set and where it came from (Texture map sets), projected in the body’s coordinates: planar along Z, box from the axis each point of the surface faces most; one repeat of the image is size, turned by rotation about the projection’s axis. uv (mitcad#1862) lays it by the body’s own texture coordinates (a mesh body imported with them, as a glTF file’s), once over 0 to 1 of each, without size and rotation; a body without them is projected as by box. Versions before it refuse uv. grain (mitcad#2186) lays it along each face’s grain: each face from a plane of its own, the image’s width along the face’s longest side (Built-in wood and panel textures); versions before it refuse grain. path is relative to the design file’s folder or absolute; data (base64 of the image file, at most 32 MB) embeds the image in the design file (Textures). The rendered view draws it with all its maps, the shaded view its base colour image (mitcad#2186; by uv the base colour)
class metal, plastic (General Plastic), fdm_plastic, resin, other none: other what it is a look of (mitcad#1102): a material’s Add… and the Appearance tool offer the appearances of the material’s class first. Set by the user (null or other takes it away), or on a filament’s colour (fdm_plastic: a material’s own colour, a printer profile’s or a 3MF import’s filament); the library’s come from their ids and are never written
Command Fields Result
create_appearance id (letters, digits, _, -; the next free custom<n> when left out), name (Appearance<n> when left out), based_on (a library or document appearance whose parameters it starts from; the defaults above without it), any parameters id; undo step Create Appearance Red
edit_appearance id, name and any parameters ("texture": null removes the texture) undo step Edit Appearance Red unless nothing changes; the library’s are refused (copy one with based_on)
delete_appearance id bodies: those that used it, which get the default look, and faces ({"body", "face"}) that used it, which get their body’s, in the same undo step Delete Appearance Red
  • Ids are unique among the library’s and the document’s appearances, and names too; parameters out of range and unknown fields are refused.
  • The appearances query lists the library’s appearances in the application’s order, then the document’s: id, name, the parameters, library (true for the built-in ones), display_color (sRGB: the colour of the shaded view and exports; the base colour), class (its own, a library appearance’s by its id, else other; mitcad#1102), bodies (the uids of bodies that use it, also those not at the marker) and faces ({"body", "face"} of faces that use it).
  • Library: steel_satin, aluminum_anodized, brass_polished, copper, cast_iron, paint_red, paint_blue, paint_green, paint_yellow, paint_black, paint_white, plastic_black, plastic_orange, rubber, glass, wood_oak (their colours as before mitcad#46), chrome, gold_polished, steel_polished, plastic_red, plastic_white, plastic_blue, plastic_clear, glass_clear, glass_frosted, wood_walnut, wood_maple, emissive_white, resin_grey, resin_white, resin_clear (mitcad#1102), and the basic colours of generic filaments (mitcad#1133, named Filament - <Colour>, the look of a printed thermoplastic: dielectric, roughness 0.55, specular 0.5, no coat): filament_white, filament_black, filament_grey, filament_silver, filament_red, filament_orange, filament_yellow, filament_green, filament_blue, filament_light_blue, filament_purple, filament_pink, filament_brown, filament_beige (natural) and filament_translucent (natural, transmission 0.7); their ids are stable; and the looks of the material dataset’s woods and panels (mitcad#1552; with built-in texture sets since mitcad#2186, Built-in wood and panel textures: dielectric, specular 0.5, no coat): wood_birch, wood_cedar, wood_cherry, wood_douglas_fir, wood_eucalyptus, wood_pine, wood_teak, panel_chipboard (Chipboard), panel_mdf (MDF), panel_osb (OSB), plywood_birch, plywood_eucalyptus, plywood_pine, plywood_spruce; their ids are stable too. Their classes (mitcad#1102): the steels, aluminum_anodized, brass_polished, copper, cast_iron, chrome and gold_polished metal; the plastic_* ones plastic (General Plastic); the filament_* ones fdm_plastic (FDM Plastic); the resin_* ones resin; the wood_*, plywood_* and panel_* ones wood (mitcad#1552, wood_oak, wood_walnut and wood_maple too, other before); the paints, rubber, the glasses and emissive_white other. An appearance of the design or a library without a class is other, as are those of the .f3d, .FCStd and .ipt imports.
  • A body without an appearance, or with an id in neither list (an imported one), has the default look. A material carries an appearance (mitcad#640): setting a body’s material sets the body’s appearance to the material’s, unless the body’s appearance was set by hand (one that is not its current material’s) or set_body_material says keep; see Materials.
  • The commands change no geometry and recompute nothing. The design file keeps the document’s appearances as "appearances": [{"id", "name", parameters...}] (left out when there are none; parameters left out of a file are the defaults; files without it have none), and the comparison of versions lists them by id.
  • A library id taken since (mitcad#1133): a design file whose own appearance has another library id is refused (no design can save one), but one with an id the library took only later (one of the filament_* colours, or of the woods’ and panels’ looks of mitcad#1552) opens; that appearance keeps its values under a free id, the first of <id>_2, <id>_3, … (and a free name, <name> (2), when the library’s has its name), and every reference follows: the bodies’ and faces’ appearances, the materials’ default and list, the components’ appearances and the bindings’ quoted texts ('filament_red'). The document’s load warnings say so once per appearance (appearance filament_red of this design is now filament_red_2: …); a parameter’s text that spells the old id names the library’s from then on.
  • A component’s unknown appearance (mitcad#1150): a component’s appearance in component_materials that neither the design nor the library has is dropped when the file opens, with a load warning (component_materials[0]: there is no appearance …; the component shows its material's); the component keeps its material.
  • Older versions (before mitcad#1102) open a design or a library file unless it holds an appearance with a class (an unknown field, as embedded images); one is written only when set.

Appearances of faces

Faces of a body can have appearances of their own, which override the body’s (mitcad#53, core/model/src/document/bodies.rs): a label area, a painted face, a rubber pad.

Command Fields Result
set_face_appearance uid (body), faces (topological names of faces of the body at the marker, F2:side(c1[c4,c2])), appearance (an id, or null: the faces show the body’s again), or expression (Bindings) undo step Set Appearance of Face of Body1 / Set Appearance of 2 Faces of Body1 / Clear Appearance of Face of Body1 unless nothing changes; faces that are not there and names that are no face names are refused
clear_face_appearances uid undo step Clear Face Appearances of Body1 unless the body has none
  • A face appearance names its face as assigned (the canonical text of the name) and follows it as features’ face references do: a later feature that changes the face keeps the name, all pieces of a split face (#k) keep it. When a change renames the face (a sketch edit after which a side face’s segment ends on another curve: F2:side(c1[c4,c2]) becomes F2:side(c1[c4,c5])), the name finds the face of the same feature and role whose key has the most curves in common with it (for a side face: the same curve), as a profile’s region key does; the name kept is still the one assigned. A face that is gone finds nothing and its appearance is kept for when it comes back (undo).
  • The bodies query lists them per body as face_appearances: [{"face" (as assigned), "appearance", "faces" (a name of each face it finds at the marker; empty when the face is gone)}], left out when there are none.
  • They recompute nothing. The design file keeps them with the body’s other attributes: "face_appearances": {"F2:side(c1[c4,c2])": "paint_red"} (left out when there are none; files without them have none); copied designs rename the feature ids in the names. The comparison of versions lists them with the body.

Textures

An appearance’s texture is an image file or an image embedded in the design file (mitcad#53).

  • "data" in a create_appearance or edit_appearance texture embeds the image: base64 of a PNG or JPEG file (checked by its first bytes; at most 32 MB). path then names the file it came from. The appearances query lists an embedded texture with "embedded": true and "image_sha256" (the digest of the image file) instead of its data; that form sent back keeps the embedded image ("embedded": true without data keeps the image the appearance has, or that of based_on for a new one; refused when there is none), so the application changes a texture’s size or rotation without sending the image again. A texture without data and embedded reads its file again.
  • The appearance_image query (id) gives an embedded image: data (base64), format (png, jpeg) and sha256.
  • The design file keeps the image in the texture’s data; the comparison of versions shows sha256 <digest> for it. A file with shared images or embedded maps keeps each image once instead (Texture map sets).

Texture map sets

A texture can be a full set of physically based maps (mitcad#313, core/model-base/src/appearance.rs), so that a design looks the same on another computer without the image files: besides the base colour image (the texture’s own path and data), each of

Map Image
normal a tangent-space normal map, OpenGL convention (green up)
roughness roughness, grey 0 (mirror) to 1
metalness metalness, grey 0 (dielectric) to 1 (metal)
occlusion ambient occlusion, grey 0 (occluded) to 1

is an optional object of the texture, {"path", "data"}, a PNG or JPEG file as the base colour’s: path relative to the design file’s folder or absolute, data (base64, at most 32 MB per image, each map one image) embeds it. The maps share the base colour’s size, rotation and projection; a set needs its base colour image. A map left out of an edit_appearance texture is removed (the texture is replaced as a whole). A grey map (roughness, metalness, occlusion) may take its values from one colour channel of its image, "channel": "red", "green" or "blue" (mitcad#1862), where an image packs several maps, as a glTF file’s image of roughness (green) and metalness (blue), whose occlusion is red; without it the image’s grey value counts. Versions before it refuse channel. The roughness and metalness maps may scale their values by a "factor" from 0 to 1 (mitcad#1874: glTF’s roughnessFactor and metallicFactor, which multiply its image’s channels); without it the map’s values count as they are. Another map with a factor, or a factor outside 0 to 1, is refused (texture: normal: only the roughness and metalness maps take a factor, texture: roughness: the factor must be from 0 to 1, got 1.5). Versions before it refuse factor.

{"cmd": "create_appearance", "name": "Oak veneer", "texture": {
 "path": "oak_diff_2k.jpg", "data": "/9j/4AAQ…", "size": [300, 300],
 "normal": {"path": "oak_nor_gl_2k.png", "data": "iVBORw0K…"},
 "roughness": {"path": "oak_rough_2k.png", "data": "iVBORw0K…"},
 "source": {"id": "polyhaven", "asset": "oak_veneer_01", "resolution": "2k",
 "license": "CC0-1.0", "url": "https://polyhaven.com/a/oak_veneer_01"}}}
  • Embedding: the application embeds the images of a set it takes from a texture source; a map given by path alone stays a file of the user’s, read when the view renders.
  • Source: source records where the set came from: id (the texture source: polyhaven, folder, …; letters, digits, _, -), asset (the asset’s id in it), and optionally resolution (2k), license (an SPDX identifier, CC0-1.0) and url (the asset’s web page, http or https). The model keeps and lists it; it never fetches anything.
  • Listing: the appearances query lists each embedded map image as the base colour’s, {"path", "embedded": true, "image_sha256"}, and source as given. That form sent back keeps the images. "embedded": true with image_sha256 keeps the image of that digest the design embeds, also another appearance’s (so a set is reused without sending its images again; refused when the design has none of that digest); without image_sha256 it keeps the image of the same map of the texture it replaces (or of based_on).
  • appearance_image takes map (base_color, the default, or a map above) and gives that image.
  • One copy per image: an image the design embeds already (the same SHA-256) is shared, not copied: in memory, in the states undo keeps, and in the design file. The file keeps a texture’s embedded image in its data as before while no map image is embedded and no image is embedded twice; otherwise every embedded image is kept once in the top-level "images": [{"sha256", "data"}] (in the order of first use) and the textures and maps refer to it by "image": "<sha256>". Opening checks each image (PNG or JPEG, at most 32 MB, its digest, listed once) and refuses a reference to an image that is not there. Files without images and maps open as before, and a design with one embedded texture is written as before. Older versions of MitCad do not open a file with images or maps (an unknown field).
  • The comparison of versions shows each map’s image as sha256 <digest>.

Built-in wood and panel textures

The library’s woods and panels (mitcad#2186: wood_birch, wood_cedar, wood_cherry, wood_douglas_fir, wood_eucalyptus, wood_pine, wood_teak, panel_chipboard, panel_mdf, panel_osb, plywood_birch, plywood_eucalyptus, plywood_pine, plywood_spruce) each have a texture set: a base colour, a normal and a roughness map, 1024 × 1024 JPEG images shipped with MitCad (core/model-base/src/appearance/wood_textures.rs; the images in core/model-base/textures, MitCad’s own, made by tools/wood-textures/generate.sh, MIT licence, listed in core/model-base/textures/README.md).

  • Shipped once, read at run time (mitcad#2218): the images are files in the installation, not data inside the programs, so the application and mitcad-cli share one copy: bin/textures on Windows (beside the programs), usr/share/mitcad/textures in the AppImage, Contents/Resources/textures in the macOS bundle. The model reads them when it first builds the library, from the first of these folders beside the running program that has them, else from the source tree’s core/model-base/textures (a build tree’s programs and the tests). Without the files the looks have no texture and show their colours.

  • Listed as embedded images: the appearances query lists each image as "embedded": true with its image_sha256, as a design’s embedded ones, path <id>-color.jpg, <id>-normal.jpg, <id>-roughness.jpg, and source {"id": "mitcad", "asset": "<id>", "resolution": "1k", "license": "MIT"}; appearance_image gives the bytes. The query lists no image data for any appearance (the images are megabytes, and the application asks often).

  • Real-world size, along the grain: projection grain, one repeat size 800 × 800 mm for the woods, 1000 × 1000 mm for the plywoods' faces, 400 mm for chipboard and 600 mm for MDF and OSB. The images' grain runs along their width; grain lays the width along each face’s longest side, so a panel’s grain follows its length on its faces and long edges, whatever way the body lies; a short end takes its own longest side. The rule (appearance::grain_axes): u and v are the directions of the largest and the middle second moment of the face’s area (exact per triangle, so the mesh does not change them), u’s largest component positive, v turned so that u × v points out of the face; a face about as wide as long (the middle moment more than 0.9 of the largest) takes the longest of X, Y and Z seen in its plane (X first); a point p is at (p · u, p · v) mm, then turned by rotation and divided by size as in the other projections. The application follows the same rule (app/render/GrainProjection.hpp); the USDZ export too.

  • The colour stays: the appearances keep their ids, names, colours and parameters; each base colour image’s mean in linear light is the appearance’s colour, which stays the shaded view’s colour without a texture, the colour of exports and drawings, and display_color.

  • Designs do not change: a library appearance is never saved, so a design that uses one of these ids shows the textures when it opens, its file unchanged; a design’s own appearance (a copy made before) keeps what it has. A copy made now (create_appearance with based_on) takes the set and embeds its three images in the design file, once each.

Render settings

How the rendered view (docs/rendering.md) lights and shows the design (mitcad#47, core/model-base/src/render_settings.rs), kept per document so a design keeps its look. Sections of fields with defaults: the four below and output, the final render’s (Render output, mitcad#48); later sections are added the same way, and files without a section have its defaults. The user’s lights are a list beside them (Render lights, mitcad#54).

Field Values Default
environment.preset studio, studio_white, studio_dark, outdoor, image studio built-in light setups (procedural, no image files): studio soft key, fill and top lights in light grey surroundings; studio_white bright white surroundings, very soft light; studio_dark dark surroundings, a key and two rim lights; outdoor a clear sky and the sun; image an HDR image all around
environment.strength 0–100 1 a factor on all of the environment’s light
environment.rotation rad, within two turns 0 turns the studio’s lights or the image about Z (counter-clockwise from above)
environment.sun_elevation 0–pi/2 rad pi/4 outdoor: the sun’s height above the horizon
environment.sun_azimuth rad, within two turns 5/4 pi outdoor: where the sun is, counter-clockwise from X seen from above (5/4 pi: front left)
environment.image a path none image: an equirectangular .hdr or .exr file, relative to the design file’s folder or absolute; kept when another preset is chosen
background.mode view, color, environment view behind the bodies: the view’s own background (View > Environment), background.color, or the environment itself
background.color sRGB [r, g, b], 0–1 [1, 1, 1]
ground.shadows bool true a ground that shows only the bodies’ shadows (a shadow catcher); without it there is no ground
ground.reflections bool false the ground is glossy and catches the bodies’ reflections too (with shadows)
ground.height mm none the ground’s Z; none: under the lowest body
film.exposure -10–10 stops 0 each stop doubles the light
film.view_transform standard, filmic, neutral standard from light to screen colours: standard sRGB, brighter than white clips; filmic a filmic curve (soft highlights, contrast in the darks); neutral base colours stay as they are under white light, only highlights are compressed
Command Fields Result
set_render_settings per section (environment, background, ground, film, output) an object of the fields that change; null gives a field its default (none for image and height) changed; undo step Change Render Settings unless nothing changes
reset_render_settings changed; the defaults, undo step Reset Render Settings unless they are already
  • Values out of range, unknown fields and sections are refused with the section’s name (ground: unknown field `depth` ); nothing changes then.
  • The commands change no geometry and recompute nothing.
  • The render_settings query gives every section with every field (image and height only when set), and lights.
  • The design file keeps them as "render": {"environment": {...}, "background": {...}, "ground": {...}, "film": {...}} when they are not the defaults (fields left out of a file are the defaults); the comparison of versions lists each changed field as a document change (render.environment.preset studio -> outdoor).

Render lights

Lights of the user’s own (mitcad#54), besides the environment’s: the render settings’ lights, a list in the render_settings query ([] without any), saved with the other sections (files without it have no lights) and changed by commands of their own. Lengths in mm, angles in radians, Z up. Every light keeps every field; those of other kinds are ignored.

Field Values Default
id letters, digits, _, - light<n> what the commands name it by; cannot change
name text Light<n>
type point, spot, area, sun point a point (or small ball) shining all around; a point light in a cone; a glowing rectangle or disc (soft light); parallel light from far away (no position)
enabled bool true off: kept, lights nothing
space world, camera world camera: position and direction are relative to the camera (x to the right, y up, z toward the viewer, from the eye): the light follows the view
position [x, y, z] mm, within 10⁷ [0, 0, 200] where it is (not for sun)
direction [x, y, z], not zero [0, 0, -1] where it shines (spot, area, sun); kept as a unit vector
color sRGB [r, g, b], 0–1 [1, 1, 1]
power 0–10⁶ 5 (sun 2) point, spot, area: watts (a 5 W point light 300 mm away gives 4.4 W/m² where it falls straight, about the default studio’s key light); sun: its irradiance in W/m²
size 0–10⁶ mm 20 point, spot: the ball’s diameter (0: hard shadows); area: the width, or the disc’s diameter
size_y 0–10⁶ mm 20 area: the rectangle’s height
shape rectangle, disc rectangle area
spot_angle more than 0, at most pi pi/4 spot: the cone’s full angle
spot_blend 0–1 0.15 spot: how softly the cone’s edge fades
angle 0–pi/2 0.02 sun: its disc’s angular diameter (0: hard shadows)
Command Fields Result
add_render_light the light’s fields (type sets the default power), all optional; id when not the next free light<n> id; undo step Add Light <name>
edit_render_light id, the fields that change (null: the field’s default) changed; undo step Change Light <name> unless nothing changes
delete_render_light id undo step Delete Light <name>
  • At most 64 lights; ids are unique. Values out of range, unknown fields or kinds and unknown ids are refused with the light’s place (lights.light1.power must be between 0 and 1000000, got -1); nothing changes then. set_render_settings has no lights; reset_render_settings removes them with the other settings.
  • The comparison of versions lists a light added or removed (render.lights.light1 (none) -> Light1 (area)) and its changed fields (render.lights.light1.power 40 -> 60).
  • The model only keeps the lights; the rendered view and the final render light the design with them (docs/rendering.md, “Lights”).

Render output

The final render to an image file (mitcad#48; File > Render Image and mitcad-cli render, docs/rendering.md “Final render”): the render settings’ fifth section, output, with the same rules as the others (set_render_settings with "output": {...}, null for a field’s default; saved when not the defaults, so files of mitcad#47 open with them; compared field by field, render.output.format png -> exr).

Field Values Default
output.width 16–16384 px 1920 the image’s width
output.height 16–16384 px 1080 the image’s height with aspect fixed
output.aspect view, fixed view view: as high as the view is in proportion (the command line, without a view, takes width x height); fixed: width x height, and the view shows the image’s frame
output.samples 1–65536 128 samples per pixel (adaptive sampling can stop converged pixels earlier)
output.time_limit 0–86400 s 0 stop after this long even before the samples are done; 0: no limit
output.denoise bool true denoise once the samples are done
output.transparent bool false an alpha channel instead of the background: only the bodies and their shadows (not for JPEG)
output.format png, png16, jpeg, exr png PNG (8 or 16 bits) and JPEG as the view shows the render (exposure and view transform, sRGB); OpenEXR (half floats) the render’s linear light without exposure and view transform, alpha premultiplied
output.quality 1–100 90 JPEG’s quality
  • Width, height, samples, time limit and quality out of range are refused with the field (output.samples must be between 1 and 65536, got 0).
  • The model only keeps these settings; the application and mitcad-cli render with them.

Render shots

The cameras of the Render workspace’s Frame stage (mitcad#2013, core/model-base/src/render_settings.rs): each shot a named camera that an image is rendered through, as a named view keeps one. The render settings’ shots, a list in the render_settings query ([] without any), changed by commands of their own. Lengths in mm, Z up.

Field Values Default
id letters, digits, _, - shot<n> what the commands name it by; cannot change
name text, unique among the shots Shot<n>
eye [x, y, z] mm, within 10⁷ [0, -500, 0] where the camera is
target [x, y, z] mm, within 10⁷ [0, 0, 0] the point it looks at; not the eye
up [x, y, z], not zero [0, 0, 1] upwards in the image; not along the line of sight
perspective bool true a perspective projection; orthographic when false
height more than 0, within 10⁷ mm 200 how much of the design the image shows: its height at the target
Command Fields Result
add_render_shot the shot’s fields, all optional (the workspace’s Save Shot sends the view’s camera); id when not the next free shot<n> id; undo step Add Shot <name>
edit_render_shot id, the fields that change (null: the field’s default): name renames, the camera’s fields move it (the workspace’s Update to View) changed; undo step Rename Shot <old> to <new> or Change Shot <name> unless nothing changes
delete_render_shot id undo step Delete Shot <name>
  • At most 256 shots; ids and names are unique. Values out of range, unknown fields, a camera that looks nowhere and unknown ids are refused with the shot’s place (shots.shot1: up must not be along the line of sight); nothing changes then. set_render_settings has no shots, and reset_render_settings keeps them: they are cameras, not settings.
  • They change no geometry and recompute nothing. The design file keeps them in "render": {"shots": [...]}, left out when there are none, so a design without shots opens in a MitCad older than mitcad#2013; an older MitCad refuses a design with shots. The comparison of versions lists a shot added or removed (render.shots.shot1 (none) -> Hero) and its changed fields (render.shots.shot1.height 80 -> 120). Reorient turns their cameras with the design, as it turns named views.
  • The application renders a shot as it renders a named view: the Render workspace’s Output stage renders the current shot, and Render All Shots renders each one after the other.

Queries

{"query": "<name>", …}; the result is JSON. Bodies are those at the timeline marker.

Query Fields Result
document features, marker, bodies (count), undo, redo (labels or null), undo_depth, units {length, angle}, warnings (what loading the file changed, such as renamed parameters), revision, modified (not the state last marked saved), display {origin, isolated}; with components components, occurrences (counts), active_component
timeline marker, groups (when any: name, features in timeline order) and features: uid, name, type, suppressed, status (ok, warning, error, suppressed, rolled_back, pending before the first recompute), error (only the error of a failed feature, mitcad#1040; null otherwise), level (error, warning, info for an import note alone, or null), acknowledged (true for a warning the user acknowledged, left out otherwise; see Acknowledged warnings) and notices (when any: the error, the warnings and the import note with their levels; see Notices), import (what the importer said about it, when it did: a fallback, a partial item, a placeholder; see The import’s outcomes on the timeline), component (when not the root), made_component (for a feature that makes a component, a new-component operation or Component from Bodies: that component, which its bodies are in; the timeline marks the feature in its colour; see Features that follow an operation change), for a sketch before the marker dof (0 when fully constrained) and project_again (how many of its linked projections Project Again repairs; left out when none), for a sketch or construction feature visible and visible_set (its light bulb was set), for a feature that uses sketches sketches (their uids in timeline order: profiles, paths, guides, curves or points it refers to, also while it is suppressed or after the marker; the browser lists the feature under each, mitcad#177)
feature uid uid, name, type, suppressed, status, error (only a failure), level, notices (when any), visible, visible_set, warnings (when any; also as notices), import (the import note, when any), missing_profiles (when any: the profiles references of its definition that no region of their sketch shares a curve with any more, {"sketch", "region"}; an edit panel leaves them out, mitcad#1264), def (parameters by name)
parameters name, expression, unit ("" for unitless), value (mm or rad), text (the value in its unit, "12.5 mm"), comment, kind (user, model, reference: a driven dimension’s, read-only), owner (the feature of a model or reference parameter), dependencies (names its expression and its limits use), favorite, group (a user parameter’s group, only when it is in one; Parameter groups); for a user parameter something uses used_by (what keeps delete_parameter from deleting it, in words: features, bindings, CAM setups and operations, the rule <name>, the configurations, and the parameters whose expressions use it, a feature’s as d1 of the feature Extrude1; mitcad#2202); with limits also limits, unclamped, unclamped_text, limited, limit_message, limit_references, and intrinsic for a feature’s own limits (Parameter limits)
parameter_groups groups: every group of user parameters, a parent before its subgroups, in the order they were made: path, name (its own), parent ("" at the top), parameters (the names in it, not in its subgroups) (Parameter groups)
evaluate expression, kind: length (default), angle or unitless; parameter (optional, Parameter limits) value (mm or rad), text (in the document’s unit, "40 mm"), references (parameter names used), expression (with decimal points: "d1 * 1,5" gives "d1 * 1.5"); with parameter also limited, limited_value, limited_text
appearances the library’s and the document’s appearances with their parameters (Appearances)
appearance_image id, map (base_color default, normal, roughness, metalness, occlusion) an embedded image of an appearance’s texture set: data (base64), format, sha256 (Textures, Texture map sets)
render_settings the document’s render settings, every section and field (Render settings)
bodies properties, volumes, versions, bbox, bbox_known uid, name, component (when not the root’s), visible, material, appearance, face_appearances (Appearances of faces) (when set), mesh: true for a mesh body (Mesh bodies in surface operations); with "properties": true also kind (solid, sheet: faces or open shells, mesh, empty), volume, area, center, bbox {min, max} (in the component’s coordinates), faces, edges (counts); with "volumes": true only volume (cheaper); with "versions": true also version, the shape’s version as 32 hexadecimal digits, which changes whenever the body’s shape does (mitcad#689: MCP’s command results list the bodies a command changed); with "bbox": true also bbox without the other properties (mitcad#714: the boxes in MCP’s changes), measured beside each other, except for the bodies bbox_known names ({uid: version}) at their current versions (mitcad#2021: MCP’s snapshot after a command measures only the bodies it added or changed)
profiles hashes, sketch (optional, mitcad#1269: a sketch’s uid or name, as Feature names are not unique reads it; only that sketch’s regions; a name or uid no sketch has is refused), measures (optional, mitcad#1587: each region’s area and center; MCP asks for them), point (optional, [u, v] in sketch coordinates, mitcad#1587: only the region that holds it) sketch, sketch_name, region, consumed (an extrude uses it), face_bounded: true when an implicit supporting-face boundary participates; outline (mitcad#2194: whether the region is in its sketch’s outline set, false for a hole’s disc; left out for a face-bounded region and for a sketch whose closed curves cross) and curves_cross (true on every region of a sketch whose closed curves cross, see The outline set); with "hashes": true also hash (16 hex digits of the region’s geometry and sketch frame: the same while the profile’s face would be the same); with "measures": true also area (mm², the outer loop less the holes, from sampled loops) and center (its centre of area, [u, v])
faces body; geometry, filters surface, min_area, max_area, normal, normal_tolerance, and offset, limit (Faces and edges with geometry) per face: names, surface (plane, cylinder, …), area; with "geometry": true also its surface’s geometry and bbox; with a filter, offset or limit an object: total, offset, faces (each also with index)
edges body; geometry, filters curve, min_length, max_length, radius, between, and offset, limit (Faces and edges with geometry) per edge: name, curve (line, circle, …), length; with "geometry": true also its curve’s geometry and bbox; with a filter, offset or limit an object: total, offset, edges (each also with index)
dependents uid dependents: uid, name of the features that refer to it, directly or through others, in timeline order (what delete_feature with dependents deletes too); a cut-scope exclusion is no reference, so a cut that only excludes the feature’s component or body is not listed (mitcad#1236)
can_reorder uid, index ok, and error (the reason reorder_feature would give) when not
sketch uid see Sketch commands
threads cosmetic (optional, false: only the cosmetic threads, the ones the view draws; a modelled thread is in the geometry, and measuring its face cost a design with modelled threads 0.3-0.6 s each time the window showed it, mitcad#878) threads on the bodies (thread features and tapped holes): feature, name, body, face, standard, designation, class, right_handed, modeled, major_diameter, minor_diameter, pitch, a multi-start thread’s starts and lead (mitcad#893), and from the face internal, radius, start, end (points on the axis where the thread begins and ends; a cosmetic thread’s end chamfers move them to where their cones meet the cylinder). A modelled thread whose crest lies on its face leaves pieces of the face between its grooves, and the face at the marker is measured. A modelled thread feature whose crest lies off its face (a class’s diameters, a radial clearance) takes or covers all of the face along its part, leaving nothing of it (over the whole face) or only what lies outside the part, which does not show where the thread runs: it is listed with the face measured on the body before the feature, as long as the faces it made from it are on the body, and its end chamfers move start and end to where their cones meet the crest (mitcad#433, mitcad#628). A tapped hole’s modelled thread whose crest lies off its wall (a radial clearance) is listed on the wall as the hole measured it before cutting the thread, as long as the thread’s faces made from it are on the body (mitcad#436, mitcad#628); a result stored before mitcad#628 keeps only the walls left without any piece, and a part’s wall in it is measured at the marker
thread_sizes standard (iso_metric, unified, whitworth, npt, tyre_valve, forming_screw, trapezoidal, iso_taper or custom; all when left out) standards, ISO metric first, then Unified, Whitworth (bolt sizes, then the pipe sizes G 1/4), NPT, tyre valve, forming screw and trapezoidal threads (Tr8x1.5, the preferred pitch first), ISO 7-1, and last custom (mitcad#893: "custom": true, no sizes and no classes; its size is given): standard, title (the thread type’s name), default (true for ISO metric), sizes (smallest first: size as the table names it, 10, 1/4, #10; major_diameter mm; designations, the coarse pitch or UNC first, each one thread and hole accept), classes_external, classes_internal, default_class_external (6g, 2A, Medium, Standard, 7e), default_class_internal (6H, 2B, Medium, Standard, 7H); a taper pipe thread’s size also tap_drill (mm: the minor diameter of the internal thread its effective length into it, NPT’s L2 and ISO 7-1’s gauge length, mitcad#733)
thread_chamfer designation, standard (iso_metric when left out), internal (false when left out); for custom (mitcad#893) major and pitch instead of designation the size’s default end chamfer (thread, mitcad#304): diameter (mm, from the size table), angle (45, degrees to the axis)
named_views in the order added: name, eye, target, up, perspective (when true), height
recompute_times the features the last recompute evaluated (cache hits left out), in timeline order: uid, name, type, ms (wall time of its evaluation); and ms, their sum
changes_since_saved known (the state last marked saved is on the undo or redo stack, or is this one), steps: oldest first, the labels of the undo steps made since (Change d3), or Undo <label> for those undone since, leaving out those that changed only the display state; empty when nothing else changed or not known (never saved, a step dropped by a new command after undo)
report timeline and bodies with properties; with components also components and instances (with properties)

Other queries: analysis, components, dxf_info (DXF), cache (Caches), tangent_chains (Tangent chains), measurements and annotations (Measurement objects, Annotations).

  • evaluate reads the expression as a value slot of that kind does: a bare number takes the document’s unit of the kind ("90" as an angle is 90 degrees); a result of the wrong dimensions, a syntax error or an unknown name rejects the query with the reason.
  • report as text is Document::report(false) (what mitcad-cli prints).
  • mitcad-cli info <file> --timings prints the slowest features after opening a design; the ctests cli.perf_recompute and cli.perf_join_recompute do so for generated models (tools/cli/tests/perf_model.json, perf_join_pattern.json: a pattern joined near bodies it does not touch). mitcad-cli run <script> --timings prints how long each step of a script took (Document::run_script_timed; cli.perf_sketch_pattern on perf_sketch_pattern_10.json, mitcad#670).
  • For picking, C++ asks the shape directly: Shape::name_of_edge, Shape::names_of_face and Shape::find_edges (geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/shape.hpp).

Faces and edges with geometry

The faces and edges queries tell where each face and edge is (mitcad#714), in the body’s component’s coordinates, mm and radians:

{"query": "faces", "body": "F2.b0", "geometry": true, "surface": "cylinder",
 "max_area": 500, "offset": 0, "limit": 50}
{"query": "faces", "body": "F2.b0", "normal": [0, 0, 1], "normal_tolerance": 0.001}
{"query": "edges", "body": "F2.b0", "geometry": true, "curve": "circle", "min_length": 30}
  • "geometry": true adds each item’s geometry and its bbox {min, max} (the tight axis-aligned box; null for a face without geometry or a degenerate edge). A face on a plane has origin (the plane’s point nearest to the model origin) and normal (out of the material); on a cylinder or a cone origin (the axis point nearest to the face’s centre), axis (pointing along its largest component) and radius (a cone’s at origin, with half_angle); on a sphere center and radius; on a torus center, axis, major_radius and minor_radius; on other surfaces (B-splines that lie on none of these) only the box. An edge has start and end; a circle or an arc also center, radius and normal (it runs counter-clockwise about the normal from start to end, the same point for a full circle).
  • Filters: faces by surface (the type surface names), min_area and max_area (mm²), normal (planar faces whose outward normal is that direction, of any length, within normal_tolerance radians, default 1e-6); edges by curve, min_length and max_length (mm). Edges also by radius (circles and arcs of that radius within 1e-4 mm) and between (mitcad#1587: one or two surface types, ["cylinder", "sphere"], the types of the two faces the edge lies between, in either order; one type: at least one of its faces of it). All given filters apply together.
  • With a filter, offset or limit the answer is an object: total (the number of items that match), offset, and faces or edges, the matching items from offset on, at most limit of them, each with its index in the body’s face or edge order. Without them it is the array of every item, as before. A large body (hundreds of faces of holes) is read in pages this way.
  • A face stored as a B-spline, Bezier, revolution or extrusion surface that lies within 1e-6 mm of a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere or torus is that one, its surface type and geometry both, and an edge stored as a B-spline or Bezier curve within 1e-6 mm of a line or circle that one (mitcad#1863), as Kernel::face_geometry and Kernel::edge_geometry read a single face or edge (mitcad#1855): the wall of a hole in a sheet body is a cylinder, its rims circles, its flat walls planes. So an MCP pick (ui_select, ui_command’s selection inputs) of such a face or edge without a geometry field, whose type the application reads from these queries, is taken as round. Only faces and edges stored as those types are tested (Kernel::recognised_face_geometries and Kernel::recognised_edge_geometries): all of them where a filter asks for the type (surface, normal, curve, radius, between’s faces), otherwise only the answer’s page. A face found on none of the surfaces is known by its shape afterwards, so asking again about a body of many free-form faces is quick. A kernel that cannot read them leaves the stored types.
  • Kernel::face_geometries and Kernel::edge_geometries describe the items in one pass; Kernel::face_bounding_boxes and Kernel::edge_bounding_boxes measure the boxes of the page’s items only. Tests: api::face_lists_tests, cli.face_geometry (tools/cli/tests/face_geometry.json, a block with two holes on the OCCT kernel).

Analysis queries

Query Fields Result
datums origin (also the origin datums) per datum: uid, name, type and its geometry; display_size where set; a construction plane’s or axis’s drawn (where the application draws it: rect or segment, source, size; Display size of construction planes and axes)
datum uid (F3 or xy) type plane: origin, normal, x_axis, y_axis; axis: origin, direction; point: point; display_size and drawn as datums gives them
properties bodies (default all), components (Physical Properties’ extent), density, densities {uid: g/cm³} bodies, one entry per placement of a body (placed bodies): uid, name, occurrence (a body of a component), material, density, no_material: true when no material is set for it anywhere (the built-in default gives material, density and mass; mitcad#1816), component, component_name and component_bodies (the body’s component, its name and its own body count; not for the root’s bodies), path (the occurrence path by uids, O1/O4; not for the root’s bodies), part (a placed part’s body: its definition with the values and the body’s index as text, the same for equal parts), volume, area, mass, center_of_mass (design coordinates), inertia (3 × 3, at the centre of mass, along the design’s axes), principal_moments, principal_axes, bbox {min, max, size} along the design’s axes, faces, edges, vertices; total: volume, area, mass, center_of_mass, inertia, bbox, faces, edges, vertices; with components also components: uid, name, occurrence

interference bodies (default all), min_volume (mm³, default 1e-6) bodies (count), pairs: a, b, names, volume
section plane, bodies (default all), world (default false) plane, per body edges, faces, length, area, clip, and the totals with cut, kept and removed (Section Analysis past every body)
compare_step file, bodies, step_body (name or index), samples, fuzzy, max_deviation, max_relative step_bodies, volume, step_volume, volume_only_mitcad, volume_only_step, relative_difference, max_deviation, mitcad_to_step and step_to_mitcad {max, rms, at, samples}, bounds_difference; with limits pass and exceeded
  • Units: mm, mm², mm³, g/cm³, kg, kg mm², radians. Density: densities[uid], else the body’s material (its own, else the nearest component default up the occurrence path that places it), else density for bodies without one. A body with none of these has no material (mitcad#1817): material null, no_material true, no density, mass, inertia or principal_moments (its volume, area, center and box as any body’s), and the total then has no mass, inertia or center_of_mass but no_material, how many such entries it counts; the text answer says no material and no mass. Never steel unasked.
  • A selection is {"body": "F2.b0"} with an optional "face", "edge" or "vertex", {"datum": "F5"} (or an origin datum, "xy", "x", "origin", in any case), either with an optional "occurrence" (a path from the root by ids, "O1/O4", or by names, "Arm:1/Pin:2"; Measure in the design), an entity as ui_state lists the selection ({"kind": "face", "owner": "F2.b0", "name": …, "occurrence": …}; Selections by names and as entities), or text: "Body1", "F2.b0", "Body1/F2:end(r{c5})", "xy", "F5". A section plane is a plane reference.
  • Kernels without an analysis answer with an error (the geometry kernel does not support …).
  • Volumes, areas, centres and masses are integrated as How volumes and areas are computed says.
  • Document::analysis(query, json) (C++ analysis) answers properties, measure, interference, section, compare_step and datums as text (mitcad-cli) or pretty JSON.

analysis_shape(request) returns a shape handle for display, null when there is none:

shape Fields Shape
datum uid (F3, xy), size (default 100) a square face, an edge or a vertex
section plane, body, occurrence (optional), curves (default false) the section faces, or curves
clip plane, body, occurrence (optional) the body without the half-space on the plane’s normal side; what is left of its faces, edges and vertices keeps the body’s names (picks on the clipped view refer to the body), faces on the plane stay whole, and the caps have no names. A body the plane does not reach is not cut (mitcad#438): one behind the plane (touching it at most) is the body’s own shape, one wholly on the normal side an empty compound
interference a, b (bodies) their overlap

Mesh bodies (triangles without surfaces, from STL, OBJ and the meshes of imported models) are sectioned and clipped triangle by triangle (mitcad#392): the section edges are one straight edge per triangle the plane crosses (an edge of triangles lying in the plane counts once), and it has faces and an area only when the mesh is closed. The clip shape keeps the triangles behind the plane, cut along it, with the section faces as planar caps when the mesh is closed; when the plane removes nothing it is the body itself. A body that mixes mesh faces with faces on surfaces is an error.

By default, section queries and the section/clip shapes operate in component-local coordinates, preserving the original API. With world:true, the section query resolves its plane in design coordinates and measures each visible occurrence separately; entries also include occurrence (UID path) and component. Repeated bodies contribute once per visible occurrence. Resolve an ambiguous plane reference with section_plane first and pass its fixed origin/normal to this query.

The section and clip shape requests accept an optional occurrence UID path for the body. When supplied, their input plane is in design coordinates and is transformed into that occurrence’s local coordinates. The returned shape remains local: display it using the body’s original placement. The path must own the body. This gives every displayed component the same physical cutting plane without applying placement twice.

Section Analysis of many bodies (mitcad#438)

analysis_clips(request) (C++ Document::analysis_clips) clips several bodies at one plane at once, as the clip shape clips each: {"plane": <plane>, "bodies": [{"body": "F2.b0", "occurrence": "O1/O2"}, …]} (occurrence optional, as for clip). The result has one entry per body in the request’s order (count, shape(i), error(i)): the clipped shape, or null with the error the clip request would give that body (an unknown body, an occurrence that does not own it, a failed boolean); one body’s error does not stop the others. Section Analysis and Hide Above Sketch clip the bodies shown with it (MainWindow::modelBodies).

The bodies’ booleans run on all cores (OCCT’s thread pool, each body one operation of geometry::run_operation, so a crash inside OCCT is that body’s error), and so do the sections of the section query with world:true (Kernel::clip_all and Kernel::section_all, whose defaults take one body after another). A body the plane does not reach needs no boolean: its kept bounding box tells the bridge (core/cpp/bridge/analysis.cpp) that the clip keeps or removes it whole, or that the plane passes it farther than the body’s tolerances, which gives an empty section.

Section Analysis off the UI thread (mitcad#438)

prepare_clips(request) (C++ Document::prepare_clips) takes the same request as analysis_clips and prepare_query(request) a section query ({"query": "section", ...}, the only query it prepares; another is refused as an invalid prepared query): each takes from the document what the work needs (each body’s shape with the plane in its coordinates, the answer’s fields, or a body’s error) while the document is idle, and its run() works it out later without the document, on any thread, as the document would have answered when it was prepared: what it holds of the bodies stays as it was when the document changes. The section worker of the application runs them (app/framework/SectionWorker.hpp). What they hold is detached from the bodies when they are prepared (Kernel::detach_all, whose default takes the shapes as they are): a body the plane may cut or touch as a copy that shares no face, edge or vertex with it, with the same face names, its box and its mesh faces' triangles; a body the plane passes farther than its tolerances as itself, its box measured then, which alone tells its clip (kept or removed whole) and its empty section. So run() never reads a sub-shape the application’s view or a model job may write into meanwhile (meshes), and what it clips can be meshed on its thread. A clipped body is what is left of its copy (the copy itself when the clip leaves it whole after all); a body the plane passes and keeps is its own shape, as with analysis_clips. input(i) and detached(i) tell what the clip of body i reads. Both stop when the running thread’s geometry is told to (geometry/cancel.hpp): the bodies not started by then fail as cancelled.

Section Analysis over a feature preview (mitcad#943)

A body of the analysis_clips and prepare_clips requests takes two more fields: "preview": true clips the body as the previewed command leaves it (Document::preview’s result, as preview_body_shape gives it) instead of the body at the marker, also a body the preview makes, which is no body at the marker (an error body … is not in the preview when the preview has no such body, or there is no preview); and "transform": {"linear": [[…], […], […]], "translation": [x, y, z]}, the rigid placement that puts the body in the design where the view draws it (a preview’s moved occurrence, a body the preview makes), takes the plane into the body’s coordinates by its inverse instead of by occurrence (which it replaces; the body’s component is not checked). {"plane": {"origin": [10, 0, 0], "normal": [1, 0, 0]}, "bodies": [{"body": "F2.b0", "preview": true, "transform": {"linear": [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]], "translation": [0, 0, 0]}}]}. The application clips the bodies a feature preview draws with their new shapes or placements this way while Section Analysis or Hide Above Sketch is on (app/framework/SectionPreview.hpp), prepared while the document holds the preview and run on the section worker.

Section Analysis past every body (mitcad#824)
