The section query’s answer also tells what the clip of the view does with each body: each body’s clip is cut, kept (whole: its box lies behind the plane, touching it at most) or removed (whole: its box lies on the plane’s normal side, touching it at most), told from the body’s box as the clip shape and analysis_clips tell it without a boolean (analysis::clip_side, within Precision::Confusion; a body without a box counts as cut). cut, kept and removed count them; with world they count the visible occurrences the query measures, a body once per occurrence. A plane that cuts none of the bodies (cut 0) leaves the view empty (all removed) or shows the bodies uncut (all kept), with a zero area and length; a plane on a face of a body behind it keeps the body (kept) while its section is that face. prepare_query answers the same: the boxes are read when it is prepared. The text answer (Document::analysis, mitcad-cli) adds The plane cuts no body: <n> kept whole, <m> removed whole then. Section Analysis’ panel shows a warning instead of the zero totals in that case (app/COMMANDS.md).

Physical Properties’ extent (mitcad#1095)

The properties query places the bodies as the design places them and also gives each body’s overall size and its topology, and their totals (physical_extent.rs):

  • Placed bodies (mitcad#1110): a body counts once per occurrence that places it, as the Center of Mass query counts it. bodies has one entry per placement, in the document’s order of the bodies and the assembly’s order of the occurrences; the entry of a body of a component has occurrence, the path’s name (Arm:2, Frame:1/Arm:2), and the root’s bodies have none. Each entry’s center_of_mass, inertia and principal_axes are in the design’s coordinates, moved and turned by its occurrence (mass, volume, area and the principal moments do not change with a rigid placement), and its material and density are what the body has on that occurrence path: its own material, else the nearest component default up the path, else the root’s, else none (no_material, no mass, mitcad#1817). Each body’s properties are computed once per density. A body asked for in bodies and also in a component of components counts once per occurrence. The total adds every entry, so a component placed twice counts twice; over every body (neither bodies nor components, every body of a material) its mass, volume and center_of_mass are the center_of_mass query’s. A body that no occurrence places (a component placed nowhere) has one entry, in its own coordinates; the center_of_mass query leaves it out.
  • bbox {min, max, size}: the axis-aligned box along the design’s axes, of the body at its entry’s placement; the total’s is the box around all the entries'.
  • faces, edges, vertices: how many distinct faces, edges and vertices the body has (Kernel::topology_counts: an edge two faces share counts once, a seam edge once); the total’s are the sums over the entries, a body counted once per placement (as its mass is). A mesh body (STL, OBJ, an imported model’s mesh) has its box but no counts: its faces are groups of triangles, not faces on surfaces, so the three fields are left out, and the total sums the other bodies (it has no counts when no body has them).
  • components: components whose bodies count, those of their sub-components included, besides bodies. An entry is a component’s uid or name ("C2", "Arm": every placement of it counts), or {"component": …, "occurrence": …} with either or both: occurrence (a path from the root by uids, "O1/O4", or by names, "Arm:1/Pin:2") takes the component only as placed there, the way the app’s selection of a component in the view or the browser names it. The root component is the whole design. The answer then lists components (uid, name, and occurrence, the path’s name, when one was given), which Physical Properties’ window names in its title. An unknown component or occurrence, or an occurrence that places another component, is an error. With neither bodies nor components, every body counts, with all its placements.
  • A kernel without boxes or topology counts leaves the fields out.
  • The text answer (Document::analysis, mitcad-cli) names an entry’s occurrence after the body (Body1 (F4.b0) in Arm:2: Steel, …) and adds a body’s bounding box [min] to [max], size X x Y x Z mm and F faces, E edges, V vertices, and the totals’ before the Total: line.

Tests: physical_properties_tests (core/model-tests/analysis: two boxes, one in a turned component, along the design’s axes; the counts; a component’s bodies with its sub-component’s; a component placed twice and moved, an entry per occurrence with the total the center_of_mass query’s; an occurrence in a component with a default material), the unit test of the turned inertia tensor in physical_extent.rs, cli.analysis (tools/cli/tests/analysis.json, on the OCCT kernel), the Physical Properties steps of tools/ui-modify-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-workflow-test.ps1.

Preview

preview takes an add_feature or edit_feature command and evaluates it on a copy of the document without committing it. An add_feature’s component (mitcad#1856) evaluates it in that component, as add_feature would add it there; the active one when left out. The result:

{"uid": "F5", "name": "Extrude3", "status": "ok", "error": null, "warnings": [],
 "bodies": [{"uid": "F2.b0", "name": "Body1", "changed": true}], "removed": [], "tool": true}
  • bodies: all bodies at the marker after the command (changed: new or modified by it); removed: the bodies it removes; warnings: what a feature that succeeded built with caveats (the status stays ok).
  • A pattern adds elements: every element’s transform as 3 rows of 4 by element number, suppressed ones too. A construction feature adds its datum. A sweep adds sweep_path, where its profile lies on its path (sweep, mitcad#795); a pipe too, with the number of its path’s sharp corners (pipe, mitcad#1448).
  • A move or move_occurrence whose motion is a rotate, point_to_point or point_to_position adds motion (mitcad#838): what the motion was worked out from, in the feature’s component’s coordinates: {"type": "rotate", "origin": [x, y, z], "direction": [x, y, z]} (the axis it turns right-handed about, a unit direction), {"type": "point_to_point", "from": [...], "to": [...]} or {"type": "point_to_position", "point": [...]}. The app’s drag of the angle or the position moves the shown bodies by it without asking the model again, about the same axis as the result. Test: f4_tests::move_previews_report_what_their_motion_turns_about. A move_face reports it alike, from the same resolution of its transform (mitcad#854), and so does a preview that failed after its motion was worked out (a motion that moves nothing, faces that cannot follow it), so that the app’s Rotate ring keeps turning about the model’s axis. Test: f4_tests::move_face_previews_report_the_axis_they_turn_about.
  • A command that places occurrences elsewhere (a joint, a move_occurrence; mitcad#55) adds placements: each occurrence whose placement in the design changes, path (uids from the root, O1/O4; an occurrence inside a moved one is listed too) and transform (4x4, in the design), so a preview can show the bodies where it puts them.
  • instances (when there are any): the occurrence/body pairs the command makes, each body, occurrence (uids from the root, O1/O4; empty in the root), transform (4x4, in the design) and visible (false in a hidden occurrence or for a hidden body); a new body has one in each occurrence of its component, at that occurrence’s placement. removed_instances: the pairs the command takes away (body, occurrence). Every other body keeps its pairs: a display shows it where and when the instances query shows it, with preview_body_shape for a changed one. A body neither shown nor in a visible new pair (a hidden body, one in a hidden occurrence, one an isolation leaves out) stays hidden, also when the command changes it, and no body is drawn without a pair’s placement (mitcad#266; the app: app/framework/PreviewBodies.hpp).
  • preview_body_shape(uid) returns a body as the command leaves it and preview_tool_shape() the extrusion before its boolean (a split’s or trim’s extended tool: The extended tool of a split or trim).
  • tool_instances (with tool): where that tool is in the design. The tool is in its feature’s component’s coordinates, so there is one entry per occurrence of that component (one with an empty occurrence in the root): occurrence (uids from the root), transform (4x4, in the design) and visible (false in a hidden occurrence). A display draws the tool, and the app’s provisional drag proxy of it, at these placements (mitcad#636).
  • An edit_feature preview computes the feature in its own component (not the active one) under its own uid, and when the marker is before the feature (an editor rolls it back) the feature is still computed, the later ones staying rolled back (mitcad#309). With through (the marker the editor rolled back from, mitcad#1860) the features right after it that only place occurrences (joints, as-built joints, rigid groups, constraint sets, motion links, move_occurrence and capture_position; suppressed ones passed over) are computed too, up to through: an assembly’s later joints and rigid groups hold in the preview as in the design, and placements lists the occurrences they place. The first other feature and those after it stay rolled back, so an edit’s preview never recomputes later geometry.
  • The next command or clear_preview drops the preview; committing the same command reuses its results.

Scripts

run_script (mitcad-cli run) takes an array of steps: commands, comments ({"comment": "…"}) and expectations ({"expect": {…}}), which check the document after the steps before them. Examples: tools/cli/tests/*.json.

Expectation Checks
"bodies": n bodies at the marker
"body": "Body1" (name or uid) "volume", "area" (relative "tolerance", default 1e-6), "faces", "edges" (counts), "has_face", "no_face" (mitcad#1588), "has_edge", "no_edge" (names), "min", "max" (bounding box corners, the same tolerance), "bbox": {"min", "max"}, "center" (of mass; "tolerance" in mm), "min_face_area" (every face has at least this area, mm²: no slivers)
"total_volume" all bodies
"occurrence" (a path, or an occurrence placed once) with "body" the body as placed: volume, area, center, bbox, min, max
"instances", "world_volume" the visible placed bodies: count, sum of volumes
"feature": "Fillet1" (name or uid; a name several features share is refused, Feature names are not unique) "status", "error_contains"
"parameter": "d3" "value"
"sketch": "Sketch1" (name or uid; of a shared name the only sketch) "regions" (its region keys in any order), "dof"
"query": {…} "result": the query’s answer contains it (objects: the keys given; arrays: element by element; numbers within the relative "tolerance", default 1e-6), e.g. {"expect": {"query": {"query": "datum", "uid": "F3"}, "result": {"origin": [0, 0, 30]}}}; "none" / "some" (mitcad#1702): no element / at least one element of the answer (an array) contains the value given, e.g. "none": {"occurrence": "O2"}

A spline in a query’s answer (degree, control, weights, knots, as the sketch and plane_geometry queries give a curve) is compared by where it runs with "runs" in its expected geometry (mitcad#1669): {"geometry": {"runs": {"ends": [[52, 6], [68, 6]], "through": [[60, 10]], "length": 18.5459}}}: its two ends in either order, points it passes through (the nearest point of the curve) and its length, each within the "runs" object’s own "tolerance" in millimetres (default 1e-6), not the expectation’s relative one. A spline the kernel approximates (where two surfaces cross) has other control points, knots and parameters on another platform along the same path, so an expectation names where it runs instead of pinning those (cli.plane_geometry_bodies). Lines, circles, arcs and vertices are compared by their values as before.

The first failing step stops the script: steps[4]: expected Body1 to have volume 48000, got 47961.37.

Sketch commands

Every sketch.* command but sketch.create names its sketch with "sketch": "F1" and is one undo step (Add Line to Sketch1). An edit works on a copy of the definition: the sketch is solved from the edited positions with the current parameter values and the solution is stored. An edit after which the sketch no longer solves is rejected, naming the constraints in conflict, as is a constraint or driving dimension the others already imply (add the dimension driven instead).

A point input is [x, y] (a new point) or "p3" (an existing point, which joins the new curve to it). The drawing tools’ point inputs take either (mitcad#1269); a field that takes only a position ([x, y]: a direction, a pick place, a point the tool only measures) says so in its row. A new point [x, y] is always a point of its own, also where a curve ends: it is not joined to that end by its position (give the end’s id, or join the two ends afterwards with a coincident, which makes them one point, Points that become one). A coordinate of a drawing tool’s new point may be a text, an expression of parameters (["w", 5], ["w/2", "h + 3"]), kept as a dimension from the sketch’s origin so that the point follows the parameters, see Point coordinates as expressions.

Ids are given out by two counters per sketch (mitcad#1269): points, curves and texts share one numbering (p3, c4 and t5 are three different entities, and "p4" names nothing when 4 is the curve c4), constraints, dimensions, patterns and offsets another (k6). Take the ids from a command’s result (entities, made, constraints, dimensions, in the order they were made) or from the sketch query; never predict the ids a command will make. In one model_command array, a later entry takes an earlier entry’s ids from its result by name, {"ref": "l1.end"} (References between the entries of a command array). A point id that names a curve is refused saying so. A sketch definition (add_feature, edit_feature, a file) in which two of them have the same number is refused naming both, entity c1 has the id number of p1: curves, points and texts share one numbering; the first one keeps the number (mitcad#1485).

Values follow Values; a new dimension gets a model parameter owned by the sketch (Sketch1 fillet radius). Tool sizes (radius, width, count …) are plain numbers: a tool only draws, and dimensions are added separately.

Results of editing commands: entities (new points and curves), constraints, dimensions (new ids), parameters (created), texts, removed (when anything was removed), made (the main curves the tool made, in order) and status (as the sketch query: dof, fully_constrained, redundant, conflicts). A drawing command’s result also has inputs (mitcad#1897): each point input field with the point at it as written ({"start": "p3", "through": null, "end": "p4"}; null where the command makes no point of its own; a spline’s points as a list), and with expression coordinates coordinates, see Point coordinates as expressions.

Command Fields Notes
sketch.create plane (default xy; xz, yz, a construction plane "F5", {"face": …, "body": …} or a curved face {"face": …, "body": …, "developed": {"angle": …}}, see Sketches on cylindrical and conical faces), frame, name (optional), occurrence and context (optional: a plane of another component, see Geometry of other components), upright (default false; see An upright sketch frame), project_face (default false: on a planar face, its outline projected into the sketch, linked, in the same undo step; see The face’s outline in a sketch on a face) result uid, name; with project_face, projected (the outline’s entities) or warnings (why it was not projected)
sketch.add_rectangle corner [x, y] (a position only: the corner is a new fixed point; sketch.rectangle takes point ids), width, height (values) a dimensioned rectangle: fixed first corner, horizontal and vertical constraints, width and height dimensions; result also curves, region
sketch.add_circle center [x, y] (a position only: the centre is a new fixed point; sketch.circle takes a point id), diameter (value) fixed centre and a diameter dimension; result also curves, region
sketch.add_point at [x, y] (a position: the new point; its coordinates may be expressions, mitcad#1897), fixed
sketch.add_line start, end (point inputs), construction, centerline; mode (optional): two_point (the default: start, end) or midpoint (center, end: the line runs through center to end and as far on the other side; mitcad#1393) midpoint makes a point at center (or takes the existing point given) and holds it at the line’s middle with a midpoint constraint; made: the line
sketch.rectangle mode: two_point (a, b corners), three_point (side a–b, c on the opposite side: a position [x, y] only), center (center, corner); a, b, center and corner are point inputs (an existing point is that corner, or the centre point held at the diagonal’s middle, mitcad#1269); construction; radius (value, optional: rounded corners, Rounded rectangles and fillets of several corners) four joined lines (counter-clockwise), horizontal and vertical (perpendicular for three_point), a construction diagonal with the centre at its midpoint for center; with radius also four arcs (made: the lines, then the arcs)
sketch.circle mode: center (center point input, radius), two_point (a, b: a diameter), three_point (a, b, c), two_tangent (lines [2], radius, near: a position [x, y] only), three_tangent (lines [3]); construction; a, b and c are point inputs: an existing point is held on the circle with a coincident (mitcad#1269) tangent constraints for the tangent modes
sketch.arc mode: three_point (start, through, end), center (center, start, end: the direction of the end, a position [x, y] only, clockwise), tangent (from: an end point of a curve, end), normal (from: an end point of a line or a circular arc, end: the arc leaves from square to that curve, toward the side toward is on, a position [x, y], else the side end is on; mitcad#1393, mitcad#1608); construction; the other points are point inputs: start and end are the arc’s ends, center its centre point, and an existing point as through is held on the arc with a coincident (mitcad#1269) tangent adds a tangent constraint; normal holds the arc’s centre on the line with a coincident, or adds a construction line from the circular arc’s centre to from that the new arc is tangent to
sketch.polygon center, vertex (point inputs, mitcad#1269: an existing point as center is the polygon’s centre point, no new one is made; as the vertex of an inscribed polygon it is the first corner; a circumscribed polygon’s vertex is a position [x, y] only), sides (3–256), inscribed (default true; false: vertex is a side’s middle), construction joined lines that stay a regular polygon (four degrees of freedom: placement, orientation, size; mitcad#303): inscribed, equal sides with the corners on a construction circle; circumscribed, the sides tangent to a construction circle and the corners on a second construction circle around the same centre point (the first circle is the one through vertex). Polygons stored earlier keep their constraints
sketch.slot mode: center_to_center (a, b), center_point (center, end: an end’s centre), arc (center, start, end: the direction of the far end, a position [x, y] only); width; the other points are point inputs: an existing point is that end arc’s centre, the slot’s middle (held at its centre line’s middle) or the arc slot’s centre (mitcad#1269) two end arcs, two tangent sides, a construction centre line or arc with the arc centres at its ends, equal end arcs
sketch.ellipse center (point input), major (end of the major axis; a point input, mitcad#1269), minor_radius, start and end (point inputs; an elliptical arc), construction
sketch.spline points (point inputs), degree (optional), closed (optional, mitcad#783), construction without degree a cubic through the points; with it, a B-spline with these control points; closed (fit points only, at least three): the cubic runs on from the last point back to the first and is smooth through it
sketch.add_text text, at (or frame; at is a position [x, y] only: a text has no point there), height, angle, font, bold, italic, align, valign, spacing, frame (three point ids, or {"corner": [x, y], "diagonal": [x, y]}: a new construction rectangle, turned by angle), path, flip_x, flip_y, cap_height, wrap, line_spacing, pen_align, ink_top, no_kerning, glyphs (stored outlines, see the sketch definition’s texts), font_file (a font file’s path instead of font, mitcad#473: the file’s family becomes font, its outlines of the text are stored; a file that cannot be read or is not a font is refused), value (a text parameter’s name or a text expression the text follows, Text parameters; text may then be left out) the glyphs bound profiles
sketch.edit_text id, and any of text, at, height, angle, font, bold, italic, align, valign, spacing, path, flip_x, flip_y, cap_height, wrap, line_spacing, pen_align, ink_top, no_kerning, font_file (a font file’s path; "" leaves the file for font), value (a text parameter’s name or a text expression the text follows; "" stops it following one, Text parameters) a new text, font, bold or italic drops the text’s stored glyphs; for a text in a font file it stores the file’s outlines again (refused when the file is not there, or when its path came with the design and no font_file is given, mitcad#929), and another font leaves the file
sketch.add_constraint constraint: as in the definition, without id a coincident between the end points of two curves merges them into one point (see Points that become one): the result has no new constraint, removed lists the removed point (and what the merge dropped), and merged is {"kept": "p3", "removed": "p7"}; a constraint that older geometric constraints imply in part replaces them: removed lists them and implied_removed is [{"constraint": "k1", "type": "horizontal"}] (see A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant); auto (default false): only when safe, nothing else changes (see Constraints a drawing tool adds automatically); check (default false): nothing changes, the answer {"check": true} says it would be added, else it is refused as it would be (see A constraint only checked)
sketch.add_dimension dimension: as in the definition, without id, value, driven; value (default: what it measures now), driven, text [x, y]
sketch.set_dimension dimension (k3), value a number or an expression changes the dimension’s own parameter; a parameter name makes the dimension use that parameter; name = expression renames its parameter and sets it (see Values); a value that uses the dimension’s own parameter keeps that parameter as a user parameter, and its bare name only moves it there (result user_parameters, mitcad#1535; see Values); a driven dimension becomes driving (its reference parameter becomes its parameter, under the same name)
sketch.set_driven dimension, driven (default true) driving again keeps the measured value; driven, its own parameter becomes its reference parameter
sketch.set_signed dimension (a horizontal_distance or vertical_distance), signed (default true) the point stays where it is: a driving value is negated where b lies on the negative side (see Signed point dimensions)
sketch.set_dimension_text dimension (k3), text [x, y] where the value is shown; undo step Move Dimension in Sketch1
sketch.set_active items (constraints and dimensions, k3), active (default true), reason (optional, with active false) inactive ones are kept but left out of the solve; activating is refused when the sketch then does not solve or is over-constrained; made lists the items whose state changed; undo step Activate in Sketch1 / Deactivate in Sketch1 (see Inactive constraints and dimensions)
sketch.redefine_plane plane (optional, as sketch.create), occurrence, context, offset, x, y, angle (values; left out: kept, a plain zero: none), flip, upright the sketch moved to another plane or face and placed there; a plane after the sketch is refused; undo step Redefine Plane of Sketch1 (see Redefine Sketch Plane)
sketch.remove items: p3, c4, t5, k6 a point takes the curves that use it, a curve its points no other curve uses; constraints and dimensions on removed entities go too; a curve or point a derived offset computes (a spline or ellipse chain’s) is refused, its source goes with the offset (mitcad#361); an offset (k8) removed leaves its curves as plain sketch geometry, no longer tied to its source (mitcad#1755, see offsets in the sketch definition); a pattern (k5) removed leaves its originals and copies where they are as plain sketch geometry (Free Pattern), and a pattern’s copy removed leaves its instance out of the pattern (skipped, mitcad#2007, see patterns in the sketch definition)
sketch.set_construction curves, construction (default true)
sketch.set_centerline lines, centerline (default true)
sketch.set_fixed entities, fixed (default true)
sketch.drag entity: a point with to [x, y], or a curve with by [dx, dy] or radius; or entities (points and curves) with by pulls as far as the constraints allow; a derived offset’s curve or point pulls its source chain by as much; entities drags a selection together (see Dragging a selection)
sketch.move entities and/or texts (texts moved or copied with them, mitcad#1911; see Moving and copying texts), and by [dx, dy], or from and to (point inputs: Point to Point, by to − from, both read before the move; mitcad#1563), or rotate {center (point input; left out: the entities’ middle, mitcad#1563), angle}; copy; hold (constraints added after the move where it was dropped, a moved entity standing for its copy, mitcad#1645; see Holding moved geometry where it was dropped); a move is read once: a coordinate written as an expression in by, from, to or rotate’s center is refused in words (mitcad#1912) a move keeps the constraints (the points are dragged); a copy copies the constraints among the entities; a derived offset’s curves move their source chain, their copies are ordinary curves; made lists the copies; a rotation turns what holds the moved geometry to the axes, see Rotating sketch geometry
sketch.trim curve, at [x, y] removes the piece around at between the curves crossing it; a curve nothing crosses is deleted; a cut end on an existing point becomes that point, so that both curves of a crossing trimmed there share one end; a projected or computed point holds it with a point-to-point coincident instead, and elsewhere (a T) the end is a new point on the crossing curve (mitcad#1191, see Points that become one); a joined end that meets a curve there tangentially gets a tangent to it, and a tangent that held the cut-off end to a curve no longer touching it then goes (mitcad#1220, same section); a curve trimmed in the middle falls into two, a line’s pieces collinear and an arc’s or an elliptical arc’s equal, so that they stay on one line or curve (mitcad#1314); of a closed spline the rest becomes a spline by control points (mitcad#783); refused for a projected curve (linked or not: sketch.convert_projected first, mitcad#357, also for sketch.extend, sketch.fillet and sketch.chamfer); on a curve an offset made (either kind) all of that offset’s curves first become plain sketch geometry, no longer tied to the source nor made again from it, with the note the offset is no longer linked to its source (mitcad#1755, also for sketch.extend, sketch.fillet and sketch.chamfer; see offsets in the sketch definition); on a pattern’s curve (an original or a copy) that pattern is first freed into plain sketch geometry, with the note the pattern's copies are now plain sketch geometry (mitcad#2007, also for sketch.extend, sketch.fillet and sketch.chamfer; see patterns in the sketch definition); a trim or an extension that ends on a derived offset’s curve ends in a plain point, since its curves take no constraints (mitcad#361)
sketch.extend curve, at extends the end nearest at (a line or an arc) to the next curve; an arc extended all the way round becomes a circle; reaching an existing point joins it (a shared end; a projected or computed point holds the end with a point-to-point coincident instead), elsewhere the end lies on the curve; result joined: the point reached, when it joined one (see Points that become one)
sketch.extend_to_meet a, at_a [x, y], b, at_b [x, y] (lines and arcs, each picked on the part that stays), result (which result, nearest the picks first: 0, the default; counted round) extends or shortens both curves to a point where their whole lines and circles meet, the two ends becoming one point; constraints and dimensions on the curves keep their meaning (a length or an arc length takes the new value); refused in words where they never meet; result joined (the shared point), results, result; see Extend to Meet (mitcad#2178)
sketch.break curve, at [x, y] (with mode point also an existing point id), mode (crossings, the default, or point) splits a curve into pieces that all stay (mitcad#2108): crossings (Break) at the crossings that bound the piece around at, on one side or both, found as sketch.trim finds them (a crossing end on an existing point becomes that point, elsewhere a new point held on the crossing curve); point (Split at Point) at the curve point nearest at, or at the existing point at names, which becomes the pieces’ shared end (a projected or computed point holds a new end with a point-to-point coincident); the pieces share one point at each split; a line’s pieces are collinear, each with the one before; an arc’s or an elliptical arc’s pieces keep the centre (and an ellipse’s major point) and so stay on one circle or ellipse without an equal; a spline’s pieces become splines by control points, tangent where they meet when the sketch still solves with it; a circle or an ellipse breaks between the two crossings around at into two arcs (the curve keeps the rest, a new curve the piece around at), a closed spline into two splines; constraints and dimensions of the curve go to the piece they belong to: one on an end point keeps naming it (on the piece that has it), a point-on-curve goes to the piece the point lies on, a tangent or smooth to the piece at its point or the piece that touches the other curve, the rest stay on the first piece, which the others follow (a radius, a horizontal, a parallel); a midpoint on the curve goes (no piece has the old middle), and so do a line’s equal, a symmetric of the curve and an arc length, each counted in notes in words; a line’s length becomes a driven distance between its old ends, with a note; refused in words for a split at an end of the curve, where nothing crosses it (crossings), for a closed curve fewer than two curves cross or that point would open at one point, and for a projected curve (sketch.convert_projected first); an offset’s or a pattern’s curve is first freed with sketch.trim’s notes; result: made (the pieces in order along the curve, the curve first), notes; one undo step Break (Split at Point for point), and a work step break (split)
sketch.insert_spline_point curve (a spline), at [x, y] a point on the spline where it is nearest at: a fit point between its neighbours, or a control point by knot insertion that keeps the shape exactly; result made: the new point; see Insert Point on a spline (mitcad#836)
sketch.fillet a, b (lines, or a circular arc and a line or arc that end together, mitcad#1192), or curves (lines and arcs) and/or points (corners) for several corners; radius (value) a tangent arc with a radius dimension; the corner stays as a point on both curves (Fillets at corners of arcs), and a length dimension of either line becomes a distance to it, so dimensions keep their meaning; several corners: one arc each, one radius dimension and the others Equal to the first (Rounded rectangles and fillets of several corners)
sketch.chamfer a, b, distance, and distance2 or angle (values) a line and its distance (and distance or angle) dimensions from the kept corner
sketch.offset curves (a chain of joined curves, or one closed curve), distance (value), corners ("sharp", default, or "round": see Rounded corners of offsets) to the right of the chain direction (a closed curve: positive is out); one parameter for the distance; an offsets record (derived with ellipses and splines); result constraints [the offset’s id] and warnings; a curve the same as another counts once, see Projected outlines and their offsets; curves that vanish at the distance are left out and their neighbors trimmed to meet, named in the record’s dropped and the result’s notes (mitcad#1234, see offsets in the sketch definition); lines on one line across them are one result (merged), and a closed chain may fall into several outlines in one record (outlines, mitcad#1244); sketch.trim, sketch.extend, sketch.fillet, sketch.chamfer or sketch.convert_projected on one of its curves, or sketch.remove of the offset, frees its curves from the source as plain sketch geometry (mitcad#1755)
sketch.edit_offset offset (k8), distance (value), flip, corners ("sharp" or "round"; left out, as they are) the distance changes, flip moves it to the other side, other corners make it again with them (mitcad#1774); the curves keep their ids; when other curves vanish at the new distance the offset is made again, kept curves keeping their ids and a curve that comes back getting a new one (mitcad#1234)
sketch.mirror entities, axis (a line c4, or the sketch’s own axis "x" or "y", made in the same undo step when the sketch has none, see The sketch’s axes and origin as entities; mitcad#876) copies with symmetric constraints (an ellipse copy also keeps an equal minor radius); points on the axis are shared; the axis line among entities is left out (refused only when nothing else is left), and a point whose curve is mirrored too (a circle’s centre picked with the circle) gets no symmetry of its own, which would be redundant (mitcad#876)
sketch.circular_pattern entities, center (point input; a new point is fixed, or, with a coordinate written as an expression, held by signed dimensions from the origin in both coordinates so that it follows the parameters, mitcad#1912), count (originals included), angle (value, default a full turn) a patterns record; result constraints [the pattern’s id]
sketch.rectangular_pattern entities, direction (default [1, 0]), direction2 (the second direction, at any angle to the first but parallel, refused then; left out: a quarter turn counter-clockwise from the first, mitcad#1969), count [n1, n2], spacing [s1, s2] (values, signed: a negative spacing goes against its direction, mitcad#447; not zero), symmetric ([bool, bool], default none: per direction the originals are the middle instance, an odd count, and the copies lie on both sides) as above
sketch.edit_pattern pattern (k5), and any of count (n, or [n1, n2]), angle, spacing, direction, direction2 (null: back to a quarter turn from the first; left out: kept), center (as sketch.circular_pattern’s), entities (the originals) the copies follow
sketch.project source: an edge, a face (its outline seen along the sketch’s normal: its boundary edges without the seams off the outline, and its silhouettes; see Projecting a curved face, mitcad#1265) or a vertex of the bodies before the sketch (left out only for a section of a whole body, mitcad#736), or a curve or point of an earlier sketch, {"sketch": "F1", "curve": "c4"} / {"point": "p3"}, or {"sketch": "F1"} for all its curves (see Projecting another sketch’s curves and points, mitcad#904), body (optional; none for a sketch’s geometry), linked (default false), occurrence and context (optional: geometry of another component, see Geometry of other components), section (default false: a face’s or a body’s section curves, or the crossing points of an edge or of another sketch’s curves, instead; see Section curves in sketches) fixed reference entities, a curve or point the same as another of the source once; a planar B-spline seen edge on is the line between its extreme points (mitcad#389), as a conic is; a linked projection follows its source when the model changes, each entity the fresh curve of its kind most like it (by_geometry in its record, since 0.4.1); a projection without it (files of earlier versions, imports) follows only a source whose curves come back of the same kinds, in the same order and joined the same way, or the same curves listed in another order or from another start, only moved or resized (each pairs with one of its kind, none is left over and nothing tears; mitcad#1303), and otherwise keeps its geometry and warns (mitcad#249); one that cannot follow is repaired by Project Again; joined to the projected geometry already in the sketch, see Projected outlines and their offsets
sketch.import_dxf path (.dxf), unit (of a drawing that names none: mm default, cm, m, in, ft), at (the sketch point the drawing’s origin goes to, default [0, 0]), layers (only the entities on these layers; all when left out; a layer with nothing on it is refused) as other edits, and curves, points (shared points made), text_count, warnings; undo step Insert DXF into Sketch1; see DXF
sketch.import_svg path (.svg), scale, at, stroke_outline (mitcad#473) see SVG
sketch.add_code text (the content), at (the lower left corner, default [0, 0]), module (mm, default 1), angle, kind (qr), ecc (L, M default, Q, H) (mitcad#473) a text with code (see the sketch definition’s texts), texts [its id]; undo step Add QR Code to Sketch1; a content no QR code holds (too long for the level) or a module of no size is refused
sketch.edit_code id (t5), and any of text, at, module, angle, ecc undo step Edit QR Code in Sketch1; refused as sketch.add_code
sketch.clean_up_projections merge (default true: also lines on or overlapping a collinear one) as other edits, and cleaned ([{"curve", "kept", "how", "link"}]; how: same, on or joined; link: the source the removed curve followed when the kept one does not) and warnings (what it removed, links lost, regions later features use that change their names); undo step Clean Up Projections in Sketch1; see Clean Up Projections
sketch.clean_up_stale_projections none as other edits, and stale ({"removed": [curves], "trimmed": [lines], "unlinked": [sources], "kept": [{"curve", "why"}], "preview": {"removed": [{"curve", "type", "geometry"}], "cut": [{"line", "start", "end"}]}}; why: region, user_curve, constrained or used; preview: the removed curves as they were, geometry as the sketch query gives it, and the pieces trimmed off lines, from the old end to the new one, for a preview to draw) and warnings (the same in words, and regions later features use that change their names); undo step Clean Up Stale Projections in Sketch1; see Clean Up Stale Projections
sketch.project_again projection (optional: its index in the sketch’s projections, an entity of it such as "c4", or its source’s name; all the sketch’s linked projections that do not follow when left out), successor (optional, mitcad#1784: for one whose source edge is gone, one of its candidates, the edge on its curve that took its place, which becomes its source; the projection with that candidate when projection is left out) as other edits, and again (one per projection: {"source", "carried": [{"from", "to"}], "kept": [{"entity", "held_by"}], "left": [constraints and dimensions]}: the old entities and the new ones that took their place, the old ones kept as construction references with the constraints, dimensions, patterns, offsets, texts and curves that hold them, and the constraints and dimensions that stay on them) and warnings (what was kept and why, curves the same as another projection’s, regions later features use that change their names); undo step Project Again in Sketch1; refused for a projection that follows its source and for one whose source is gone (one with candidates asks for a successor); see Project Again (mitcad#1303)
sketch.convert_projected entities: curves and points; profiles (optional, region keys of the sketch, mitcad#2051: the projected curves of their boundaries, and the face’s edges that bound them projected first; see The face’s outline in a sketch on a face) the projected ones become ordinary free sketch geometry, and a curve an offset made frees all of that offset’s curves from its source (mitcad#1755); as other edits, and converted (the entities converted, an offset’s curves too), kept (their points that stay projected), offsets (the offsets freed, when any; a note says the offset is no longer linked to its source) and warnings; undo step Convert to Sketch Geometry in Sketch1; see Convert to Sketch Geometry
sketch.explode_text text (t5: a text or a QR code) the text becomes plain, unconstrained lines and splines (degree 2 or 3) where it is laid out, the pieces of each contour sharing their end points; later features’ names of its pieces rewritten to them; result made (the new curves), rewritten, warnings; undo step Explode Text in Sketch1; see Explode Text

The sketch query ({"query": "sketch", "uid": "F1"}) returns:

  • uid, name, plane, frame (origin, x_axis, y_axis, normal in the coordinates of the sketch’s component, moved into the design by an occurrence’s world placement, mitcad#958; or null when the sketch did not evaluate), solved, error;
  • warnings: the sketch evaluation’s (as the timeline’s), such as linked projections that could not follow their sources; then the solve’s redundant constraints (mitcad#1171), one warning per offset, pattern and the sketch’s own that has any, counted by kind, without ids (mitcad#1612): An offset: 2 dimensions follow from the others, A pattern: 1 constraint follows from the others, Redundant: 1 dimension and 1 fixed entity follow from the others (an offset’s own are its lines’ distances and parallels, its helpers’ lengths and point-on-curve constraints, and its held corners; a pattern’s its bindings);
  • warning_entities (mitcad#264): one list of entity ids per warning, in the order of warnings, of what the warning is about, so that a client need not read the text: a linked projection’s warning lists all of its entities when it is kept or lost, else its stale curves when it has any, else its unfollowed entities; the warning about collapsed curves (mitcad#365: a line of no length, a circle or arc of no radius, which make no region) lists those curves, also as degenerate beside dof and redundant; a warning about redundant constraints lists the entities they name (an offset’s or a pattern’s own bindings: its results or entities; a fixed entity itself); a warning about anything else (a font replaced) has an empty list. The warnings entries stay strings (the timeline and feature queries’ are the same strings), so their readers are unchanged;
  • entities: the definition’s (linked projections, and what is constrained to them, where the last evaluation put them: their sources' current geometry), with solved at for points, geometry for curves (line start, end; circle center, radius; arc also start_angle, end_angle, start, end; ellipse major_radius, minor_radius, rotation; splines degree, control, weights, knots) and fully_constrained; entities a derived offset computes have "derived": true;
  • constraints, dimensions (with parameter names, measured, and for a driving one its parameter’s expression and comment), projections (each also, after an evaluation where it did not follow all the way: unfollowed, its entities that found nothing like them in the source; unmatched, how many of the source’s curves and points none of its entities follows; lost: the source is gone; kept: its curves no longer match the source’s, so it kept its last geometry: following by geometry would tear an arc from the curves it shares points with, or one without by_geometry found them changed, mitcad#249; stale: its curves that match none of the source’s current curves, all of them for a lost source, mitcad#252; successor: the edge on the same curve it followed in its source’s place, candidates: for a lost source, the edges on a curve of its kind that could have taken its place, none of them alone, and candidate_curves, each one’s kind and size for a list a person reads (mitcad#1794); see A source edge merged or split, mitcad#1784);
  • texts, also family (the font used), fallback (the bundled font instead of the one asked for), stored_outlines (true when the outlines are the text’s stored glyphs, its font missing; family is then the text’s font and fallback false), lines (the lines it was laid out in: its \n breaks and, with wrap, the breaks that fit it to its frame’s width, mitcad#2029; not for a QR code) and outline: [{"id": "t9.g0.c0", "curves": [geometry, …]}]; a text’s stored glyphs are left out, has_glyphs true in their place;
  • patterns and offsets, also values and value: parameter, value, expression;
  • regions: key, area, centroid, loops (segment keys, outer loop first), perimeter (mm, the length of all its loops, holes included: lines, circles and arcs exactly, ellipses to a few parts in a million; left out when a loop has a spline; mitcad#1741, the selection card’s); a glyph’s region also text and letter (false for a counter);
  • outline_set (the keys of the regions in the sketch’s outline set, a plate less its holes; empty when its closed curves cross) and curves_cross (true when two of its closed curves cross through each other), mitcad#2194, see The outline set;
  • dof, fully_constrained (entity ids), redundant (constraint ids implied by the others, all of them; the warnings group them, and fixes that follow only from other fixes are not listed, mitcad#1171), partly_redundant (only when not empty: those of them that still take degrees of freedom away, with how many, {"k9": 1}; information, not warnings, see Rounded corners of offsets and partly implied constraints, mitcad#1992) and conflicts (sets of ids that contradict each other; error says it in words, see Conflicting constraints);
  • unmet_inactive (only when not empty): the inactive constraints and dimensions the geometry does not meet (Inactive constraints and dimensions);
  • order: the ids of the points, curves, constraints and dimensions in the order they were made (see The order of a sketch’s items, mitcad#1492);
  • steps: the work steps that made them, in that order (see The work steps of a sketch, mitcad#1750): {"id": "s2", "kind": "rectangle", "items": ["c1", "p5", …]} (a trim’s or an extension’s also changed, the curves it changed), an item no step holds as {"items": ["p7"]}.

The positions, curves and status come from the sketch’s last evaluation while it succeeded and was made from the definition and the parameter values the document has now (mitcad#679: Document::evaluated_solve; the definition the result cache keeps with the evaluation, and the values it read). A sketch with projections, one that failed, is rolled back or suppressed, or whose definition or values changed since is solved by the query, with the same result. The document also keeps the last answers (Document::known_sketch_answer), each with the sketch’s definition, its evaluation, warnings and the parameters it was made from: asked again while none of them changed, the query answers at once. A drag’s edit stores the drag’s own solve instead of solving its result again, so one sketch.drag solves twice: the drag and the recompute.

Clean Up Projections

sketch.clean_up_projections (mitcad#232, sketch/cleanup.rs) tidies projected (reference) curves; nothing else does it automatically across projections, since two projections that coincide now may differ after a change (the region finder counts coincident curves once, so they make no slivers):

  • a curve the same as another (either way round, its own points or shared) goes; the lower id stays, which keeps the regions’ names;
  • with merge, a line on a longer collinear one goes, and two collinear lines that overlap and follow no source become one (the lower id, from the outer ends);
  • constraints, dimensions and other curves that used the removed curve or its points use the kept curve and its points there; constraints that then say nothing (a curve parallel to itself) go; a curve a pattern, an offset or a text uses stays;
  • a kept curve follows its own projection’s source only (link in cleaned, and a warning): a merged curve is not split again when the sources differ;
  • a region whose name changes (names are made of curve ids) and that a later feature uses is a warning; the whole is one undo step, and it is refused when there is nothing to clean up.

Clean Up Stale Projections

sketch.clean_up_stale_projections (mitcad#252, sketch/stale.rs) tidies a sketch whose linked projections stopped following their sources (the source changed shape since: an imported projection, a face edited upstream). It works on the curves the last evaluation found stale (the sketch query’s stale of each projection), so the sketch must have evaluated:

  • a stale curve goes when it matters to nothing: it bounds no region a later feature uses (the profiles later features sweep, as they find them, and the regions their definitions name) and names no segment of one (a curve at a segment’s end), no pattern, offset or text uses it, no constraint or dimension ties it, or a point that goes with it, to geometry that stays, and no curve of the user’s ends on it; the others stay, listed in kept with why;
  • a stale line that stays because it bounds a used region, and runs past the region, is trimmed to where the region’s last segment on it ends (the user’s line that closes the profile, the new outline’s corner); only an end that nothing else holds moves (an old corner that only other stale lines share gets a point of its own), only when the points constrained onto the line stay on what is left and no dimension measures it, and only when every used region keeps its name and area;
  • a projection that would still not follow (kept, lost, or with stale or unfollowed entities left) is unlinked: its entities stay as fixed references and the sketch stops warning; one whose entities all go goes with them. A projection is never linked again by geometry (by_geometry): following by geometry moves its entities to the nearest curves of the source, which can change the profiles and faces later features and other sketches see;
  • a region whose name changes and that a later feature uses is a warning; the whole is one undo step, and it is refused when there is nothing to clean up.

Project Again

sketch.project_again (mitcad#1303, sketch/again.rs) repairs a linked projection that did not follow its source at the last evaluation: one that kept its geometry (kept: its curves no longer match the source’s) or has entities that found nothing like them (unfollowed) or that match nothing of the source (stale). Its source must be there (a lost one is for Clean Up Stale Projections). The projection is made anew from the source’s curves as that evaluation found them, as sketch.project makes it (joined to the other projections of the same body, by_geometry from then on), and what the sketch tied to its old entities goes with them where that is unambiguous:

  • the old outline is laid over the new one (its bounds moved and scaled onto the new outline’s), so that an outline that moved or was resized covers itself;
  • an old curve goes to the new curve of its kind (a circle and an arc count as one kind) that covers the most of it: the new curves nearest to more than half of 17 points along it, new curves on one line or one circle counted together (an arc split in two goes to its larger piece); a curve no new one covers so goes nowhere;
  • a point of such a curve goes to the new curve’s point in the same role (a line’s end, either way round; an arc’s centre and ends), another point to the new point nearest to where it lies; each only within a tenth of the new outline’s size, and the nearest only when no other new point is within twice its distance;
  • a constraint or dimension on them moves with them when every one of its entities of the projection moves (one that needs an arc’s ends or length, as Arc Length or Midpoint, stays off an arc that became a circle), and so do the ends of the user’s curves on its points and an offset whose curves all go one to one to curves of their kind; constraints that then say nothing (two arcs Equal that became one circle) go;
  • a new entity that takes the place of old ones takes the lowest of their ids, so that the regions keep their names where their outline is the same; a region whose name changes and that a later feature uses is a warning;
  • the old entities go; one that something still needs (a constraint or a dimension that did not move, a pattern, an offset or a text, a curve of the user’s ending on a point that did not move) stays outside the projection, a curve as a construction reference, listed in kept with what holds it, so that nothing is dropped silently; points the projection shares with another projection stay as they are;
  • the whole is one undo step; the sketch must solve after it, or it is refused.

A projection that only moved or was resized follows on its own, without Project Again: one recorded without by_geometry (an import’s, an earlier version’s) whose source lists the same curves in another order or from another start, and one with by_geometry whose nearest-first pairing would tear its arcs from the curves they share points with, follows when another pairing (the order of the lists, or nearest once the old outline’s bounds are laid over the new one’s) pairs every entity with one of its kind, leaves none of the source’s over and tears nothing. So does one whose arcs of one circle, joined end to end, now come from the source as one arc of their whole sweep (the kernel no longer splits a rounded end where it did, mitcad#1325): that arc is split as the projection’s are, at the same angles from its start, and the projection keeps its pieces (only where every such run of the projection splits that sweep the same way).

The timeline query’s project_again counts the projections it repairs; the application offers it in the sketch’s context menu, under the warning in the Sketch Palette and in the timeline’s tooltip.

Tests: core/model-tests/sketch-refs/src/project_again_tests.rs (with the mock kernel: an outline of two arcs and two lines whose arc comes back in two pieces, kept, then repaired with its offset dimensions and parallels carried over and one undo step; a circle that becomes two arcs and two lines and back; an import’s projection listed from another start that follows on its own; an outline whose arc in two pieces comes back as one arc, in place and moved, follows with its offset ring, mitcad#1325), tools/ui-project-again-test.sh (Linux) and tools/ui-windows-projections-test.ps1 (Windows).

A source edge merged or split

A model change can make one edge of several that lay on one curve (a disc’s rim that the corners of a prism touching it split into arcs, the corners moved off it) or split one edge into several (a new face across it). A linked projection of such an edge (mitcad#1784, core/sketch/src/successor.rs, core/model/src/features/projection_successors.rs) follows the edges on the same carrier of its curve’s kind, a circle or arc about one centre (its radius may change, as for a resize) or a line on one line:

  • its source is gone: the edges between the faces it lay between (each face as the shape names it now: its pieces, the whole face it was a piece of, or the face a sketch change renamed it as) whose curves are of its kind; its source’s name finds the pieces instead (all of them of its kind, nothing of them like its curve): those pieces;
  • they must all lie on one carrier, and its used points (those a constraint, a dimension or a curve outside the projection needs) must have one place: the piece that holds all of its used ends, of those the one that holds most of its ends;
  • a line or an arc within that piece keeps its span where it was when an end of it is used, and becomes the piece otherwise; one that is not within it becomes the piece; an arc whose ends nothing uses keeps its span where several pieces would do (its centre has one place); a circle follows the circle through the pieces;
  • an arc of what is now one whole circle becomes that circle (mitcad#1794) when its ends are used by nothing (no constraint, dimension, curve, pattern or text) and nothing on the arc needs an arc (an arc length, a pattern, an offset or a text on it; Coincident, Tangent, Equal, Concentric, Symmetric, radius, diameter and the distances to a circle hold a circle as they hold it); its id and centre stay, and the sketch as it evaluated (what the sketch query shows and edits start from) has the circle without the arc’s ends, so the next edit keeps it as a circle; with an end used, or something on it that needs an arc, it keeps its span on the circle. In a 3D sketch’s kept projections (below) an arc always keeps its span: a 3D sketch’s curves take only their points’ places and radii from what they follow;
  • it then follows without a warning, with an information notice, “the projection of an edge follows an edge on the same curve, which took its place when edges were merged or split” (its places the old and the new edge; the agents’ text and projections[].successor name them); it follows again at every evaluation, so it follows the edge as that moves or is resized.

With none, or with several that leave its used points no one place, it keeps its last geometry and warns as before (lost), and the sketch query lists the edges that could have taken its place (candidates). sketch.project_again with one of them as successor makes that edge the projection’s source and projects it again from it, as Project Again projects one; without it Project Again refuses such a projection and asks for one. The sketch query describes each candidate for a list a person reads (candidate_curves, one per name in candidates, mitcad#1794): {"type", "length", "radius"}, its curve of the projection’s kind as projected onto the sketch’s plane (line, arc or circle; radius for an arc or a circle; lengths in mm). The application’s Project Again offers them so (mitcad#1794, app/COMMANDS.md): a row per candidate that says in words which edge it is, the edge painted while the pointer is over its row, the chosen one the successor.

3D sketches follow the same way (mitcad#1794):

  • a converted sketch’s kept linked projections (mitcad#1550) follow as a planar sketch’s do, with the same information notice and candidates;
  • a linked reference record (an attachment or a reference curve, mitcad#1543) whose edge is gone takes the edge between the faces it lay between (as above) when exactly one is there whose curve is a line, a circle or an arc, with the information notice “a reference of the 3D sketch follows an edge between the same faces, which took the place of its edge when edges were merged or split” (its places the old and the new edge; the agents’ text names them); an attachment at an end or the middle takes none that is a whole circle, which has no ends. A 3D sketch keeps no last geometry of a record, so with several (or none) nothing says which: the record fails as before (“the edge does not exist at this point of the timeline”), the agents’ text listing the edges that could have taken its place.

Tests: core/model-tests/sketch-refs/src/projection_successor_tests.rs (with the mock kernel: an arc of a rim that became one circle, followed, the hole on its centre with it, also when the disc moves, and the arc the whole circle, kept so by an edit; the same arc with a used end, and with an arc length on it, keeping its span; a circle split into arcs; a line split in two, the piece that holds its used end; two edges on two lines, which warn and are listed, and Project Again with one of them as its successor; a 3D sketch’s point at the middle of a gone edge, which follows the one edge between the same faces and fails with two; a converted sketch’s kept projection that follows).

Points that become one

Curves are joined only through a shared point (Offset’s chains, the chain selection, the free-end markers); two ends held together by a point-to-point coincident are two ends. So (mitcad#259, mitcad#260, mitcad#1191, sketch/points.rs):

  • sketch.extend: when the extension’s nearest hit lies on an existing point (within the tolerance of the full-turn check), the extended end becomes that point: a point of the curve reached first, else any other (the lower id), never one of the extended curve. A projected point, or one a derived offset computes or a pattern makes, is the model’s: the end is a new point with a point-to-point coincident to it. Elsewhere the end point stays (mitcad#362): when only the extended curve ends it and it is not fixed, projected, computed or a pattern’s, it moves onto the curve reached and keeps its id, its constraints and its dimensions (the extent constraints of the curve, its length, arc length and midpoints, go), and a coincident holds it on the curve; a dimension on it whose parameter is a plain number of its own takes the value it now measures, one with an expression or a shared parameter keeps its value and holds. Any other end is a new point on the curve reached. A hit in the middle of a curve (a T junction) is not a split; collinear lines stay two lines.
  • sketch.trim (mitcad#1191): a cut end that lies on an existing point (within the same tolerance as Extend’s; where the two curves touch, whose computed contact is only accurate to about 5e-5 of the sketch size, within that) becomes that point by the same rules: a point of the crossing curve first, else any other (the lower id), never one of the trimmed curve; a point that is none of the crossing curve’s points (a lone point, another curve’s end) is held on it with a point-on-curve coincident unless one holds it there already; a projected, computed or pattern point holds a new end with a point-to-point coincident. A point-on-curve of the joined point on the trimmed curve, which its end now holds, goes. So both curves of a crossing, trimmed there one after the other in either order, end in one point, also two arcs that touch. A cut in the middle of the crossing curve (a T) is a new point on it, as before. A joined end that meets a curve there tangentially (the crossing curve or another curve ending at the joined point; directions within 1e-3, as a cut where curves touch) gets a tangent to it, as the Line and Arc tools add one when drawing tangentially (mitcad#1220): not where an active tangent or smooth between the two holds there already, not between two lines or with an ellipse or a derived offset’s curve, and not when the others already imply it or it conflicts (the solve’s redundant or conflicting constraints would grow). When such a tangent takes the place of the cut-off end (a trim that cuts off one end), a tangent that held that end to a curve that met it there and no longer touches the trimmed curve (the two share no point) goes: it held the joint that is gone. A tangent that still constrains something real stays: one at a point the curve still has, one between curves that still share a point, and every tangent where no new one took the old one’s place (a join at an angle, a trim that splits a curve in two). So a slot extended by a second one, its old top trimmed where its arcs touch the new sides, is held as before.
  • sketch.add_constraint with a coincident between two points that are both ends of curves (lines, arcs, elliptical arcs, spline ends) merges them: one is kept (a fixed point over a free one, else the one more constraints and dimensions name, else the lower id) and everything that named the other (curve ends, constraints, dimensions, text frames) names the kept one. Constraints and dimensions that then say nothing go (a distance between the two points, a point-on-curve on a curve the point now ends, the same constraint twice); a point symmetric to itself about a line becomes a point on the line. The sketch is solved with the coincidence first, where it solves, so the kept point is where the solve puts it; a merged sketch that does not solve, or that the merge over-constrains, is refused, and nothing changes. It stays a constraint when either point is no curve end (a lone point, a centre, a spline’s inner point), one curve has both points, both are fixed, or either is projected, computed by a derived offset or a pattern’s. Existing constraints are not migrated.

Convert to Sketch Geometry

sketch.convert_projected (mitcad#257, sketch/convert.rs) turns the projected (reference) curves and points among entities into ordinary sketch geometry: not reference, not fixed, out of their linked projection’s entities:

  • a curve takes its points with it, except a point a projected curve that stays also uses: that point stays projected (fixed, still following), the converted curve joined to it, and it is listed in kept;
  • a projected point given (a projected vertex) converts the same way when no projected curve that stays uses it;
  • a projection with nothing left goes; the others follow their sources for what is left. One without by_geometry (an import’s, or of a file of an earlier version) follows only a source whose curves come back as it listed them, so with some of its entities converted it keeps its geometry from then on, which warnings says;
  • constraints and dimensions stay (the sketch may get degrees of freedom); region keys do not change (a key naming a face edge a converted curve lies on finds its region by that curve, see The face’s outline in a sketch on a face); a stale curve converted is no longer stale;
  • a curve an offset made (mitcad#1755) frees that offset: all of its curves become plain sketch geometry, no longer tied to the source nor made again from it (see offsets in the sketch definition, “Freed from the source”); they are listed in converted, the offset in offsets, and a note says the offset is no longer linked to its source;
  • other entities that are not projected are left as they are (warnings); the command is refused when none of entities is projected or an offset’s curve, or when nothing would convert (only points projected curves that stay use).

The face’s outline in a sketch on a face

A sketch on a planar face of a body can start with the face’s outline, and a profile can be converted whole (mitcad#2051):

  • sketch.create with "project_face": true on a planar face ({"face": …, "body": …}, also another component’s with occurrence) projects the face’s outline into the new sketch as sketch.project with the face as source and "linked": true does, in the undo step that adds the sketch (Add Sketch2). The result lists the outline’s entities in projected; a projection that fails leaves the sketch empty, with the reason in warnings. Origin planes, construction planes and curved faces get nothing, and so does every call without the field (scripts, imports). Create Sketch in the application sets it from its Sketch preference. The outline is a linked projection of the face marked "automatic": true in the sketch’s projections (saved with the design, mitcad#2197): like the face’s own edges, its curves do not split an area the sketch’s own curves close (see Profile selections); a face outline the user projects with sketch.project has no mark and splits as any projection does. Project Again keeps the mark, Convert to Sketch Geometry (which takes the projection away) drops it, and the converted curves are the user’s from then on. sketch.redefine_plane keeps the projection (it stays a projection of the old face, which sketch.clean_up_stale_projections handles once that face is gone).
  • The outline lies on the face’s edges that bound the sketch’s regions (face-bounded regions, mitcad#1138). Each piece counts once: a stored curve on a face edge stands for it (the regions and their count are those of the sketch without the outline), and a region key that names a face edge a stored curve now stands for finds the region by that curve (Layout::aliased, sketch/regions.rs). So a key taken before the face’s edges were projected, or before their projections were converted, keeps resolving.
  • sketch.convert_projected with profiles converts the projected curves on the boundaries (outer and inner loops) of those regions, with their projected points, as entities of those curves would; with entities too, the union. A face edge that bounds such a region (a face-bounded region of a sketch without the outline, face_bounded in profiles) is projected first, linked, and converted in the same step. One undo step Convert to Sketch Geometry in Sketch2, the result as with entities. Refused for a key the sketch has no region for and for a region bounded only by ordinary sketch geometry.
  • The sketch query’s regions carry "projected": true for a region whose boundary has projected curves; with face_bounded it tells the application where Convert to Sketch Geometry applies.

A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant

A new constraint the others already imply is refused (“the new constraint would over-constrain the sketch: …”; a new driving dimension “the new dimension …”, without ids since mitcad#1566). When it is implied only in part, it replaces the older constraint it makes redundant, as the user’s last intent (mitcad#287, SketchEdit::drop_implied in sketch/edit.rs): a rectangle standing on a projected line, its bottom horizontal and its left corner coincident with the line’s left end; a coincident of its right corner with the line’s right end fixes the corner’s x, which nothing else does, and its height, which the left corner and the horizontal already fix. The horizontal goes and the coincident is added:

  • sketch.add_constraint removes older geometric constraints from the redundant sets the new constraint makes (the solver’s diagnosis), one at a time, each only when it lowers the redundant count, until the count is back where it was before the command; the new constraint must still take at least one degree of freedom away.
  • Never removed: a dimension, a fixed entity, an equal_spacing and a constraint on projected geometry (the links that hold the sketch to the model). When only those would do, nothing is removed and the constraint is refused as before; a constraint that contradicts the others (a dimension of another length) fails the solve and is refused.
  • The result lists the removed constraints in removed and, with their types, in implied_removed: [{"constraint": "k1", "type": "horizontal"}]. The command is one undo step: undo restores them.
  • The sketch tools show it as a hint (Horizontal removed: implied by the new Coincident), also for a constraint a snap makes while drawing.
  • The removal tries first the constraints on the new constraint’s own movable geometry (its points and curves and the points of those curves, not fixed ones such as an axis or the origin), then the others, each group in id order (mitcad#865): a Symmetry of two circles replaces the constraint that held one of the circles, not one further along the chain its position follows from.

A constraint only checked

sketch.add_constraint with "check": true (mitcad#2184) runs the same edit on a copy of the design and drops it: nothing changes, not the sketch, its solution, the undo history or the evaluated design (Document::check_sketch_edit in core/model/src/document.rs). When the constraint would be added the answer is {"check": true}, with the merged and implied_removed the command would give; otherwise the command is refused with the words the plain command would give (implied by the others, a conflict, a kind of curve it does not take). With auto it checks the automatic addition.

The sketch’s Horizontal/Vertical asks with it which direction to add (app/COMMANDS.md, “Horizontal/Vertical in the other direction”): two points nearer to level whose heights are already held, the fixed point p1 (-10, 6) and p2 held on a fixed line along y = 0, refuse horizontal_points (a conflict) and take vertical_points, which puts p2 at (-10, 0). Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_constraint_check_2184_tests.rs.

Symmetry of circles with fixed radii

A symmetric constraint of two circles or two arcs mirrors their centres and makes their radii equal (an arc: its ends mirrored, start to end). When the others already make the radii equal (both dimensioned, or an equal), sketch.add_constraint leaves the radius equality out (mitcad#865, SketchEdit::fit_symmetric in sketch/edit.rs) and stores the constraint with "radii": false: it then mirrors the positions only (the centres, and an arc’s end directions from its centre), so that it takes what is not fixed yet instead of over-constraining the sketch:

  • Implied in part, it replaces the older geometric constraints it makes redundant, as in A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant, never a dimension: four Ø10 circles in a dimensioned square, the bottom left one free along a construction diagonal (1 degree of freedom), and a Symmetry of the two left circles about the x axis: the radii are left to the dimensions, the bottom left centre’s coincident with the diagonal goes, and the sketch is fully constrained.
  • Implied in full, it is refused as before (the new constraint would over-constrain the sketch: …).
  • Without radii (all designs before), or with two radii free, the radii are made equal as before.

Rounded corners of offsets and partly implied constraints

GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#324 (mitcad#1774): a rounded outline at a distance round a projected triangle, its lines parallel to the triangle’s sides at the distance and an arc at each corner, drawn three ways.

  • A constraint implied only in part is kept. sketch.add_constraint (and sketch.add_dimension, sketch.set_driven, sketch.set_active and the holds of Move/Copy) refuse what the others imply in full: it raises the solve’s redundant count and takes no degree of freedom away (SketchEdit::require_needed with edit::Freedom; “the new constraint would over-constrain the sketch: it takes no freedom away, the others already fix all it constrains (a dimension can be added as driven)”). A constraint that contradicts the others is refused by what blocks it ("… can’t hold with the new constraint", Conflicting constraints). One that raises the count but takes at least one degree of freedom away is added: the centre of an arc tangent to two parallel offset lines slides along the corner’s bisector (its radius is free); a coincident of the centre with the corner is two equations of which one (the centre on the bisector) follows from the tangents, and it fixes the radius. Before, it was refused as if the others fixed all it constrains. Where removing older geometric constraints brings the count back, they still go in its favour first (A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant); else its redundant part is listed in redundant like any other, and undo, the constraint list and the sketch’s status show it as any constraint.
  • A constraint redundant only in part is information (mitcad#1992, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#420). The solver reports the newest constraint of a dependent set as redundant, also when only some of its equations follow from the others: a Symmetry of a construction arc’s ends about the y axis, the arc’s centre on the origin, is two equations (the ends' middle on the axis, the ends level), and with the ends equally far from the centre one follows from the other, while the Symmetry still takes a degree of freedom away. The sketch query tries each of the sketch’s own redundant constraints and dimensions (at most eight; none of an offset or a pattern) without it, from the solved positions (SketchDef::freedom_taken): one whose leaving out raises the degrees of freedom stays in redundant, is listed in partly_redundant ({"k9": 1}: the degrees of freedom it takes away; only when there is one), is no warning, and is information about it in notices (its target the constraint’s id): “the Symmetry between two points about an axis partly repeats the others; it still removes one degree of freedom” (several: “… removes 2 degrees of freedom”; conflict::partly). One the others imply in full takes nothing away and stays a warning (“Redundant: … follows from …”). Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_partly_redundant_1992_tests.rs and, with MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED, the reporter’s design in core/model-tests/files/src/sketch_partly_redundant_reported_1992_tests.rs.
  • Redundant constraints in words. The sketch’s own redundant constraints and dimensions (of no offset or pattern), when there are at most three and no fixed entity among them, are each a warning that says what it follows from: “Redundant: the Coincident between a point and a projected point follows from the Tangent between a line and an arc and the projected geometry” (conflict::follows), with the entities it names; more are counted as before (“Redundant: 4 constraints follow from the others”).
  • Singular points (mitcad_solver’s analysis::regular_nearby): without the tangents, each arc’s radius is free (3 degrees of freedom), but where an arc touches the line it ends on (its circle meets the line in a double point) the linearized equations lose rank: the arc’s ends seemed free to slide along the lines (6 degrees of freedom), the lines' distances followed from the rest, and a drag got nowhere. Where a part of the sketch has consistent dependent equations and free unknowns, the analysis moves every unknown by up to 1e-3 of the sketch size (the same pseudo-random amounts every time), solves again from there, and takes the rank found there (with a stricter tolerance) where it is higher: a rank only drops at special points of the solution set. A drag that gets nowhere from such a point is taken again from a point beside it, and kept when it gets nearer (solve::nudge). The sketch then has 3 degrees of freedom, nothing redundant, and dragging an arc changes its radius. Where the lines are an offset’s results (the reporter’s), each solve started them at the offset of their sources’ ends (mitcad#641), which put a dragged arc back to the distance; an end of a result line that a curve the offset did not make goes through now starts where it is along the line (offset::seed), so the drag stays.
  • A line distance between lines that are not parallel: line_distance holds (and measures) the distance of the middle of the second line from the first, which is the lines’ distance only where they are parallel. The solved sketch lists such dimensions in not_parallel (the sketch query, and an edit’s status, only when there is one; the ends of the second line lie at distances from the first that differ by more than 1e-5 mm), and warns “a distance between lines that are not parallel: it holds the middle of one line, not the lines’ distance (the Dimension tool gives an angle for such lines)” (several: “2 distances between lines that are not parallel: …”), a warning of the sketch’s evaluation and a notice of the query, whose warning_entities are their lines. The application draws them as in conflict. The equation of line_distance stays as it is.
  • Arcs keep their side. A change of driving values (a dimension, a parameter, a configuration’s value) is solved in steps (the solver’s continuation); a step after which an arc lies on the other side of its chord (the sine of its sweep changed sign, each clearly away from a half circle) is taken again in halves, up to 8 times (System::arc_sides). Linked projections that moved are solved in steps the same way (project::solve_followed, up to 6 halvings), and one solve after which an arc changed its side is taken again in 4 steps. A fillet’s arc keeps its sweep and its side when its dimensions are scaled by 1.5 and back.
