Folders and designs

A project’s folders and designs for the Projects panel (mitcad#144; core/vcs/src/projects/listing.rs and operations.rs). They are commands of a project (Project::command; command_with with a SyncControl when the core pushes). Paths are relative to the project’s folder with / (an absolute path inside it also does). A name starting with a dot is hidden (the listing and the commit’s walk leave out every dot-folder), a link on the way is not followed, and names some system cannot hold (<>:"|?*\, a dot or space at the end, CON, NUL, COM1 and the like) are refused, so a project opens everywhere.

Command Fields Result
project_tree session (optional: the application’s lock session), author, fallback_author (optional: who same_owner compares with) below; no network and no writes
create_folder path the folder (and those above it) with an empty placeholder, .gitkeep (git records files, not folders; never listed), recorded as Add folder <path>
new_design path (ends with .mitcad), text (optional: the design; default an empty design, mitcad_model::file::empty_design()), units (optional, not with text: the empty design’s length unit, mm when left out; New designs in other units) the design (folders above it made), recorded as Add <path>
move from, to a design (to a design’s name) or a folder with everything in it, recorded as one version, Move <from> to <to>; folders above to made
delete path, force (default false) a design or a folder with everything in it, deleted from the folder and recorded as Delete <path>; the history keeps what its versions hold (restoring deleted designs is a later ticket)

The writes also take author, fallback_author (as commit), message (instead of the default one), session (whose locks are the caller’s) and push. Each follows Save’s rules: one version of only its paths (the index locked, other staged changes kept), refused with nothing changed while HEAD is detached or a merge is in progress. In a Cloud project the version is pushed at once when push is true (default: the project’s sync.send_at_once, else true); the application passes false and pushes as after a Save. Their answer is commit’s ({commit, skipped, written, removed, deleted (B-rep files deleted), warnings}) with push (push’s answer, or null), error and log, and:

  • create_folder, new_design: path;
  • move: from, to, moved ([{from, to}]: every design that moved, so open designs follow), display_moved (how many per-user display states followed: .mitcad/local/display/, as follow_rename); the design opened last (.mitcad/local/recent.json) follows too; links_updated lists designs whose component source paths changed;
  • delete: path, deleted_designs (the designs deleted).

A move records the old paths and the new ones in one version: the moved designs keep their history (it follows the rename, as history does) and the B-rep files they refer to stay in the store. Files under a moved folder that no version holds move along and stay unrecorded; designs that no version holds are recorded at their new path. A move or a delete that would leave the source’s folder with nothing recorded adds that folder’s placeholder, so folders never vanish from the versions.

Moves also retarget ordinary component links in visible working designs, including unversioned designs, and record those edits in the same version. Relative links keep their meaning when the owner moves, including links to sources outside the project; library links keep their library identity. Unreadable designs or folders prevent the move rather than leaving an unknown set of links broken. Link edits and the move are rolled back if the version cannot be recorded.

Callers with open documents pass open_designs and modified_designs (arrays of absolute filenames). Unsaved project designs must first be saved so the scan sees their current links. A design whose links must change must be closed first, including another window’s edit-locked design, and can be reopened after the move. This prevents its undo states or a later save from restoring an old source path. The Projects panel supplies every window’s state and reports these refusals without moving files.

Refusals change nothing and answer error ({class, message, detail}, commit null; in text an error, mitcad-cli exits with 1):

  • exists: the new folder or design, or the move’s target, is there (also as another case of the same name on a system that does not tell them apart);
  • invalid_path: outside the project, hidden, a link on the way, a name not every system can hold, a design’s new name without .mitcad, a file that is not a design, a folder moved into itself;
  • not_found: nothing to move, or nothing to delete in the folder or the latest version;
  • locked: a design in it is locked by someone else (the project’s edit locks on; a lock of another session than session and another person than the author, as the last lock poll saw it; the message names them);
  • local_changes: a delete of files the latest version lacks or holds otherwise, which deleting would lose, unless force;
  • unsupported: HEAD detached or a merge in progress.

A failed push after a recorded version is error too (its class, the message starting The version is recorded but was not sent), with commit set. A command without its fields is a failed command.

project_tree answers root, name (the folder’s), display_name (the display name on this computer, project_settings’ local.name, or null), kind (local, cloud), branch, head, remote (as in inspect_folder), remotes, ahead and behind (by the remote-tracking reference of the last fetch or push, null without), edit_locks (the project’s edit locks on), folders (relative paths, sorted, every folder but dot-folders, empty ones too), designs ([{path, modified (RFC 3339, UTC), recorded (in the latest version), changed (not recorded, or differs from it), version ({number (as history counts the design’s versions, through renames), id, short_id, time, date (RFC 3339, UTC), author ({name, email}, cleaned)} of its latest version, null when not recorded), lock ({owner ({name, email}), session, state (active, idle), taken_at, active_at, mine (the lock’s session is session), same_owner (the owner is the author)} or null)}], sorted by path, at most 1000), truncated (more designs, or more than 50 000 entries), history_truncated (more than 10 000 versions on HEAD’s history: the numbers count the newest 10 000), error (null). The locks are the local copies the last lock poll left (refs/mitcad/remote-locks/), read with the lock reader’s limits.

mitcad-cli project tree <folder>, project mkdir <folder> <path>, project new-design <folder> <path>, project move <folder> <from> <to> and project delete <folder> <path> [--force], the writes with [--author A] [--message M] [--no-push], each with --json (tools/cli/projects.cpp).

Tests: core/vcs/src/tests/folders.rs (nested folders and new designs, versions and changes in the tree, the dot-folder rule, a moved folder whose designs refer to B-rep files, a rename keeping the display state and the design opened last, deleted designs and folders in the history, every refusal changing nothing, a detached HEAD, a Cloud project’s push and a refused push, designs locked by someone else) and ctest cli.project_folders.

Edit locks

Advisory edit locks of the designs of Cloud projects (mitcad#89), kept on the remote as refs outside the branches: refs/mitcad/locks/<id>, a parentless commit whose tree holds lock.json (authored by the holder), and refs/mitcad/lock-requests/<id>/<session> with request.json, so a requester never races the holder; <id> is the SHA-256 (hex) of the file’s path in the project. MitCad honours them, other git tools do not see them (core/vcs/src/remote/locks.rs; the files and their checks in locks/format.rs; design in docs/architecture.md).

  • Writes are compare-and-swap pushes, git push --porcelain --no-verify --no-signed --no-recurse-submodules --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected> <remote> <commit>:<ref> (<expected> empty: the ref must not exist); a release is a deletion with the same lease. A ref the remote rejects is listed again: changed means someone else wrote it first (changed), unchanged means the remote refuses lock refs (error class unsupported, “This remote does not accept MitCad’s lock references”).
  • Reading: one git ls-remote <remote> refs/mitcad/locks/* refs/mitcad/lock-requests/* refs/heads/<branch> per command; only when a ref points to an object the project lacks, git fetch --prune <remote> +refs/mitcad/locks/*:refs/mitcad/remote-locks/locks/* +refs/mitcad/lock-requests/*:refs/mitcad/remote-locks/lock-requests/*. fetch, push, sync and clones name only branches, so they never fetch or push lock refs, and lock commits are in no version’s history.
  • Untrusted contents: a lock or request commit is read only when it is at most 64 KiB, without parents, with a tree of at most 4 KiB and its file a blob of at most 16 KiB; then format (mitcad-lock, mitcad-lock-request) and version (1; another version is listed as unreadable, not guessed at), ids and commit ids as hex of the right length, sessions as lowercase UUIDs, times as RFC 3339 from 2000 to 2200, paths relative without .. and matching the ref’s id, names at most 100 characters, messages at most 200, texts cleaned (control, bidirectional and other invisible characters removed, whitespace collapsed; shown as plain text only), idle_minutes clamped to 1–120 and poll_seconds to 5–600. A malformed ref is listed (readable false, problem) and counted once (dropped), never an error; a lock that cannot be read holds its file until it is stale by the project’s settings.
  • Stale locks are judged on this process’s monotonic clock, never by comparing another computer’s clock (the times in locks are only shown): unchanged, the ref seen unchanged for idle_minutes × 60 + 2 × poll_seconds; no_receipt, this session’s request missing from the holder’s requests_seen 2 × poll_seconds after it was asked (or the holder took the lock; the project’s poll interval when both listen to the broker); unanswered, a receipt without an answer for the idle time and two polls (after a keep, from the end of the keep). What each listing saw is kept per project folder in the process and shared by every Project of it (the application opens one per task). MITCAD_LOCK_TIME_SCALE (a factor) speeds this clock up for the application’s tests.
  • Requests go stale as locks do (mitcad#89), so that a requester whose MitCad was killed is not asked about for ever: while a request waits (no answer, or a keep; not declined, not granted), the requester’s lock_poll writes it again every half the project’s idle time, as a refresh of itself (refresh_of its id, refreshed_at, and the requester’s poll_seconds: one compare-and-swap push, the request’s id, place in the order, receipt and answer kept). Another session’s request whose ref this process has seen unchanged for the project’s idle time and two of the requester’s polls (poll_seconds of the request, else the project’s) is stale: it gets no receipt (requests_seen), a hand-over without to passes it by, it is listed with stale unchanged, and the next lock_poll of any session removes it with a compare-and-swap deletion (a refresh in between keeps it). A declined request is not refreshed, so it goes the same way. A session never judges its own requests.

lock.json ("format": "mitcad-lock", "version": 1): path, owner ({name, email}), session, application_version, taken_at, refreshed_at, active_at (RFC 3339, UTC), idle_minutes, poll_seconds, mqtt, base (the commit of the version the holder edits), state (active, idle), idle_since, requests_seen (request ids: the receipts), answers ({request id: {answer: declined | keep, until, message}}), handed_over_from and taken_from ({name, email, session}, taken_from with reason: unchanged, no_receipt, unanswered or take_over). A lock MitCad writes always fits in 16 KiB (the oldest answers and request ids are left out). request.json ("format": "mitcad-lock-request", "version": 1): path, requester, session, asked_at, message, and since mitcad#89’s stale requests poll_seconds (the requester’s git poll interval, clamped to 5–600) and, in a refresh, refresh_of (the request’s id) and refreshed_at (shown only); a reader takes a request without them as before. A request’s id is the commit it was first written as (a refresh names it), so asking again is a new request.

The commands are Project commands, run with command_with (their git runs show progress and stop on a cancel); each answers error and log as the remote commands do, a failure of git or the network being an answer. Common fields: path (a design, absolute or relative to the current folder), session (the application’s UUID for this run; without it the command line’s session, a UUID made from the author’s email, the same in every run), author and fallback_author (the holder or requester, as for versions), mqtt (this session listens to the project’s broker).

Command Fields Result
lock_poll session, receipts (default true), mqtt, poll_seconds (this session’s poll interval, written into its requests’ refreshes; default the request’s), tidy (default true) one listing; with tidy this session’s waiting requests refreshed when due and other sessions’ stale requests removed (one push); receipts written for the requests to this session’s locks; the view below, and receipts (the paths whose locks got them), lost ([{id, path, lock (as it is now, or null)}]: locks this session held in this process that are not its own any more: taken, or removed), refreshed_requests (the paths of this session’s requests refreshed) and removed_requests ([{id, file_id, session, path, requester}]: stale requests removed)
lock_status path (optional), session, network (default true; false: what the last listing saw, no git), mqtt the view (of one file with path, and path, file_id, lock or null). Nothing is written
lock_take path, session, author, idle_minutes and poll_seconds (default the project’s), mqtt, base (default HEAD), take_over (a lock’s commit, as shown when the user confirmed) outcome: taken (free, stale, or take_over still names it: another session of the same person, or a holder whose application went offline), refreshed (this session’s already, one handed over to it too: written with these values, this session’s request withdrawn), held (another session’s; nothing written), changed (someone wrote it between the listing and the push); path, file_id, session, lock (as it is now), taken_from, and with taken previous (the lock as it was, for “Alex’s edit lock had expired (last active 14:02)”; null when it was free)
lock_refresh path, session, active_at (RFC 3339, or now), state (active, idle: idle_since follows), idle_minutes, poll_seconds, mqtt, base outcome refreshed (with the receipts of the requests seen that are not stale; answers of requests that are gone dropped) or lost; lock
lock_release path, or all true; session; force outcome (released, not_held, free, changed), released and withdrawn (paths of the locks and requests removed), changed, lock. With force any lock of the file and the file’s requests; all: this session’s locks and requests, with force every lock and request ref of the project
lock_hand_over path, session, to (a requester’s session; default the first request served that is not declined; never a stale one), base (default HEAD) outcome: handed_over (one compare-and-swap writes the requester as the owner, handed_over_from this session, so nobody else can take it in between), no_request, lost, free, changed; to ({name, email, session}), lock
lock_request path, session, author, message (at most 200 characters), mqtt, poll_seconds (the requester’s poll interval; default the project’s) outcome: requested, free (nothing written: take it), mine, changed; request (its id), my_request, receipt_due_seconds
lock_withdraw path, session outcome withdrawn or none (the requester’s window closed, or it got the lock)
lock_answer path, session, request (its id), answer (declined, keep), minutes (keep: 1–120, default 15), message outcome answered (written into the lock with until for a keep), no_request, lost; lock
lock_probe session remote, accepted, message (“This remote does not accept MitCad’s lock references” or null), reason, left (a probe ref the remote did not let go): refs/mitcad/locks/probe-<hex> created, listed and deleted

The view: remote, session, polled, head (the remote branch’s commit, from the same listing), tracking (the remote-tracking reference’s), newer (the two differ: newer versions to fetch), locks, requests_without_lock, my_requests (this session’s requests), dropped (malformed lock and request refs seen by this process), settings (the project’s enabled, idle_minutes, poll_seconds).

  • A lock: id, commit, readable, problem, the fields of lock.json (null when it cannot be read; owner {name, email}), mine, same_owner (another session of the same email: “You have this design open elsewhere”), unchanged_seconds, stale (null, unchanged, no_receipt, unanswered; never for this session’s), stale_in_seconds (until it is, by the earliest rule), requests (in the order they are served: the order this process first saw them) and my_request.
  • A request: id, commit (its ref’s commit: the id, or the latest refresh), file_id, path, session, requester, asked_at, refreshed_at, message, mine, order, waiting_seconds (since this process first saw it), unchanged_seconds (since its ref last changed), stale (null, or unchanged for another session’s request not refreshed in time), stale_in_seconds, seen (the holder’s receipt), answer ({answer, until, message} or null), readable, problem.
  • my_request: id, commit, file_id, path, state (waiting for the receipt, seen, kept, declined, granted: the lock was handed over, free: there is no lock), answer, stale, stale_in_seconds, tracked (asked in this process).

The application’s lock controller polls every poll_seconds (2 minutes while live updates are connected) with lock_poll (with its poll_seconds, so a request it waits on stays alive), takes a design’s lock when it opens (lock_take; held opens it read-only), refreshes it every half idle time and when its state changes (lock_refresh), answers requests (lock_answer, or lock_hand_over after saving and syncing), releases at idle time or on closing (lock_release) and turns a window read-only when a lock is lost; turning locking off or Cloud → Local releases this session’s locks and requests (lock_release with all). sync_plan takes session and locks (last: the last listing, no git) and answers locked ([{path, lock}]: the files its push would send whose lock another session holds, for “Send Anyway”; empty when locks are off or nothing is sent) and locked_error (null, or why the locks could not be read: locked is then null).

mitcad-cli lock status <project-or-file>, lock take <file>, lock release <project-or-file> [--force], each with --author and --json (a lock someone else holds is the exit status 1). Tests: core/vcs/src/tests/locks.rs (two clones of a bare repository and a file:// remote: two takers at once, refresh, release, hand-over, requests, receipts and answers, each stale rule on an injected clock, a killed requester’s request going stale and removed, a waiting request refreshed with its id, receipt and answer kept, a hand-over passing declined requests by, a takeover that fails because the holder refreshed, take-over from another session, release with force and all, Sync and fetch never carrying lock refs, sync_plan’s locked, a remote whose hook refuses them, malformed and oversized refs, the readers’ checks and a seeded random run of mutated files; git fsck clean), ctest cli.remote, and the fuzz targets in core/vcs/fuzz (by hand: cargo +nightly fuzz run lock_json, request_json).

Live updates

The optional MQTT client of Cloud projects (mitcad#89), all in Rust (core/vcs/src/remote/mqtt.rs and mqtt/; design in docs/architecture.md): the socket, TLS (rustls with ring, the broker’s certificate checked by rustls-webpki against the system’s root certificates), MQTT 3.1.1 and the checking of everything received. It is only an accelerator: a message makes the application poll git at once, and only the lock refs grant a lock. One connection per broker, user and prefix is shared by the open projects on it; each project subscribes to <prefix>/<project>/#, the project id being the repository’s first commit.

The bridge has a LiveHub (new_live_hub()) with command(json) (an error only for a command that is wrong; what happens on the network comes as events) and events(timeout_ms), a blocking read of the checked events run on a worker thread. Both may run at once on two threads. The application never sees MQTT’s bytes.

Topics and payloads

Topic Payload (format)
<prefix>/<project>/locks/<file> mitcad-live-lock retained; empty when the lock is released
<prefix>/<project>/requests/<file> mitcad-live-request QoS 1, not retained: requests, receipts, answers, withdrawals
<prefix>/<project>/versions mitcad-live-version QoS 1, not retained: a branch and commit after a push
<prefix>/<project>/open/<file>/<session> mitcad-live-open retained; empty when the window closes
<prefix>/sessions/<session> mitcad-live-session retained online after each connect; the connection’s will offline; empty after a clean disconnect

<file> is the SHA-256 (hex) of the file’s path in the project (/ between folders), <session> the application’s session (a UUID in lowercase). A session’s presence is not under a project, since one connection has one will and serves every project on the broker (which is also why the connection is per prefix). Payloads are JSON with format and version (1); a reader takes only the topic’s format and version 1 and ignores fields it does not know. No email address is sent (the broker may be more public than the repository).

Format Fields
mitcad-live-lock path, owner ({name}), session (the holder’s), state (active, idle), taken_at, active_at, idle_since, idle_minutes, poll_seconds, commit (of the lock ref)
mitcad-live-request kind (request, receipt, answer, withdrawn), session (the sender’s), name, at, for (the requester’s session; receipts and answers), answer (released, keep, declined), until, message
mitcad-live-version branch, commit, session, name, at
mitcad-live-open name, mode (editing, read-only), since
mitcad-live-session state (online, offline), since

Everything received is checked (mitcad#89, “Untrusted input”): a packet’s remaining length at most 64 KiB, read only after that check (larger: the connection ends, class protocol); more than 200 messages in a second end the connection (flood), which connects again after the back-off (the retained copies a broker sends at once after a subscribe count apart, up to 2000 a second, so that a project with many designs open can subscribe); topics only under the connection’s prefix, of the forms above, of a subscribed project or a followed session; no retained copies of requests and versions; payloads at most 16 KiB of UTF-8 JSON of the right format and version; ids as lowercase hex of their length, sessions as UUIDs, times RFC 3339 between 2020 and 2100 (given back in UTC), paths relative without .., a lock summary’s path the one its topic’s id is of, branch names as git allows them (stricter), idle_minutes and poll_seconds clamped to the project settings’ bounds, names 1 to 100 characters and messages at most 200 after cleaning (control characters, bidirectional overrides and other invisible format characters removed, whitespace collapsed); at most 64 retained messages per file and 10 000 per project. A message that fails is dropped and counted, never an error.

Commands

Command Fields Answer
connect broker (mqtts://host[:port], port 8883, or mqtt://host[:port], 1883: plain text), prefix (default mitcad; letters, digits, -, _, /), session (the application’s; one per hub), user, password (only with mqtts:// and a user: else the class insecure, before anything is sent), ca (a PEM file of certificate authorities trusted besides the system’s) connection (c1), broker, prefix, user, tls, state, warning (for mqtt://: the messages are plain text). Opens the connection of the broker, user and prefix, or gives the open one; with a new password, or when it is offline or failed, it connects again at once (with these password and ca)
subscribe connection, or the fields of connect; project (the first commit id, 40 or 64 hex) connection, project, topic, state; a subscribed event follows
unsubscribe connection, project subscribed (it was), closed: the project’s open entries of this session are cleared first; the connection’s last project closes the connection
watch connection, session follows a session’s presence (session events); sessions named in a project’s messages are followed without it, at most 512 per connection
publish connection, project (subscribed on it), message (below) topic, qos, retain, connected; the message as others will read it (checked, cleaned, times in UTC, numbers clamped), sent at once or after the reconnect
disconnect connection (none: all), wait_ms (at most 10 000, default 0) closed (the ids), finished (all disconnected within wait_ms): this session’s open entries and presence cleared, DISCONNECT (no will), in the connection’s thread
status session, closed, connections ([{connection, broker, prefix, user, projects, state, error, retry_in_ms, connected_since, tls, connects, received, dropped, dropped_reasons ({reason: count}), inflight, queued, watched_sessions}]): the lock details’ MQTT state
test the fields of connect but session; timeout_ms (per step, default 10 000), text ok, broker, prefix, user, tls, topic, steps ([{step: connect, sign_in, subscribe, publish, receive; ok, ms}], up to the one that failed), error, warning; with text the same as text for people. Project Settings’ Test: a connection of its own subscribes to <prefix>/test/<random>, publishes once and waits for the message. Blocks: run it on a worker thread
close wait_ms as disconnect of all (quitting: wait_ms lets the others see a clean leave rather than the will); then events answers at once with closed (the reading thread ends) and connect fails (closed)

The messages of publish (type and its fields):

type Fields Sent
lock path, lock: {owner ({name}; lock.json’s owner may be given, its email is not sent), session (default this session), state (default active), taken_at, active_at (default now), idle_since, idle_minutes, poll_seconds (default the settings’ defaults), commit}, or null: released retained, QoS 1
request path, name, message (optional) QoS 1
receipt path, name, for QoS 1
answer path, name, for, answer, until (with keep), message QoS 1
withdrawn path QoS 1
version branch, commit, name QoS 1
open path, name, mode, since (default now) retained, QoS 1
closed path the open entry cleared

The session keeps its own retained state (its locks’ summaries and its open entries) and publishes it again after each reconnect, as the broker had it last; a lock summary of another session (a hand-over) is published once, and another session’s summary received for one of this session’s locks (a takeover) ends that. QoS 1 messages without a PUBACK are sent again after 20 s and after a reconnect; while offline up to 256 wait.

Events

events(timeout_ms) answers {"events": [...], "lost": n, "closed": bool}: at most 1000 events a read, lost those pushed out by the limit of 10 000 waiting. Every event has type and connection; those of a project project, retained (the broker’s retained copy, after a subscribe) and own (sent by this session).

type Fields
state broker, prefix, state: connecting, connected, offline (connects again in retry_in_ms: 1 s doubling up to 5 min, ±20 %), failed (not again until a new connect: auth_failed, certificate, refused, invalid), closed; error ({class, message} or null)
subscribed project, error (the broker refused): after each SUBACK, also after a reconnect: what was known of the project’s retained topics is to be forgotten, their retained copies follow
lock file, lock (the summary, checked) or null (released)
request file, kind, session, name, at, for, answer, until, message (fields not sent are absent)
version branch, commit, session, name, at
open file, session, entry ({name, mode, since} or null: closed), cleared (true: cleared on the broker by this session because that session went offline; given once the broker acknowledged it)
session session, state (online; offline: its connection was lost, the will; left: it disconnected cleanly), since
dropped reason, topic (cleaned, at most 200 characters), count (the connection’s total; one event stands for a run of drops)

Error classes: invalid (a wrong command or field), insecure (a password without TLS), network, timed_out, certificate (not trusted, another host name, expired; or no root certificates on the computer), tls, auth_failed (the user name or password refused, not authorised; in test also a topic the broker does not let the user read or write), refused, protocol (the broker broke MQTT’s rules or sent a packet over 64 KiB), flood, closed, internal.

When a session goes offline (its will), the sessions that follow it clear its open entries on the broker (they become open events with cleared once the broker has acknowledged the clearing, so that a session subscribing after that event does not get them); its lock summaries stay, as its lock refs do. Another session’s open entry is given only while that session is known to be online: the retained copies after a subscribe come before the session’s presence, so an entry waits until its presence says online (then it is given), offline (then it is never given and is cleared on the broker, as above, without an event) or nothing yet (a session that left, or whose presence has not come: it waits). A closing is given only for an entry that was given. When the broker refuses the subscription to a session’s presence, or the limit of followed sessions is reached, its entries are given as they come.

mitcad-cli live test <broker> [--prefix P] [--user U] [--ca FILE] [--timeout S] [--json] runs test, the password from MITCAD_MQTT_PASSWORD. The project’s id

Command Fields Answer
project_id (a Project command) project: the first commit of HEAD’s first-parent chain (hex), the same in every clone; null before the first version

The application subscribes a Cloud project under it (app/files/LiveController.cpp, app/COMMANDS.md). Test: core/vcs/src/tests.rs (the_project_id_is_the_first_commit_of_the_history).

Component libraries

Component libraries and the community library (mitcad#64, mitcad#63) are git repositories of MitCad designs with a manifest; their format is in docs/libraries.md. The model knows no git: it reads a library’s component at a version through a LinkResolver (core/model/src/library.rs), which mitcad-vcs implements over the cache of fetched libraries (core/vcs/src/library/). The bridge’s configure_libraries(json) sets the cache ({"root"}, default MITCAD_LIBRARIES_DIR, else the user’s data folder) and installs the resolver for every document; Rust code can give a document its own (Document::set_link_resolver).

Configuration tables

A design’s table of sizes and options (configurations in the design file, left out when empty) is described in Configurations (mitcad#797): its options, open and closed tables, rows, rules, the cascade, the configure command and query and check_rules. A library’s design is inserted in one of its rows (config below). A design written before mitcad#798, whose table has selectors, opens as a closed table whose options are text parameters made from the selectors.

Library parts

insert_component with library instead of path inserts a library’s component: {"id": "<library id>", "url": "<where it was fetched from>", "rev": "<commit or tag>", "component": "<component id>", "config": "<row>"} (config left out: the table’s default), with link, transform and name as for files. The design is read at that version, the row applied to a copy of its parameters, and:

  • linked (default): its visible bodies in a base feature of a new, read-only component (one body is named after the designation), its link path the design’s path in the library;
  • a copy ("link": false): the design with its history in the row (the table is not copied), editable.

Either way the component records library (in the design file too): library (id), url, rev (the commit, also for a tag), label (the commit’s tag), component, path, config, license, authors, designation (ISO 4762 M5x16) and, for a part not for print services, "non_printable": true (Print service check). The component is named after the designation unless name is given; the undo step is Insert <name>.

  • Versions stay. update_links (when a design opens) reads every linked library part at its recorded commit and takes new bodies only when that design or row differs from what was saved; a library or version that is not on this computer keeps the saved bodies with a message (... library mitcad-fasteners v1.0.0 (3f9a2c1) (url) cannot be read (...); it keeps the bodies saved with the design). Nothing follows a library’s newest version on its own.
  • Materials come along. The part’s bodies are made of the materials its design gives them and show its appearances, linked or a copy (Materials of inserted components).
  • Updates are explicit. update_library_parts with changes: [{component (uid or name), rev (another version), config (another row)}] changes linked parts as one undo step (Update <name> to v1.1.0, M5x20 or Update Library Components) and returns changes (ISO 4762 M5x16: version v1.0.0 (3f9a2c1) -> v1.1.0 (7d0e5b2), ... size M5x16 -> M6x20). A part named after its designation, and its body, take the new designation. A copied part is refused (it does not follow its library).
  • The comparison of versions (diff) shows a part’s changes field by field (library.rev, library.config, …) and a table’s changes row by row (configuration M5x16: dk 8.5 mm -> 8.7 mm).
Query Result
library_parts parts: component, name, linked, occurrences, library (as recorded), version (v1.0.0 (3f9a2c1))
parts_list rows, one per component other than the root in the order they were made: component, name, designation (a library part’s, else the name), quantity (how many times the design places it, through every occurrence of the components it is in), linked, library, version, config, license, authors, url (with properties, a list of keys Key or Set/Key: each row’s properties, the text of each key’s value or null; Properties)

Materials of inserted components (mitcad#1921)

A component inserted with insert_component, from a library (library) or a file (path), linked or as a copy, has the materials and appearances its source design gives its bodies, so that its masses, parts list and looks are those of the source:

  • What a body is made of is what the source design makes it of: the body’s own material there, else the default material of the nearest component up its path in the source, else the source’s root’s. Its appearance is the body’s own there, else the appearance of the component whose default material it takes; without either it shows its material’s look.
  • Built-in materials and library appearances are taken by their ids. A material of the source design’s own (made there, or brought from a material library, with its reference) is copied into the design once and found again for every further body and insert: the same material by its id, else one of the same density and name (a numbered copy’s name, Oak (2), counts) or of the same material library reference, the design’s own or a built-in, as a BUILD part’s library material is (mitcad#1817, core/model/src/build/library_material.rs). A copy brought in gets a free id and name (oak_2, Oak (2)) when the design has another material of that id or name. The source’s own appearances come the same way (their images from where the source keeps them: a library’s embedded, a file’s by their absolute path); one whose image cannot be read is left out, and the body shows its material’s look.
  • Linked: each body of the base feature takes its source’s material and appearance as its own (material, appearance in the bodies query), and its entry of the base feature’s bodies records them. When the link is read again (update_links, update_link, update_library_parts with another version or row), a body whose material is still the one its source gave takes the source’s new one; a material set on the inserted body by hand (set_body_material) or by a material binding (set_body_material with expression) stays. Appearances follow the same rule. A link shown by its envelope keeps its bodies’ materials as they are.
  • A copy ("link": false) brings the materials and appearances with its bodies and components as every copy of a design does: a body’s own material stays the body’s, a component’s default its copy’s (the source’s root’s default the new component’s).
  • No material in the source: a body whose source design names no material for it gets none of its own. It is made of the design’s default material, named as the body’s component’s or the root’s (set_component_material), and of no material where the design names none: no density and no mass, never a silent steel (mitcad#1817).
  • Linked with options (parameters, Options of inserted components, mitcad#1923): the derived part’s bodies take what the source design, in the part’s row and values, gives them, by the same rules: when it is inserted, when its source is read again (update_library_parts with another version or row, update_links and update_link for a linked file that changed) and when set_component_parameters changes its row. To know which bodies the source shows, its design is evaluated once more then, unless it gives no body a material or an appearance. What it gave each body is recorded on the component’s link (given); a body whose material or appearance was set by hand, or by a binding, keeps it. Changed values of its options alone do not read the materials again. A copy has the design’s own parameters and takes no options ("link": false with parameters is refused); it brings its materials as every copy does.
  • Designs saved before (mitcad#1923): a link whose bodies did not take their materials (a link without looks in the design file) is read again on the design’s next update_links (and update_link) even when its source is unchanged, once: its bodies take the source’s materials and appearances (a design linked with options from the source the design keeps), a material set on a body by hand stays, and the line <component> takes the materials of <file> says so. A source that cannot be read, or whose materials cannot be taken, leaves the bodies as they are with a line saying why, and is tried again at the next update. A link shown by its envelope is not read for this.

Library commands

Commands of the cache of libraries, not of a document: the bridge’s library_command(json, control) (a fetch reports its progress to the SyncControl and stops when it is cancelled) and describe_library (the answer as text); mitcad-cli library. A fetch’s failure is an answer with error (class, message, detail, as the remote commands’) and log; other failures are errors.

Removed sources and one clone per repository

mitcad#1436 (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#172): the forms of one repository’s URL have one key (repository_key, core/vcs/src/library/sources.rs: without user information, the scheme of a network address (https://, http://, ssh://, user@host:path) or file://, a host’s leading www., trailing slashes and .git; / for a backslash; in lower case), so https://www.github.com/mitcad/parts.git and https://github.com/mitcad/parts.git are one repository.

Command Fields Result
library_remove url (a source removed from the application’s list), sources (the sources still listed, any form), removed (default true; false when the source is added again) url, repository (its key), removed, changed (the clones’ folders whose mark changed). Marks the clones of that repository (mitcad-source-removed in the clone), in every folder of the cache, unless one of sources names the repository; with removed: false takes the mark off
  • library_search and library_build_candidates read one clone per repository and leave marked clones out; their answers have clones: read (dir, url) and left_out (dir, url, reason: its source was removed or same repository as <url>, text). Of two clones of one repository (an older MitCad cloned each form of the URL apart) they read the one whose URL is one of the command’s sources as written, else the one with the newer newest version, else the first.
  • library_fetch of another form of a repository already cloned updates that clone (dir is its folder; the log says so), and a fetch takes a clone’s mark off.
  • library_list gives each clone’s removed; library_show, library_preview, library_diff, library_configure and the resolver read marked clones too, so designs keep their parts. library_show’s url finds a clone fetched under another form of it.

Standards and suppliers of library rows

A library’s manifest may name each configuration row’s standards and the suppliers’ articles of it (mitcad#949; the format is in docs/libraries.md): the component’s rows ({"M6x8": {"standards": ["DIN 912"], "supplier_parts": [{"supplier", "part_number", "material", "finish", "checked"}]}}) and the library’s suppliers ([{"id", "name", "url"}]). A library without them answers as before.

  • library_show: each row of a component’s configurations.rows has its standards and supplier_parts (each with supplier_name, the supplier’s name from suppliers) when the manifest gives them; a component has standards (the standards its rows name, those of its standard first in that order, non-standard last) and suppliers ([{"id", "name", "url"}] with articles on its rows). The manifest has suppliers and replaces.
  • library_configure takes standard (the Standard filter’s: DIN 912): the designation of a row that names it is DIN 912 M6x10; without it, or for a row without that standard, the row’s first; a row tagged non-standard is M6x6 (non-standard). The answer adds rows (each row’s name, select, standards, supplier_parts), standard (the standard the combination’s row is named by, or null) and supplier_parts (that row’s).
  • library_search: a component’s standards and suppliers as above; supplier also finds a component whose rows a supplier sells (its id or name), part_number a supplier’s article number. With sources (the enabled sources’ URLs), a library an index offers, or a fetched clone of one, is left out when an enabled source has its repository under another id (the same URL, or the source’s clone has its newest commit or a version the index reviewed) or when a fetched library’s replaces names its id; left_out lists them (id, url, reason, text: mitcad-fasteners left out: same repository as https://github.com/mitcad/parts.git). Without sources every fetched library counts as a source.
  • library_check refuses an article whose supplier is not one of the library’s suppliers, a checked that is no date (YYYY-MM-DD), an article without a part number, a supplier without an id or a name, and a row name the design’s table lacks.
  • insert_component takes the library’s standard ({"id", "url", "rev", "component", "config", "standard": "DIN 912"}): the part is named by it when its row has it. The component’s library records standard (the standard it is named by) and supplier_parts (its row’s articles, with the suppliers’ names); update_library_parts keeps the standard where the new row has it.
  • parts_list: each row adds supplier_parts and supplier_parts_text (Würth 0084 6 8 (8.8 zinc-plated); …, the parts lists’ “Supplier part numbers” column).

A part with options (inserted with parameters) is named by its component’s standard as before.

Tests: core/vcs/src/tests/library_rows.rs (the manifest read and checked, library_show, library_configure with standard, library_search by supplier, the index’s library left out), core/model-tests/links/src/library_tests.rs (library_parts_follow_the_rows_standards_and_list_supplier_parts, library_parts_without_row_blocks_read_as_before) and core/model/src/library.rs (the designation).

Suppliers’ shops and product links

The libraries store their suppliers’ part numbers without addresses (mitcad#949). The product links are made from MitCad’s own list of the suppliers’ shops by region (mitcad#950, mitcad_model::supplier_shops; docs/libraries.md): per supplier id (the libraries’ suppliers[].id) how its canonical part number is written in its shops’ addresses (part_number: group_widths, each group but the last filled with spaces to that width, and the separator between the groups) and its shops, at most one per region (an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code), each with a product_url pattern whose {part_number} is the part number in that form, percent-encoded. Two library commands, which need no library:

Command Fields Result
supplier_shops locale (optional: the system’s, fi_FI, or a territory code), region and shops (optional: the region and the supplier ids chosen in Preferences) chosen (with region: those of shops that have a shop in it, in the list’s order: the Supplier filters’ default), regions ([{"id": "FI", "name": "Finland"}]: the regions some shop sells in, by name), suppliers ([{"id", "name", "url", "part_number": {"group_widths", "separator"}, "shops": [{"region", "name", "url", "product_url"}]}]), default_region (the locale’s territory when a shop sells there, else empty)
supplier_links region, and parts (articles as supplier_parts has them) or rows (rows with supplier_parts, as parts_list gives them) or both region; parts as given, each article with a link in the region adding product_url (https://eshop.wurth.fi/product/00846%20%208.sku/fi/FI/EUR/ for Würth 0084 6 8) and shop (the shop’s name); rows as given, their supplier_parts likewise and each row’s product_urls (its articles’ links, each once)

An article has no link without a region, for a supplier the list lacks or one without a shop in the region, and when its own region (an article’s field, only where a supplier’s part numbers differ by country) is another; library_check refuses an article’s region that is no region code. Nothing is stored: a design keeps the part numbers only.

Configurations: options, rows and rules

A configurable design stands for a family of products (mitcad#797; the design note is docs/configurations.md). The user picks a value for each option (Color, Length, Size), rules remove the values and combinations that are not allowed, and named rows are presets of option values. A configuration only ever sets parameters. The model is core/model-base/src/configurations.rs (the table, the rules and the cascade, without a kernel) and core/model/src/document/configurations.rs (the commands); the api is core/model-api/src/configurations.rs.

The table

configurations in the design file and in set_configurations:

Field
options names of user parameters, in choice order: the order in which the cascade repairs them and the choosers show them
closed default false. An open table allows every combination the rules allow; a closed table allows only its rows’ combinations
parameters other parameters the rows set (a closed table only, as tables did before mitcad#798)
default a row’s name; the first row when left out
rows presets: name (unique; what apply_configuration, library.config, BUILD’s build.rows and derived_part.config name), values ({parameter: expression}: the options’ constants and a closed table’s parameters), and optional designation, part_number, supplier_url
rules see Rules (mitcad#799)
  • The UI’s words (mitcad#968, docs/ui-conventions.md “Configurations”): the JSON keeps its names, and the window, the Configuration bar and the user guide say Possible values for a domain, Allowed values for allowed, By formula for a driven option, row (configuration row) for a row and Only these rows for closed; a closed table’s restriction is named Only these rows in moves, refused and restricted_by.
  • Options. An option is a user parameter. Its expression is a constant ('Black', 1200 mm, 1); choosing a value writes that constant. An option whose expression is a formula is driven: it is shown as driven (By formula), it is never moved, and a rule it breaks refuses the change that made it so.
  • Domain. What an option can be before rules: a list (its parameter’s values limit, Allowed values), else a range (its min, max and step, Parameter limits), else free.
  • Rows. In an open table a row sets options only; an option a row leaves out keeps its value. In a closed table each row gives every option a value, and no two rows the same combination. A row’s option values are constants.
  • The row of a combination. The row whose option values the parameters have (all its values in a table without options) is the combination’s row; it gives the designation, the part number and the supplier URL. Any other combination of an open table takes the library’s designation pattern with the option values in braces (ISO 4762 M{Size}x{Length}: a text option’s text, a number option’s number in its unit without the unit, 16), as BUILD writes {L}. A closed table refuses a combination that is no row, and a command that chooses its options (configure, set_parameter of an option, the cascade) also sets the row’s other parameters, except those the command sets itself.
  • Problems (problems of the queries; set_configurations and opening a file refuse the table with the first): an option or parameter that does not exist, is not a user parameter, or is listed twice; a parameter that is both; an option of an open table among parameters of rows (an open table’s rows set options only); a row without a name, two rows with the same name, a value for a parameter not in the table, a row option value that is not a constant, a closed table’s row without a value for an option (A: no value for Size), two rows of a closed table with the same combination (B: another row has the same Size and Length), a value its parameter refuses (unit, cycle, syntax, a strict limit: A: d = 1 deg: …), a default that is no row, and the rules' problems (Rules).
  • Old tables. A table with selectors (before mitcad#798) opens as a closed table: each selector becomes a text parameter of its name (the next free name, Size2, when a parameter already has it, with a warning), each row’s select becomes its values of those options (as texts: "Size": "'M5'"), and the new options take the values of the row the parameters have (else of the default row). Row names, the default, parameters and their values stay. An old table without selectors (its rows chosen by name) is closed too: a table with parameters and no options is always read as closed. The file is written in the new form from then on; set_configurations reads the old form the same way (the new parameters and the table are one undo step).

Open options of a closed table

open (mitcad#1950; a list of option names, default empty): the options of a closed table that its rows do not restrict, such as a timber board’s or a steel tube’s length L beside the rows of its sizes in the parts library. Each is listed in options too; migrating an old table’s selectors puts them after the selectors’ options.

  • A row leaves an open option out (a value it gives is a starting value only); the rows’ combinations, the closed table’s restriction (Only these rows), a combination that is no row and the row of a combination count the other options only. An open option is chosen within its domain (its limits) and the rules, like an open table’s.
  • Problems: open in a table that is not closed (option L is open, but only a table with Only these rows (closed) has open options), a name that is no option (the open option L is not an option of the table) or listed twice.
  • library_show gives open, and its selectors and selector_values (for the pickers that choose by rows) leave the open options out; the pickers offer them beside the rows (app/COMMANDS.md, “Options of library components”). The component configure query gives open.

Allowed values

values is a parameter limit next to min, max and step (mitcad#798), on any parameter: a list of expressions in the parameter’s unit (["'Black'", "'White'"], ["300 mm", "500 mm", "800 mm"]; they may use other parameters, which then take part in the dependency order like the other limits).

  • A number whose result is not in the list snaps to the nearest listed value (the lower one of two as near), and limited is values (Length is limited to its allowed value 500 mm (its expression gives 520 mm)); a strict parameter refuses it instead (parameter Length: 520 mm is not one of its allowed values 300 mm, 500 mm, 800 mm). With min, max or step as well, the result is clamped and snapped first, then snapped to the list.
  • A text whose result is not in the list is always refused (parameter Color: 'Green' is not one of its allowed values 'Black', 'White'): a text has no nearest value. values is the only limit a text parameter can have.
  • add_parameter and set_parameter take values as a list of expression texts or numbers (in the parameter’s unit); null or [] removes it in set_parameter. The parameters query’s limits has values (as written, or null), values_value (evaluated: mm or rad for a number, the texts for a text) and values_text (["300 mm", …]). The design file stores values with the parameter; undo, copies and renames treat it as the other limits; the parameters CSV has a values column (the list as a JSON array of expression texts, ["300 mm","500 mm"]; empty for none).

Rules

rules of the table (mitcad#799): each rule has name (unique), enabled (default true), an optional comment, an optional when (a condition in the expression language, true when left out), then and an optional else (lists of actions).

"rules": [
 {"name": "Black is short", "when": "Color == 'Black'",
 "then": [{"option": "Length", "max": "1000 mm"}]},
 {"name": "Power needs tables", "when": "Tables == 0",
 "then": [{"option": "Power", "values": ["0"]}]},
 {"name": "No red XL", "when": "and(Color == 'Red'; Size == 'XL')",
 "then": [{"forbid": "Red is not made in XL"}]},
 {"name": "Deep enough", "then": [{"require": "Depth >= Length / 4",
 "message": "the shelf is too shallow for its length"}]}
]
  • Conditions (when, require) are expressions of the language of Values that give a number: zero is false, anything else true (==, <>, <, and, or, not, if, text comparison; a condition is read in parentheses, so a single = compares too: Color = 'Black'). They may use any parameter. A condition that does not evaluate is a problem of the table.
  • Actions:
    • {"option": "Length", "values": [...]} allows only these values, and {"option": "Color", "exclude": [...]} not these (expressions in the option’s unit; a text option’s are texts);
    • {"option": "Length", "min": "…", "max": "…", "step": "…"} restricts a number option’s range (any of the three; expressions in its unit; they may be given with values or exclude in one action);
    • {"require": "<condition>", "message": "…"} and {"forbid": "<message>"} reject the combination.
    • {"in_table": "Made", "columns": {"Color": "Color"}} requires the combination to be a row of a table: Configurations and tables (mitcad#806).
  • Rules only narrow. An option’s allowed values are its domain intersected with every active restriction (the actions of the then of each enabled rule whose when holds, and of the else of each whose when does not). Their order does not matter, and a rule never sets a computed parameter. When an intersection is empty, the problem names the rules (Black is short and Long only leave Length no value).
  • Rules do not take part in evaluation. They check the evaluated parameters and change only the constants of options. They add no dependency edges, so they cannot form a cycle: two rules may point in opposite directions (Color restricts Length, and Length restricts Color).
  • Renames and deletes. Renaming a parameter rewrites the rules' conditions and action expressions and option names; a parameter that a rule uses cannot be deleted (parameter Wall is used by the rule Thick walls), nor an option or a row’s parameter (configurations: option Color of the table does not exist, as before mitcad#799). The rules are checked first: an option that a rule uses is refused with the rule’s name. The parameters query gives each parameter option (true for an option of the table) and rules (the names of the rules that use it).

Rule problems: a rule without a name, two rules of one name, an action of no kind or of two (values with require), an option that is not an option of the table, a range action on a text option, a step that is not positive, an expression that does not parse or evaluate. An empty intersection depends on the values: it is a broken rule (the configure query’s problems, a refusal), not a problem of the table.

Where a rule problem is (mitcad#1064): the configurations query’s rule_problems gives each rule problem as index (the rule’s index in rules), rule (its name), place, level and message (the words of problems). place is when; an action of the then or else as then.0 or else.1 (an action of two kinds or of none, an action that names no option, an in_table problem); or the part of an action: then.0.option (no option of the table), then.0.values.2 and then.0.exclude.0 (a listed value, by its index), then.0.min, then.0.max, then.0.step, then.0.require. It is null for the rule itself (no name, a name another rule has). level is error for the problems above, and warning for a value outside its option’s domain, which is no problem of the table and refuses nothing: a value of values or exclude that is no value of the option (the rule Colors: values: Green is not one of the values of Color), a min above all of its values or a max below all of them. The rule editor marks the block at the place. With rules, the query checks rules that are not set yet, as set_configurations would (the editor asks it where a refused rule is wrong).

The cascade

After every change of parameters (set_parameter, apply_configuration, configure, the parameters CSV import, set_configurations, and so MCP and the CLI, which send those commands), the model goes through the options in order:

  1. An option keeps its value when it is allowed.
  2. Otherwise it moves: a number with a range to the nearest allowed value by the step rule of Parameter limits; a list to the nearest listed value (a number), else to the default row’s value when it is allowed, else to the first allowed value; a single allowed value is chosen by itself.
  3. An option the change itself set, an option before the first of those (only the later options move; all may when the change set no option), and a driven option, is never moved.

When every rule then holds, the change and the moves are one undo step, and the answer lists the moves: moves, a list of option, from and to (the values as text, 1500 mm, Black), from_expression, to_expression and rule (the rule that moved it), and text (Length 1500 mm → 1000 mm: Black is short). When a rule that held before the change is broken after it (a require, a forbid, a restriction of an option the change set or of a driven one, a closed table’s combination that is no row), the change is refused with the rule’s name and message (the rule Black is short: does not allow Length = 1500 mm, the rule No red XL: Red is not made in XL, Only these rows: Size M6 and Length 99 is no row), and nothing changes. A rule already broken before the change (a file opened so, a table just edited) does not refuse it: the configure query reports it.

set_parameter, apply_configuration and import_parameters_csv add moves to their answers (left out when empty for the first and the last). Rust: Document::configuration_moves() gives the moves of the last command.

For a list each value is tested through the cascade from it: it is allowed when the cascade from it, given the options before it, ends with no broken rule. A range is the intersection of the active min, max and step. A closed table’s allowed values are those of its rows that match the options before. Every chooser uses this query (the Configurations window, the active configuration bar, the part pickers, MCP); the final check of a whole combination is always exact.

Options of inserted components

A library part, a linked design and a BUILD part have options of their own (mitcad#801; docs/configurations.md, “Inserted components”, decisions 8 and 11): parameters, values of the source’s options (and other user parameters), each an expression of this design’s parameters. The model is core/model/src/part_options.rs (the source’s rules, the combination, the choosers’ JSON) and core/model/src/document/component_options.rs (the commands).

{"cmd": "insert_component",
 "library": {"id": "shelves", "url": "...", "rev": "v1.0.0", "component": "shelf-board", "config": "Standard"},
 "parameters": {"Length": "Shelf_W - 2 * Wall", "Color": "Color"}}
  • How it is made. A component inserted with parameters (with library or with path, linked; a copy has the design’s own parameters and is refused) is made by a derived_part feature, the feature BUILD’s parts have: the design keeps the source’s design in library_sources (a linked file’s as a source with an empty library and its path), and the part evaluates it in the row config (else the default row) with the parameters at recompute. A change of a parameter the values use recomputes that part only; the design needs no library to open. The component is linked (read only, link.feature is the derived part) and has the source’s mount frames as joint origins on the part’s frames (F7:mount(name)), so that they follow its options; insert_component with parameters: {} gives a component that can take options later. derived_part.parameters is the same field: a value may be a number (mm or rad), a text (a text option’s, 'Black') or any expression, in the source’s parameter’s unit.
  • Options belong to the component. All of its occurrences share them; a second configuration is a second component (both use one source).
  • The source’s rules hold. A bound value (its expression names this design’s parameters, or it is one) is never moved; a constant is. The cascade runs when the options are set (insert, set_component_parameters, update_library_parts, update_links): the constants it moves are written into the part and listed in moves (option, from, to, from_expression, to_expression, rule, text: Length 1500 mm → 1000 mm: Black is short). When a bound value breaks a rule, the part fails with the rule (the rule Black is short: …): the component has the error status of a failed feature, the answers give it as refused (rule, message, text), and the design’s own change (set_parameter of the bound parameter) goes through. A constant that a later change of a bound value no longer allows is moved in the evaluation, with a warning on the part.
  • Parts list and designation. A library part’s record (library: config, designation, part_number, supplier_url) follows its combination: the row whose option values it has (the row it starts from first) gives its own designation, part number and page; any other combination takes the library’s pattern with the option values in braces (Board {Color} {Length} → Board Black 800), else the name and standard followed by the option values. A component whose name was its designation is renamed with it. A BUILD part’s designation is BUILD’s, with its options and {L}.

Configurations and tables

The design’s tables (Tables, mitcad#803) meet its configurations in three places (mitcad#806; the design note is docs/configurations.md, “Tables and configurations”). Otherwise they stay separate: a row sets a key, and lookups (XLOOKUP(Size; Screws.Size; Screws.dk)) do the rest.

Option values from a column. A parameter’s values limit (Allowed values) can be a table column instead of a list: "values": "Screws.Size" in add_parameter, set_parameter, the parameters query and the design file (which also reads the list of that one entry, ["Screws.Size"]; a column is a whole list, never mixed with listed values).

  • The domain is the column’s distinct non-empty cells, in the table’s order (values_value, values_text and the configure query’s domain list them). A text option takes a text column; a number option a number column of its dimension (an in column gives 0.25 in, the cell kept exact) or a unitless one, whose numbers are in the option’s unit (16 in an option in mm is 16 mm). Another kind is a problem (Screws.Size is a text column, and option Length is a number).
  • A table edit (set_table, a CSV import) that takes an option’s value out of its column moves the option before the parameters are evaluated with the new table: to the nearest value for a number (the lower of two as near), else to the default row’s value when the column still has it, else to the column’s first value. The cascade then runs as after any change, and set_table’s answer lists every move in moves (Size M7 → M6: its possible values Screws.Size), and so does import_table_csv’s (mitcad#849; Rust: Document::configuration_moves). A driven option is not moved: the edit is refused when its value would fail, as for any parameter. The edit and the moves are one undo step.
  • A column as allowed values makes its parameter a user of the table (used_by of the tables query): a table or column rename rewrites the reference, and deleting the table is refused while an option’s values or a rule (in_table, a list of its column) uses it (table Made is used by the rule Made sizes).

Combinations in a table. The rule action in_table requires the values of some options to be a row of a table:

{"name": "Made sizes",
 "then": [{"in_table": "Made", "columns": {"Color": "Color", "Length": "Length"}}]}
  • columns maps options (keys) to columns of the table (values); each option’s column is of its kind, as above. An action with in_table has no other kind of action.
  • For the choosers and the cascade, each mapped option is narrowed to its column’s cells in the rows that match the mapped options before it in option order (the first is narrowed by none): with Color = 'Black', Length may be only the lengths of the Black rows. A row with an empty cell in a mapped column takes part in nothing.
  • The final check is exact: the combination of every mapped option must be a row. A change that leaves it none is refused with the rule’s name (the rule Made sizes: Color Black and Length 1200 mm is no row of Made), as a forbid is.
  • Renaming an option renames its key; renaming the table or a column rewrites the action. rules of the parameters query names the rule for each mapped option.

One row per distinct non-empty key of the column, named by the key (a text’s text, M5; a number in its column’s unit without the unit, 16), whose values set the option to it ('M5', 16 mm). A row of the same name is updated, not duplicated: it keeps its other values, designation, part number and supplier URL, and is listed in updated only when its value changed. The option becomes an option of the table when it is not one; a closed table’s parameter column chosen as the option moves to the options with its rows’ values (mitcad#1044). Progress and cancellation

A document can be given a RecomputeMonitor (Document::set_monitor, core/model-base/src/monitor.rs), shared with another thread that shows the progress and may cancel. Every recompute then reports to it and checks for a cancel before each feature before the marker. The bridge gives it to C++ as a JobControl (core/ffi/src/jobs.rs). Threading and the application’s worker: docs/architecture.md.

Rust Meaning
RecomputeMonitor::cancel(), is_cancelled() ask the computation to stop; it stops before the next feature, or when the evaluation running now returns, which the kernel’s long operations cut short. A monitor stays cancelled: a new job takes a new one
progress() position (the features before the one computed, shown as position + 1 of total; total when done), total (features before the marker), evaluated (evaluations kept in the cache so far, in all recomputes of the job), feature (the name of the feature evaluated last; a cache hit leaves it), cancelled
set_test_delay(ms) for tests: each evaluation takes ms longer, in 10 ms steps that end on a cancel
cancel_after(n) for tests: cancel once n evaluations were kept, as between two features
ask(question), question(), answer(answer), take_answer() a question the job puts to its user (one line; the .f3d import’s retry_bodies ask, mitcad#283): the thread that shows the progress finds it with question() until it answers; the job takes the answer once. A new question drops an answer not taken
cancel_because(reason), cancel_reason() cancel for a reason rather than on the user’s request (the memory guard of model commands, monitor::memory_guard, mitcad#1480); the first reason stays, a monitor the user cancelled first takes none, and a monitor within others has their reason. The bridge’s command then fails with the reason instead of the computation was canceled, and JobControl::cancel_reason() gives it to C++ (empty otherwise)
Document::try_recompute, try_undo, try_redo fail with ModelError::Cancelled; recompute, undo and redo stay for callers without a monitor (a cancelled undo gives None, a cancelled recompute keeps the last results)
C++ (mitcad_bridge/lib.h) Meaning
new_job_control() a rust::Box<JobControl>, one per job
JobControl::cancel(), is_cancelled(), set_test_delay(ms) as the monitor’s; both threads may call them at once
JobControl::progress() a JobProgress {position, total, evaluated, feature, cancelled}
JobControl::question(), answer(text) the job’s question waiting for an answer (empty when none) and the answer (keep or replace for the .f3d import’s)
Document::attach_job(control), detach_job() the document’s recomputes report to the control until detached
  • A cancelled computation rejects what ran it with the computation was cancelled (Cancelled::MESSAGE, ModelError::Cancelled): a command (recompute, undo and redo too), a preview, the update_links of an opened design. The document stays as it was: the definition state, the undo and redo steps, the revision, the results of the last recompute and recompute_count. The exception is import_f3d with the timeline, which a cancel stops early with what it imported (.f3d import with the timeline).
  • A cancelled preview leaves no preview (preview_body_shape is null).
  • An array of commands stops at the cancelled one as at any error (commands[2]: the computation was canceled); the commands before it stay done.
  • Results evaluated before the cancel stay in the cache, so trying again continues where it stopped. An evaluation that returns after the cancel request is not cached.
  • Inside an evaluation: a recompute with a monitor runs each evaluation through Kernel::interruptible(monitor, ...). The OCCT kernel (core/ffi/src/kernel/cancel.rs) gives the geometry the monitor as its CancelSource (geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/cancel.hpp) for the evaluation’s thread; booleans, fillets and chamfers, sweeps, lofts, shells and offsets, drafts, splits and sewing run with a progress range whose user break asks it, and the geometry also asks between its own steps (throw_if_cancelled); a stopped operation throws Cancelled (“the operation was cancelled”). OCCT’s checker (BRepCheck_Analyzer) cannot be stopped. Without a monitor nothing stops early.
  • A kernel call that does not return (mitcad#1917, mitcad#1922): the kernel calls whose OCCT algorithm does not look at its progress range everywhere run on a thread of their own (core/ffi/src/kernel/abandon.rs): fillet, chamfer, shell, offset_face, thicken, offset_surface, sweep (solid, along guide surfaces, of a body face, and surface), pipe, coil, helix, loft (solid and surface), delete_face (OCCT’s defeaturing heals the body) and the bodies built from their boundaries (the IFC import’s breps, healed by OCCT’s ShapeFix). A cancel gives it up within 10 ms, however long OCCT would still compute; the command is rejected as above. A call that runs longer than the kernel’s time limit is given up too, monitor or not (mitcad-cli as well), and the feature fails with the geometry kernel did not finish within N s; the operation was given up; that failure is the feature’s result like any other, and the features after it are computed. The limit is 300 s, or the seconds of the environment variable MITCAD_KERNEL_TIME_LIMIT (0: none; C++: kernel_time_limit(), set_kernel_time_limit(seconds) in mitcad_bridge/lib.h). A call given up goes on in the background until OCCT returns, and its result is dropped; the process then ends without its static destructors (abandoned_imports()). For tests, MITCAD_TEST_KERNEL_HANG (seconds; set_test_kernel_hang) makes every such call first wait that long, deaf to any cancel.
  • Commands that compute nothing (renames of parameters, comments, named views) are not cancelled.
  • A document is used by one thread at a time; the other thread may hold shapes of earlier results meanwhile but must not read them (OCCT’s algorithms set flags on the sub-shapes of their inputs, which earlier results share).
  • The .f3d imports (import_f3d with or without the timeline) run without the control: they build the document in several steps and are not undone as a whole.
  • Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/monitor_tests.rs; core/tests/test_bridge.cpp (a cancel from another thread, jobs handed between two threads, a modelled thread cancelled inside OCCT); geometry/tests/test_cancel.cpp. A ThreadSanitizer build of test_bridge (by hand, not in ctest) reports the progress read of the feature name: the Rust mutex is not instrumented.

Caches

How the recompute cache and the result store work: docs/architecture.md.

Result store

Results of costly evaluations can be kept on disk, so that opening a design again (or a copy, or an older version of it) does not evaluate them again. A result’s version is a fingerprint of the feature’s uid, its definition and what it read (core/model-base/src/fingerprint.rs), the same in every document and process. Store code and file format: core/model/src/store.rs (module comment).

Rust Meaning

ResultStore::with_quick_results(memory_per_ms) quick results (below): stored when their shapes take at most memory_per_ms bytes per millisecond of evaluation; None for none. Default store::QUICK_MEMORY_PER_MS (128 KiB), None with MITCAD_STORE_QUICK=0; worth_storing(time, memory) tells
Document::persist_results(min_time) writes the results of the last recompute that are not in the store yet: features that succeeded, took at least min_time or are quick results worth storing, and whose results the store takes; returns PersistReport {results, shapes, bytes, quick, failed, errors, time} (quick: of the results, those quicker than min_time). A preview’s results are not written
store::gc(dir, budget), store::clear(dir) gc removes the files used longest ago until 80 % of budget bytes are used (when more is), and temporary files more than an hour old; clear removes all. GcReport {files, bytes, removed, removed_bytes}

C++ (mitcad_bridge/lib.h; core/ffi/src/result_store.rs) Meaning
Document::set_result_store(dir, build_id, label) as above; an empty dir for none. build_id: mitcad::geometry::kernel_build_id() (the shape format, OCCT’s and MitCad’s versions, the size and time of the running program’s file)
Document::persist_results(min_ms) JSON {"results", "shapes", "bytes", "quick", "failed", "errors", "ms"}
result_store_gc(dir, budget_mb), result_store_clear(dir) JSON {"files", "bytes", "removed", "removed_bytes"}; any thread may call them
  • Not stored: sketches and construction features, features that move occurrences, failed features, results evaluated with a parameter renamed since (their versions hold the old name). A result read from the store is in the memory cache afterwards and is not written again.
  • Base features are stored too, also those that only bring in bodies (mitcad#887): bringing a body in reads its B-rep data and derives its edges’ and vertices’ names, which a stored body keeps (a body of 23 000 faces: 1.4 s to bring in, 0.45 s to restore). Restored results whose shapes a recompute unpacks together are unpacked on the machine’s threads, a result’s several bodies too.
  • Quick results (mitcad#882): a result that took less than min_time is stored too when its shapes (the bodies it sets and its tool, as Kernel::shape_memory estimates them) take at most 128 KiB per millisecond of its evaluation. Restoring it reads its file and leaves the state before it packed, so a run of restored features unpacks only its last state, where evaluating the quick feature unpacks the state it reads; quick results with large shapes (a move of a large body) are left out. On three large designs the quick modelling features were within the limit, and their warm recomputes evaluated 107, 75 and 288 features before and 68, 53 and 143 after (store.rs’s module comment has the times).
  • The store keeps up to four variants per feature uid and definition, for different inputs. A file that cannot be read (damaged, cut short, a shape the kernel cannot read) is removed and the feature evaluated; a file of another build is passed over and replaced when the feature is stored again. A hit touches the file’s time, for gc. Files are written to a temporary file and renamed, so programs sharing the folder see whole files.
  • Kernel: Kernel::shape_bytes and Kernel::shape_from_bytes (the shape with its face names, notes and measured properties; OCCT: geometry::serialize_shape).
  • mitcad-cli info <file> --result-store DIR [--persist-min-ms MS] (also run --open) opens the design with the store, writes the results that took at least MS (default 100) and the quick ones worth storing, and prints Result store: restored from store: N, evaluated: M; stored: K (B bytes, Q quick); recompute T ms (T: the recompute’s wall time).
  • Document::hand_off_results(&store) (the bridge’s hand_off_results(dir, build_id, label)) writes every result of the last recompute that a store takes to store, however quick, and marks none written to the document’s own store: the import worker hands the import’s evaluation over to the application this way, which reads the imported design with that store instead of evaluating every feature again (mitcad#413, app/COMMANDS.md The .f3d worker).

Warm opens: lazy restore and display meshes

Opening a design whose results the store holds (mitcad#858).

Lazy restore. With a kernel that can make stored shapes later (Kernel::shape_unpacker; the OCCT kernel can), a result found in the store keeps the shapes of the bodies it sets packed (Output::changes, Changes::heads without them) and the body states hold a stand-in under the stored version; its tool is read at once. The shapes are unpacked when something reads them: an evaluation unpacks the results that set the bodies it reads as it reads them (mitcad#886: a sketch on a face the face’s body, a join or a fillet its bodies; reading all of a component’s bodies unpacks them all), and the other bodies stay packed (the time it takes is not the evaluation’s); before a joint is applied every body; at the end the bodies left; and whenever anything reads the result’s changes later (the timeline’s history, body_before, a pattern of features). A state the next restored result replaces before that is never unpacked. Not with recompute workers nor for a preview. MITCAD_LAZY_RESTORE=0 reads every result whole.
